title: Trump shuts down Pentagon plan for public execution: 5 takeaways
content: President Trump ended speculation on Thursday regarding the Department of Defense’s plan to livestream the firing squad execution of former Army Major Nidal Malik Hasan, the Fort Hood shooter. In a post on Truth Social, the President stated that while a public execution could serve as a deterrent, he did not wish to subject “good and well-meaning” individuals to the event.
summary: President Trump put an abrupt end on Thursday to questions about whether the Pentagon would really livestream the firing squad execution of the Fort Hood shooter, former Army Maj. Nidal Malik Hasan.
author: The Hill

title: Shooter dead, two hospitalized after active shooter at Silver Rail Elementary, Bend, Ore.
content:
A shooter is dead and two people have been hospitalized following an active shooter incident at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, according to the Bend Police Department. The incident was reported on Thursday, and police confirmed that multiple victims, including children, were involved.

The conditions of the hospitalized individuals are currently unknown. The Bend Police Department is investigating the shooting at the elementary school.
summary: A shooter was killed and two people were hospitalized after an active shooter incident at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon. Police confirmed multiple victims, including children, but the conditions of those injured are unknown.
author: The Hill

title: Musk bankrolls PAC spending big on Paxton in Texas
content: Tech mogul Elon Musk contributed $158 million to a key super PAC supporting Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton’s (R) Senate campaign. According to the report, Musk was the sole donor to the Texas PAC during the third quarter. This financial support is part of a broader effort to maintain Republican majorities in Congress.
summary: Tech mogul Elon Musk poured $158 million into a key super PAC backing Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton’s (R) Senate run as part of his push to keep Republican majorities in Congress. Musk was the single donor to Texas PAC — a political action committee backing Paxton’s run — in the third quarter, according to…
author: The Hill

title: 4 GOP senators demand Pentagon IG probe into Ukraine Starlink outage
content: Four Republican senators have joined a letter addressed to the Defense Department’s inspector general, expressing “grave concern” over Ukraine’s sudden loss of access to high-speed Starlink data and intelligence-sharing capabilities. The senators noted that Ukraine requires this access to intercept Russian drones and requested an investigation into whether senior Defense officials played a role in the outage.
summary: Four Republican senators signed a letter to the Defense Department's inspector general requesting an investigation into Ukraine's sudden loss of access to intelligence-sharing and high-speed Starlink data. The senators expressed grave concern over the outage, which Ukraine needs to intercept Russian drones, and asked for an inquiry into whether senior Defense officials played a role.
author: The Hill

title: Ukraine military faces Starlink restrictions for objects over 100 mph
content:
Elon Musk’s Starlink system has become the focus of a new controversy after Ukraine’s military experienced restricted access to Starshield, the military variant of the satellite-based network. According to a source familiar with the situation, Starlink services were disconnected for objects traveling at speeds exceeding 100 miles per hour.

This speed restriction directly impacted the operational capabilities of Ukraine’s military assets, including drones, airplanes, and helicopters. The incident has raised questions regarding the United States' role in the shutdown of these services.
summary: Ukraine's military encountered restricted access to Starshield after Starlink services were cut off for objects traveling more than 100 mph. This limitation impacted the capabilities of Ukraine's drones, airplanes, and helicopters.
author: The Hill

title: Anthropic PAC splits Q3 donations down the middle
content: Anthropic’s corporate political action committee split its third-quarter donations evenly between the two major parties, according to spending records first shared with The Hill. The employee-funded PAC reported total third-quarter spending of more than $250,000, with $161,000 poured into campaigns across the aisle last month.
summary: Anthropic's corporate political action committee spent $161,000 on campaigns across the aisle last month. This brings their total third-quarter spending to more than $250,000, according to spending records shared with The Hill.
author: The Hill

title: Rural women face widening breast cancer death rate gap
content: New studies from the American Cancer Society indicate that women in rural areas are increasingly less likely to survive breast cancer. According to a study presented at the American Society of Clinical Oncology, breast cancer death rates are now higher in rural locales than in cities.
summary: New American Cancer Society studies indicate that rural women are becoming less likely to survive breast cancer. Breast cancer death rates are now higher in rural areas than in cities.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Drug-coated balloons match stents in preventing heart attacks, UEA study finds
content: Research from the University of East Anglia (UEA) indicates that drug-coated balloons may serve as an alternative to permanent heart stents for thousands of patients. A major analysis involving more than 7,800 patients demonstrated that this newer treatment performed as effectively as conventional stents in preventing heart attacks and cardiovascular deaths.
summary: Research from the University of East Anglia indicates that drug-coated balloons can treat heart patients without permanently implanted metal stents. A major analysis of over 7,800 patients showed the newer treatment performed as well as conventional stents at preventing heart attacks and cardiovascular deaths.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Heart failure reshapes bone marrow to create inflammation-related immune memory
content:
Heart failure (HF) affects the body beyond the heart’s pumping and circulation functions by inducing a lasting form of innate immune memory in bone marrow (BM). This condition specifically impacts stem cells responsible for synthesizing blood, as well as progenitor cells within the bone marrow.

The resulting immune memory leads to the production of immune cells that promote inflammation, which in turn worsens heart function. Despite these known consequences, the exact mechanism behind this process remains unclear.
summary: Heart failure causes a lasting form of innate immune memory in bone marrow stem and progenitor cells. This process leads to the production of immune cells that promote inflammation and worsen heart function.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Moldable gel controls bleeding and supports bone repair in preclinical tests
content:
A research team from the Faculty of Dentistry at The University of Hong Kong (HKU), collaborating with Su Ryon Shin's group at Brigham and Women's Hospital, Harvard Medical School, has developed a shape-adaptive hydrogel intended for complex clinical trauma. The material is specifically designed to address scenarios involving severe bleeding, irregular bone defects, and comminuted fractures.

The team has advanced the hydrogel and completed preclinical validation of its performance. These tests confirmed the gel's ability to control bleeding and support bone repair in challenging injury environments.
summary: A research team from the Faculty of Dentistry at The University of Hong Kong (HKU), working in collaboration with Su Ryon Shin's group at Brigham and Women's Hospital, Harvard Medical School, has advanced and preclinically…
author: Medical Xpress

title: WEHI study finds immune cells that kill small cell lung cancer
content:
A study published in Cancer Cell reveals that a previously overlooked immune cell type is capable of recognizing and killing small cell lung cancer, the most aggressive form of the disease globally. The research, conducted by the Walter and Eliza Hall Institute (WEHI), identifies this hidden immune defense as a potential target for new treatment strategies against these difficult-to-treat tumors.

The WEHI study further found that patients with higher levels of these specific immune cells demonstrated longer survival times. These findings suggest that exploiting this natural immune response could provide a new avenue for attacking small cell lung cancer.
summary: Researchers at WEHI identified a previously overlooked immune cell capable of recognizing and killing small cell lung cancer. The study, published in Cancer Cell, found that patients with higher levels of these cells lived longer.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Women explain why they avoid clothes stores after Primark announces home delivery
content: Primark has announced plans to introduce home delivery services, a move that follows reports from women who avoid visiting physical clothing stores. These individuals cite the in-store shopping experience as quite demoralizing, which has led them to conduct all their clothing purchases online.
summary: Primark has announced plans to offer home delivery services. Several women who never enter clothes stores shared their reasons for shopping exclusively online.
author: BBC Business

title: Study: 44% of reef-building coral species face higher extinction risk
content: A major global study led in part by a University of Portsmouth scientist reveals that 44% of the world’s reef-building coral species are currently threatened with extinction. The research team warns that the actual number of at-risk species is likely to be even higher than the reported figure.
summary: A University of Portsmouth scientist helped lead a global study finding that 44% of reef-building coral species are threatened with extinction. Researchers warn that the true figure is likely to be even higher.
author: Phys.org

title: Study of lunar fault maps provides detailed estimate of moon's contraction
content:
A new study of young tectonic landforms on the moon offers the most detailed estimate yet of how much the moon has contracted as its interior gradually cooled over time.

The research focuses on the moon’s tectonic features to quantify the extent of contraction.
summary: A new study examined young tectonic landforms on the moon. It provides the most detailed estimate yet of how much the moon has contracted as its interior gradually cooled.
author: Phys.org

title: New spectroscopy method enables direct comparisons of nuclear sizes across heavy elements
content: The size of a nucleus, defined as the nuclear charge radius, is a critical physical quantity that reflects the internal arrangement of protons and neutrons. This metric is particularly significant for deformed nuclei, such as those found in rare-earth elements, where analyzing changes in the charge radius can enhance the scientific understanding of nuclear structure and deformation.
summary: The size of a nucleus (nuclear charge radius) is an important physical quantity that reflects the arrangement of protons and neutrons within the nucleus. Particularly in deformed nuclei, such as those of rare-earth elements, examining changes in the charge radius can deepen our understanding of nuclear structure and nuclear deformation.
author: Phys.org

title: Food, fear and physics help explain group behavior from plankton to whales
content:
The open ocean presents a challenging environment characterized by patchy food distribution, abundant predators, and constantly shifting oceanographic conditions. Survival in this dynamic setting demands specific adaptations for organisms living within the pelagic environment.

This pelagic zone encompasses the offshore waters extending from the sunlit surface down through the twilight zone. The physical and biological constraints of these waters shape the behavior of marine life, ranging from microscopic plankton to large whales.
summary: The open ocean is a dynamic environment, where food is patchy, predators are plentiful, and oceanographic conditions change constantly. Life in the pelagic environment—the offshore waters that extend from the sunlit surface through the twilight zone—requires unique adaptations for survival.
author: Phys.org

title: Jev meets the Trolley Problem
content:
The article titled "Jev meets the Trolley Problem" was published on the website zachlandes.com. The piece was subsequently featured on the Y Combinator news platform, where it generated significant community engagement.

The discussion associated with the article on the Y Combinator news site received 254 points and 115 comments.
summary: The article titled "Jev meets the Trolley Problem" was posted on zachlandes.com. It received 254 points and 115 comments on the Hacker News platform.
author: Hacker News

title: 2026 films offer critical looks at Silicon Valley founders
content:
2026 has seen a notable increase in films that offer a critical perspective on Silicon Valley’s influence on reality, moving away from the traditional celebration of disruptive tech founders. Aaron Sorkin’s The Social Reckoning portrays Mark Zuckerberg as a robotic villain whose ambitions are destabilizing society, while Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s You Can See Everything presents a damning depiction of Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes as she prepares for her ongoing prison sentence.

The shift in public narrative around Elon Musk is also reflected in recent projects, including Alex Gibney’s documentary, which illustrates how the perception of the tech executive has changed from being widely celebrated as a visionary to facing more scrutiny.
summary: Aaron Sorkin's The Social Reckoning portrays Mark Zuckerberg as a robotic villain whose ambitions destabilize society. Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's You Can See Everything depicts Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes preparing for her ongoing prison stint.
author: The Verge

title: Sega pulls Total War: Shogun 2 remaster from sale following disastrous launch
content:
Sega has removed Total War: Shogun 2 - Complete Edition from digital storefronts following a poorly received launch. The remaster, which launched on Tuesday, bundles the 2011 strategy game with all its DLC and promised upgrades such as improved visuals, 1440p and 4K UI scaling, and modernized controls.

The release has drawn significant criticism from users who reported bugs and upscaling issues that appear to have been processed by AI. The game currently holds an "Overwhelmingly Negative" rating on Steam, where it has already been pulled, while posts on Reddit feature artwork that users believe was negatively altered by AI.
summary: Sega is removing Total War: Shogun 2 - Complete Edition from storefronts following a disastrous launch where users complained about issues like bugs and upscaling that appears to have been done by AI. Complete Edition, a remaster of the 2011 strategy game, launched on Tuesday, and it bundled the main game and all of its DLC with promised upgrades including "improved visuals," "1440p and 4K UI scaling," and modernized controls.
author: The Verge

title: Steam introduces achievement sets to organize game and DLC trophies
content:
Valve is rolling out a new feature for Steam called "achievement sets," which allows developers to organize achievements into distinct groups for base games and downloadable content. According to Valve, the core gameplay mechanics remain unchanged, meaning players unlock achievements by playing the game as usual. However, the new system reorganizes the display of these accomplishments to improve navigation.

When browsing unlocked achievements, Steam will now separate the long list into the developer-created sets. This structure is designed to make it easier for players to see what they have completed and to find other related achievements to unlock next. Each achievement set includes its own progress bar, and completing a set awards players a "set complete" trophy that is visible on their profile.
summary: Valve is adding a feature that allows developers to group base game and DLC achievements into separate sets. This organization includes individual progress bars and a special trophy awarded when a set is completed.
author: The Verge

title: Porsche previews new mid-engined supercar as part of 2035 plan
content:
Porsche has previewed a new mid-engined supercar, positioning it above its 911 model in the brand’s lineup. This vehicle is part of the manufacturer’s broader strategic shift toward higher-end products.

The introduction of this supercar aligns with Porsche’s turnaround plan for 2035, which prioritizes producing fewer vehicles that command higher prices.
summary: Porsche has previewed a new mid-engined supercar positioned above the 911. The vehicle is part of a 2035 turnaround plan that focuses on lower volume and higher-priced cars.
author: Ars Technica

title: Hegseth's low-T screening may flag 25% of Army despite expert opposition
content:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s proposed low testosterone screening for Army personnel has drawn criticism from medical experts. The initiative could potentially flag up to 25 percent of the Army’s force, according to reports on the policy’s scope.

Medical professionals explicitly recommend against implementing such blanket screenings, citing concerns over the medical validity and necessity of the proposed tests.
summary: Medical experts explicitly recommend against the blanket low-T screening proposed by Hegseth. The screening initiative may flag up to 25 percent of the Army.
author: Ars Technica

title: Cal AI's viral success driven by influencers leads to $30M revenue and acquisition by MyFitness
content: Cal AI generated over $30 million in revenue within two years before being acquired by MyFitness in March for an undisclosed amount. The company’s rapid growth was attributed to a campaign involving a small army of influencers that drove its viral success.
summary: Cal AI generated over $30 million in revenue in two years. The company was acquired by MyFitness in March for an undisclosed amount.
author: TechCrunch

title: UK to ban porn depicting choking or incest from early November
content:
The government has announced that pornographic material depicting choking or incest will be prohibited from early November, officials said.

The decision comes after a review of pornography regulation scheduled for 2025, which was conducted by Conservative peer Baroness Gabby Bertin.
summary: The government announced that pornography showing choking or incest will be prohibited from early November. The decision follows a 2025 review of pornography regulation by Conservative peer Baroness Gabby Bertin.
author: BBC Technology

title: Student protests in Tirana erupt into violence for third day
content: Violent protests have rocked central Tirana for a third consecutive day, marked by fires, stone-throwing by demonstrators, and a police response utilizing tear gas and water cannons. The ongoing demonstrations are led by students who are demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama.
summary: Fires burn in central Tirana as protesters throw stones and police use tear gas and water cannon. The student‑led demonstrations demanding Prime Minister Edi Rama's resignation have entered their third day.
author: Euronews

title: Sally Rooney's books banned in UK after publisher cites Palestine Action support
content:
Irish author Sally Rooney can no longer sell her books in the United Kingdom, publisher Faber announced on Wednesday. The decision follows Rooney’s public support for the activist group Palestine Action, which the UK government designated as a “terrorist” organisation in July 2025.

Palestine Action remains unbanned in Ireland, where Rooney resides. The ban in the UK has effectively halted the sale of Rooney’s titles within the country.

The source also notes that FRANCE 24’s Sharon Gaffney spoke with Alan Greene, Professor of Constitutional Law and Human Rights at the Birmingham Law School.
summary: Irish author Sally Rooney can no longer sell her books in the UK because her publisher, Faber, said she supports the activist group Palestine Action. The group was banned as a terrorist organization by the UK government in July 2025, but it is not banned in Ireland where Rooney lives.
author: France 24

title: At least five dead in Silver Rail Elementary School shooting in Bend, Oregon
content:
Authorities believe at least five people died in a shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, on Thursday, according to law enforcement officials.

Police confirmed the suspect was dead and said children were among the victims.

The incident occurred at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon.
summary: Authorities believe at least five people died in a shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, on Thursday. Police confirmed the suspect was dead and said children were among the victims.
author: France 24

title: Zelensky seeks European backing after pledging to resume attacks on Russian refineries
content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky sought European backing Thursday after U.S. support for Ukraine has reportedly waned.

Zelensky vowed to resume strikes on Russian oil refineries, a move that ran counter to demands from U.S. President Donald Trump. The decision came amid rising tensions with Washington over sanctions, attacks on energy infrastructure, and restrictions on satellite communications.

The escalating disputes underscore the growing strain between Ukraine and the United States.
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky sought European backing Thursday after pledging to resume strikes on Russian oil refineries. He did so despite demands from U.S. President Donald Trump, as tensions with Washington escalated over sanctions, energy infrastructure attacks and restrictions on satellite communications.
author: France 24

title: Security Council Debates Rising Lethal Strikes and Demolitions in Gaza and West Bank
content:
The United Nations Security Council convened an open debate on Thursday to address the escalating situation in the Occupied Palestinian Territory.  

The discussion was prompted by a rise in lethal Israeli strikes, as well as increased demolitions and violence across Gaza and the West Bank.  

The Council’s session focused on the current conditions in these areas, with participants calling for renewed attention to the humanitarian and security implications of the recent developments.
summary: The Security Council held an open debate on Thursday about the rising lethal Israeli strikes, demolitions, and violence in Gaza and the West Bank. The debate focused on the current situation in the Occupied Palestinian Territory.
author: UN News

title: Ukraine: Russian attacks destroy $1.5M in UN medical supplies
content:
Ongoing Russian attacks across Ukraine are disrupting the country’s healthcare system.  

More than $1.5 million worth of medicines and supplies have been destroyed in four separate strikes on warehouses used by the United Nations since July.  

These attacks have caused serious healthcare disruption in the affected areas.
summary: Russian attacks on Ukraine have destroyed more than $1.5 million worth of medicines and supplies. The strikes hit four UN warehouses since July, causing serious healthcare disruption.
author: UN News

title: Afghanistan Reaches Record Levels of Acute Hunger, 15.9 Million Affected
content:
Afghanistan faces record hunger levels amid rampant rights violations.  

According to a global hunger monitor report released on Thursday, acute malnutrition and hunger have reached the highest levels ever recorded. 15.9 million people are facing acute food insecurity. The report warns that conditions are set to worsen in the coming months.
summary: Acute malnutrition and hunger have reached the highest levels ever recorded in Afghanistan. A global hunger monitor report released on Thursday states that 15.9 million people are facing acute food insecurity and conditions are expected to worsen in the coming months.
author: UN News

title: UN report warns AI, green energy, shifts could leave vulnerable communities behind
content:
The United Nations warned on Thursday that the rapid shift toward artificial intelligence, digital technologies, renewable energy and demographic changes could leave vulnerable communities behind.  

According to the new UN report, these transformations are reshaping economies worldwide, offering new opportunities while also threatening to deepen socio‑economic inequalities.  

The report was released on Thursday.
summary: The UN report warns that rapid transformations, including artificial intelligence, digital technologies, renewable energy, and demographic shifts, are reshaping economies worldwide. These changes create new opportunities but also threaten to deepen socio-economic inequalities, potentially leaving vulnerable communities behind.
author: UN News

title: UN warns fewer than half of biodiversity targets on track ahead of COP17 in Yerevan
content:
The United Nations has warned that fewer than half of the national targets set to protect the world’s plants, animals and ecosystems are on track, according to a new report.  

The report highlights that progress on biodiversity goals is lagging, a concern that comes days before the COP17 biodiversity conference.  

The COP17 conference will be held in Yerevan, Armenia.
summary: The UN report says fewer than half of national biodiversity targets are on track. Countries are meeting in Yerevan, Armenia, for the COP17 biodiversity conference.
author: UN News

title: UN report urges limits on neurotechnology as brain data could be used in court
content:
A new United Nations report warns that advances in neurotechnology are outpacing existing legal protections for human rights.  

The report notes that brain signals captured by devices such as gaming headsets or wellness gadgets could potentially be presented as evidence in court. It calls for limits on the use of such technologies to safeguard individual rights.
summary: Brain signals recorded by a gaming headset or a wellness gadget could one day be used as evidence against you in court. A new UN report warns that neurotechnology is outpacing the laws meant to protect human rights and calls for limits.
author: UN News

title: Polls show Trump's ICE crackdown divides voters ahead of 2026 midterms
content:
ICE tactics have ignited debate as the United States approaches a pivotal midterm election cycle. The controversy centers on the agency’s immigration enforcement actions and their political ramifications.

Polls have found that President Donald Trump’s hardline immigration enforcement effort has divided voters ahead of the 2026 midterm race.
summary: Polls have found that Trump's hardline immigration enforcement effort has divided voters. The division is emerging before the 2026 midterm race.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israeli ad firm used to infect Al Jazeera journalists' devices with spyware
content:
An Israeli digital‑advertising firm, operating as a front for spyware, has been linked to the infection of devices used by journalists at Al Jazeera. The operation involved the deployment of Israeli spyware that was disguised as a legitimate advertising service.

The malicious campaign specifically targeted Al Jazeera journalists, compromising their equipment with the hidden surveillance tools. The incident highlights the use of commercial‑type fronts to deliver espionage software to media personnel.
summary: An Israeli spyware operation disguised as a digital advertisement firm targeted devices used by Al Jazeera journalists. The campaign helped infect those devices with spyware.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Three dead, several missing after severe flooding in Istanbul
content:
Severe flooding swept across Istanbul after torrential rain, leaving multiple casualties.  

Authorities reported that three people have died and several others are missing as a result of the floods.  

The incident underscores the impact of the heavy rainfall that triggered the flooding across the city.
summary: Three people have died after torrential rain triggered severe flooding across Istanbul. Several people are reported missing following the floods.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israel stops commercial goods entering Gaza as Hamas rejects tax allegations
content:
Israel has stopped commercial goods from entering Gaza, according to the announcement in the title.  

The suspension affects shipments such as fruit and winter clothing, cutting off a key source of critical supplies.  

Hamas has responded by denying tax claims related to the halted shipments.
summary: Israel has halted commercial shipments, including fruit and winter clothing, from entering Gaza. Hamas says it does not accept the tax claims.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Two Syrian pipelines damaged: Baniyas-Homs leak linked to fuel theft, Hasakah gas line fire
content:
Two Syrian pipelines were damaged as part of a recent spate of attacks on the country’s energy infrastructure. One incident involved a leak on the Baniyas‑Homs pipeline, which officials attributed to fuel theft.

In a separate event, a gas export line in the Hasakah region caught fire, further highlighting the vulnerability of Syria’s energy network.
summary: A leak on the Baniyas‑Homs pipeline was attributed to fuel theft. A gas export line in Hasakah caught fire, damaging the second pipeline.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US teen's Hindu temple attack plot foiled after gun jammed, police say
content:
Police say a tip‑off helped prevent a 19‑year‑old suspect’s plan to attack a Hindu temple in the United States.  

According to authorities, the alleged assault never took place because the suspect’s gun jammed outside the place of worship.  

Police confirmed the weapon malfunction stopped the attack.
summary: Police say a tip-off helped foil a 19-year-old suspect's plan to attack a Hindu temple in the United States. The plot failed when his gun jammed outside the place of worship.
author: BBC World

title: Bus collides with stopped train on French side of Channel Tunnel, 19 injured
content:
A bus collided with a train that was stopped on the French side of the Channel Tunnel, leaving 19 people injured, officials reported.

Two of the injured were airlifted to a hospital, but officials said no one’s life appeared to be in danger.
summary: A bus struck a train that was stopped on the French side of the Channel Tunnel, injuring 19 people. Two of the injured were airlifted to hospital, and officials said no one's life appeared to be in danger.
author: BBC World

title: Scientists Discover Sun May Turn Green as Cosmic Zombie After Death
content:
Scientists have discovered the first green star, a phenomenon described as a "cosmic zombie" that aligns with the Halloween season. The discovery suggests that our Sun could potentially exhibit a similar spooky green glow in the distant future.

This hypothetical transformation would occur after the Sun's death in billions of years, at which point it may undergo a change that results in the distinctive green coloration.
summary: Scientists discovered that the Sun may go green after its death. The green glow would occur when the Sun becomes a cosmic zombie billions of years from now.
author: Space.com

title: Klara and the Sun review – Taika Waititi’s manic pixie dream robot sci-fi is a sentimental mess
content:
Taika Waititi’s adaptation of Kazuo Ishiguro’s novel, Klara and the Sun, has been criticized for being a "sentimental mess" that fails to offer substantial commentary on artificial intelligence, love, or grief. The director of Hunt for the Wilderpeople and Jojo Rabbit is described as creating a "twee, tiresome tale" filled with "postmodern quirkiness" and "ironic dorkiness," which the review characterizes as unbearably mannered and poorly acted.

Set in a post-World War III future where the internet has been wiped out, the film features families purchasing "artificial friend" (AF) robots for their children. The review notes technical inconsistencies in this world, such as the unclear status of AFs and the inclusion of a purple, highly flammable substance called PEC-9 in the robots' bodies. Despite Waititi’s previous success with comedy in films like Thor: Ragnarok, this project is compared unfavorably to his "fey-Hitler fantasy," Jojo Rabbit, being labeled as misjudged and self-admiring.
summary: The director of Hunt for the Wilderpeople and Jojo Rabbit turns Kazuo Ishiguro’s AI fable into a twee, tiresome tale of love and griefTaika Waititi detonates an explosion of postmodern quirkiness and ironic dorkiness in this unbearably mannered, unspeakably acted film. It’s a slice of sentimental whimsy-futurism and non-satire, adapted by Waititi from the Kazuo Ishiguro novel, which winds up saying nothing substantial or meaningful (or funny) about artificial intelligence, love or grief.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Chris Woakes criticizes England players' conduct and Rob Key's treatment
content:
Chris Woakes, a Test stalwart who has just concluded his 20th professional season, has criticized the behavior of some England players, describing their actions as “unacceptable.” The Warwickshire bowler, who recently secured his third County Championship title, addressed these issues during an interview at Edgbaston’s indoor nets on a rainy October afternoon.

Woakes’ international career included 62 Tests for England, in which he took 192 wickets and scored 2,034 runs, along with two World Cup victories. Throughout his tenure, he worked under various coaches, including Andy Flower and Brendon McCullum, and played for captains such as Sir Alastair Cook, Eoin Morgan, Joe Root, and Ben Stokes.

Reflecting on his long career, Woakes recalled advice from his parents, particularly his father, to “always be myself” when he was 17 and beginning his professional journey. The article also notes his discussions regarding his final appearance at the Oval and what he described as “shabby” treatment from Rob Key, alongside the ongoing issue of cricket’s drinking culture.
summary: Chris Woakes describes his final season at the Oval and criticizes the behavior of some England players as unacceptable. He also discusses his treatment by Rob Key and the issue of drinking culture in cricket.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Noah Sadiki scores dramatic late winner for Sunderland against Torreense
content:
Democratic Republic of the Congo midfielder Noah Sadiki scored a dramatic late goal to secure a win for Sunderland against Torreense in Portugal. With three minutes of stoppage time remaining, Sadiki half-volied the ball into the net following excellent work from Enzo Le Fée and Granit Xhaka.

The goal marked Sadiki’s first for Régis Le Bris’s side, sparking an ecstatic reaction from Sunderland supporters who had feared their celebration in Portugal might fall flat. After scoring, Sadiki hurdled a set of advertising hoardings and sprinted across a running track to join the fans.
summary: Noah Sadiki scored a dramatic late goal to secure a win for Sunderland against Torreense. The Democratic Republic of the Congo midfielder half-volleyed the ball after excellent work from Enzo Le Fée and Granit Xhaka.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Martínez apologises to Manchester United's Wilcox after outburst
content:
Lisandro Martínez has apologized for his comments suggesting that Manchester United’s director of football, Jason Wilcox, did not sufficiently strengthen the squad during the summer transfer window. The defender issued the apology following discussions held on Thursday with manager Michael Carrick and the club hierarchy.

While the club has stated that any disciplinary action taken against Martínez will not be made public, it is believed that the player has been fined for the outburst.
summary: Lisandro Martínez apologised for claiming director of football Jason Wilcox failed to strengthen the squad sufficiently in the summer window. The defender discussed the incident with manager Michael Carrick and the club hierarchy, and it is thought he has been fined.
author: Guardian Sport

title: 5 GOP House members join letter urging Trump to cancel Russia diesel deal
content:
Five House Republicans signed a letter on Thursday urging President Trump to cancel the Russian diesel deal he announced the previous week. The bipartisan group also called for increased sanctions against Russia.

The Republican signatories included Representatives Don Bacon of Nebraska, Brian Fitzpatrick of Pennsylvania, Michael McCaul of Texas, Dan Newhouse of Washington, and Joe Wilson of South Carolina. They joined 17 Democratic colleagues in the letter, stating they were “particularly concerned” about the agreement.
summary: Five House Republicans signed a letter on Thursday urging President Trump to cancel the Russian diesel deal announced last week. They joined 17 Democratic colleagues in expressing concern about the agreement.

title: Katie Zacharia names Scarlett Johansson as ideal SNL cast member
content:
White House press secretary Katie Zacharia, who recently made headlines for her rocky debut at the podium, has identified Scarlett Johansson as the actress she would like to see portray her on the NBC sketch comedy show “Saturday Night Live.”

Zacharia shared this preference during an interview with conservative commentator Jack Posobiec, stating, “Maybe a Scarlett Johansson-type character.”
summary: White House press secretary Katie Zacharia said she would like a Scarlett Johansson-type character to portray her on "Saturday Night Live." She made the comment in an interview with conservative commentator Jack Posobiec.

title: Trump White House ballroom donors disclosed by Washington Post
content:
The Washington Post reported on Thursday that it had obtained a new list revealing major donors to President Trump’s White House ballroom project. The document details more than $330 million in private donations intended to fund the construction effort.

According to the report, the majority of these funds were donated prior to the demolition of the East Wing.
summary: The Washington Post released a list of major donors to President Trump’s White House ballroom project. The list shows over $330 million in private donations, most of which were made before the East Wing was demolished.

title: Trump says Elon Musk has “a little problem” while attacking Arizona Gov. Hobbs
content:
President Donald Trump took a brief jab at tech entrepreneur Elon Musk on Wednesday while speaking at a rally in Arizona. Trump said Musk “has a little problem,” noting that the billionaire remains a close ally despite a “rollercoaster relationship” between the two.

During the same appearance, Trump turned his criticism toward Arizona Democratic Governor Katie Hobbs, describing her as “horrible” and “a dumb person.” The comments were made as Trump campaigned in the state.
summary: President Trump told a rally audience that Elon Musk has “a little problem.” He also criticized Democratic Arizona Governor Katie Hobbs, calling her “horrible” and “a dumb person.”

title: DOJ sues California after pushing state to match voter list with USB drive
content: The U.S. Department of Justice filed a lawsuit against the state of California on Thursday following a demand that state officials compare their voter registration data with information provided by the Department of Homeland Security. The DOJ issued a letter to California and local election officials on Tuesday, requiring them to complete this data matching process within 48 hours using a provided USB drive. The letter warned that legal action would be taken if the state failed to comply with the request.
summary: The Justice Department sued the state of California Thursday after giving them a USB drive and demanding that within 48 hours they compare their data rolls with information provided by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). DOJ sent the letter to the state as well as local election officials Tuesday, threatening legal action if they…

title: Matt Gaetz, 2 Others Accused in Federal Sex Trafficking Lawsuit
content: Former Representative Matt Gaetz (R-Fla.) is facing a federal lawsuit filed Thursday in the Middle District of Florida, alleging that he and two others sexually exploited two anonymous women in their early 20s. The legal action accuses Gaetz, former Seminole County Tax Collector Joel Greenberg, and former Florida state Representative Chris Dorworth (R) of participating in sex trafficking.
summary: A federal lawsuit filed in the Middle District of Florida accuses former Rep. Matt Gaetz and two others of sexually exploiting two anonymous women. The suit also names former Seminole County Tax Collector Joel Greenberg and former Florida state Rep. Chris Dorworth as alleged participants.

title: U.S. historic preservation law faces 60-year-old threat from Congress
content: Congress and a federal agency are currently moving to weaken the United States’ historic preservation law, a move that critics describe as the most serious threat to the legislation in its sixty-year history. This proposed weakening has sparked a significant backlash among opponents, who compare the intensity of the current reaction to the fervent opposition that originally led to the law’s creation six decades ago.
summary: Congress and a federal agency are threatening to weaken the country's historic preservation law. Critics say this action is fueling a backlash as fiery as the one that led to the law's creation 60 years ago.
author: NPR Politics

title: UN report urges nations to boost insufficient nature policies at COP17
content: A major United Nations report intended to guide biodiversity negotiations in Armenia indicates that while nations have achieved some progress, they remain off track to meet the goal of protecting 30% of land and oceans by 2030. The findings highlight that current nature policies are insufficient to reach this landmark target.
summary: A major UN report indicates that countries have made some progress but remain off track for the goal to protect 30% of land and oceans by 2030. This report will inform biodiversity negotiations taking place in Armenia.
author: Climate Home News

title: Sports supplement may shield brain from gut inflammation damage
content:
Research suggests that a popular sports supplement may help protect the brain from damage associated with gut inflammation. The gut-brain axis functions as a two-way biochemical connection, where chronic inflammation in the gut sends inflammatory signals throughout the body that trigger neuroinflammation in the brain.

The hippocampus, the brain region responsible for memory, learning, and mood, is particularly vulnerable to this process. Disruption of the hippocampus can impact cognitive functions such as thinking and remembering, as well as emotional well-being.
summary: The gut-brain axis transmits inflammatory signals from the gut to the brain, triggering neuroinflammation. This process particularly endangers the hippocampus, which governs memory, learning, and mood.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Genetic testing for antidepressants does not improve treatment effectiveness
content: A clinical trial conducted in Australia by an international team of researchers found that genetic testing to select antidepressants did not result in better improvements in depressive symptoms compared to standard prescriptions based on clinical guidelines. The study evaluated whether prescribing medication based on a patient's genetic makeup offered any advantage over traditional clinical methods.
summary: An Australian clinical trial found that genetic testing to select antidepressants did not improve depressive symptoms compared to standard prescriptions. The study was conducted by an international team of researchers using clinical guidelines for the control group.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Alzheimer's drug access varies by race, vulnerability, and health status
content: The first disease-modifying drugs for Alzheimer's disease are designed to slow cognitive decline by targeting amyloid plaques in the brain. However, a new study indicates that patients do not have equal opportunities to receive these treatments. According to the research, race, vulnerability, and health status are key factors that shape access to the medication.
summary: New Alzheimer's drugs slow cognitive decline by targeting amyloid plaques in the brain. A new study indicates that race, vulnerability, and health status shape patient access to these treatments.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Harvard team develops faster antibody screening for cancer treatments
content: A research team led by scientists at Harvard Medical School, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, and Dana-Farber Cancer Institute has developed a new antibody screening method. This approach is designed to accelerate the process of identifying and engineering cancer-fighting therapies.
summary: Researchers at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center and Dana-Farber Cancer Institute have developed a faster method to identify cancer-fighting therapies. The antibody screening approach aims to accelerate the engineering of immune-based treatments.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study finds prebiotic fiber helps girls build more bone
content:
A one-year clinical trial led by Florida International University nutrition researcher Cristina Palacios found that prebiotic fiber supplements can enhance bone development in girls. The study compared participants who added the supplement to their regular diets against a control group that received a placebo.

The results indicated that girls taking the prebiotic fiber supplement built more bone over the course of the year than those who took the placebo.
summary: A clinical trial led by Cristina Palacios at Florida International University found that girls who took a prebiotic fiber supplement for a year built more bone. The results showed these girls built more bone than girls who took a placebo.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Protein modification reverses cancer muscle wasting in preclinical study
content:
Cachexia, a severe form of muscle wasting affecting up to 80% of cancer patients, is driven by pro-inflammatory cytokines released by tumor cells. Known as cancer-induced cachexia (CIC), this condition is responsible for 30% to 50% of all cancer-related deaths worldwide, earning it the nickname "final disease" due to the absence of curative treatments.

A preclinical study indicates that protein modification can partially reverse this cancer-related muscle wasting, offering a potential avenue for addressing a condition currently without a cure.
summary: A preclinical study found that protein modification partially reverses cancer-related muscle wasting, known as cachexia. This condition affects up to 80% of cancer patients and is caused by pro-inflammatory signaling molecules released by tumor cells.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study links nature contact to positive food relationship
content: A study led by Anglia Ruskin University (ARU) suggests that contact with natural environments may help individuals develop healthier eating habits. Published in the journal Body Image, the research provides the first evidence that exposure to nature can influence people's relationship with food.
summary: A study led by Anglia Ruskin University found that contact with natural environments may help people develop healthier eating habits. Published in the journal Body Image, this is the first research to provide evidence that exposure to nature can influence people's relationship with food.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Porsche Reveals Mission S Concept Car Previewing New Design Identity
content:
Porsche has unveiled the Mission S concept car, which serves as a preview for the brand’s new design identity. The vehicle was introduced as a key component of the company’s broader strategic turnaround plan.

This initiative aims to improve profitability by focusing on higher-end products while reducing overall sales volumes.
summary: Porsche unveiled the Mission S concept car as part of a turnaround plan. The strategy aims to boost profits through higher-end products and lower sales volumes.
author: CNBC Business

title: PWDA report outlines six lessons to improve leadership for women with disability
content: A new report from People with Disability Australia (PWDA), the national disability rights and advocacy organization, states that employers must take greater action to remove barriers preventing women with disability from advancing into leadership roles. The researchers behind the report have identified six specific lessons intended to help drive change in this area.
summary: A new report from People with Disability Australia states that employers must remove barriers preventing women with disability from reaching leadership roles. Researchers in the report identify six lessons to help drive change in this area.
author: Phys.org

title: North Sea Heat Wave Triggers Underwater Plankton Bloom Missed by Satellites
content:
Satellites are frequently used by scientists to monitor ocean responses to marine heat waves by detecting changes in ocean color, which indicate shifts in phytoplankton populations. These microscopic organisms are essential to marine food webs and the global carbon cycle, yet satellite observations are limited to the ocean's surface.

In the North Sea, a recent heat wave triggered an underwater plankton bloom that was largely missed by these satellite systems due to their inability to detect activity below the surface.
summary: Scientists use satellites to detect changes in ocean color during marine heat waves. Satellites can only see the ocean's surface, missing underwater plankton blooms in the North Sea.
author: Phys.org

title: Battle of Neville's Cross: 1346 Capture of King David II Outside Durham
content:
On October 17, 1346, the Battle of Neville’s Cross took place outside Durham in northeast England. This conflict served as a decisive moment in Anglo-Scottish history, resulting in the capture of King David II of Scotland.

Despite its significant impact on relations between England, Scotland, and France, the battle remains little-known to many people.
summary: The Battle of Neville's Cross was fought on Oct. 17, 1346 outside Durham in northeast England. The battle captured King David II of Scotland, marking a decisive moment in Anglo-Scottish history.
author: Phys.org

title: AI converts scrap impurities into ingredients for stronger recycled iron
content:
AI technology is being applied to transform impurities found in scrap metal into useful ingredients that can produce stronger recycled iron.  

Global metal output reaches roughly 2 billion metric tons each year, a level that underpins industry, infrastructure and the energy sector. That scale of production accounts for an estimated 40 % of industrial greenhouse‑gas emissions and about 10 % of worldwide energy consumption.  

Expanding the use of recycled metals therefore offers a pathway to lessen the environmental footprint of metal manufacturing and to reduce dependence on imports of scarce, strategically important raw materials.
summary: AI can transform impurities in scrap metal into useful components for producing stronger recycled iron. Using more recycled metals could lower the 40% of industrial greenhouse gas emissions and 10% of global energy consumption tied to primary metal production.
author: Phys.org

title: New paper traces CDK research evolution and next-gen cancer therapies
content: A new paper traces the evolution of cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) research, marking more than 30 years since the direct connection between the molecular machinery controlling cell division and cancer was established. The study outlines the next generation of CDK-targeted therapies, extending from the initial discovery of CDK9 to applications in precision medicine and beyond.
summary: A new paper outlines the next generation of CDK-targeted therapies for cancer. The publication also traces the evolution of cyclin-dependent kinase research over more than 30 years.
author: Phys.org

title: Single 2D crystal becomes transistor with built-in insulation and contacts
content:
A new development in semiconductor technology involves a single two-dimensional crystal that transforms into a transistor with built-in insulation and electrical contacts. Traditional transistors require several fundamentally different materials, including a semiconductor to carry current, an insulating dielectric to control it, and metallic contacts for current entry and exit.

Integrating these distinct components becomes increasingly difficult as semiconductor devices approach the atomic scale. The new single-crystal approach addresses this challenge by combining the necessary functional elements within one material structure.
summary: A transistor typically requires multiple different materials, including a semiconductor, insulating dielectric, and metallic contacts. Integrating these components is difficult as semiconductor devices approach the atomic scale.
author: Phys.org

title: Building trust in governments through digital platforms
content:
Global surveys indicate that a significant portion of the population reports a lack of trust in their respective governments. This decline in confidence has been particularly notable in recent decades across Latin America, North America, and Africa.

As these regions experience falling trust levels, the focus has turned to methods for restoring public confidence. Digital platforms are being examined as a potential tool for governments to rebuild this trust with their citizens.
summary: Around the world, many people report distrusting their government. In some places, such as Latin America, North America and Africa, trust in government has declined in recent decades.
author: Phys.org

title: Satellite data offers clues on how glacial ice cliffs will collapse as climate warms
content: Scientists have not yet determined with certainty how the towering ice cliffs at the leading edges of glaciers will behave as global temperatures rise. However, recent analysis of satellite data provides initial clues regarding the stability of these glacial ice cliffs.
summary: The behavior of towering ice cliffs at the leading edge of glaciers remains uncertain as the climate warms. Satellite data provides some clues regarding how these cliffs may collapse.
author: New Scientist

title: New computational approach reveals how cells communicate to assemble tissues
content:
A new computational approach has revealed how cells communicate to assemble into tissues. This discovery provides insight into the language cells use to coordinate their interactions during tissue formation.

The findings could accelerate stem cell engineering and improve the development of disease models. Additionally, the research may inform the creation of new therapies by clarifying the mechanisms of cellular communication.
summary: A new computational approach reveals how cells communicate to assemble into tissues. This discovery could accelerate stem cell engineering, improve disease models, and inform therapies.
author: MIT News

title: MIT report finds record supply chain sustainability commitment but governance lags
content: A new report from MIT's Center for Transportation and Logistics indicates that corporate commitment to supply chain sustainability has reached a record high. However, the findings reveal significant governance gaps and external disruptions that are currently hindering the execution of these sustainability goals.
summary: MIT's Center for Transportation and Logistics reports that corporate sustainability commitments are at a record high. However, governance gaps and external disruptions prevent the execution of these commitments.
author: MIT News

title: Neanderthal shoulder wound in Iraqi Kurdistan may be oldest spear kill evidence
content:
Archaeologists excavating the Shanidar cave in Iraqi Kurdistan have identified a Neanderthal adult who died more than 70,000 years ago with a smooth round hole in the shoulder blade. This distinctive injury, described as a “kill shot,” may constitute the oldest evidence to date of a human ancestor being killed by a wooden spear.

The skeletal remains of the adult and other Neanderthals were recovered from beneath nearly 8 meters of rock and sediment. The discovery provides significant insight into prehistoric hunting practices and the physical capabilities of early human ancestors.
summary: An adult Neanderthal excavated from Shanidar cave in Iraqi Kurdistan died more than 70,000 years ago with a distinctive shoulder injury. This wound may be the oldest evidence so far of a human ancestor being killed by a wooden spear.
author: Guardian Science

title: NASA Satellites Track Historic 2026 El Niño Development
content: NASA is closely monitoring the development of the 2026 El Niño, a natural climate pattern characterized by warmer-than-normal water temperatures in parts of the equatorial Pacific. This phenomenon, which emerges roughly every two to seven years, is described as being rarer than a solar eclipse and more powerful than any single storm system.
summary: NASA is closely monitoring a 2026 El Niño event described as rarer than a solar eclipse and more powerful than any single storm system. This natural climate pattern involves warmer-than-normal water temperatures in parts of the equatorial Pacific and typically emerges every two to seven years.
author: NASA News

title: NASA to Support JAXA's MMX Mission to Study Mars' Moons
content:
NASA is collaborating with the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) on the Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission to investigate the origins of Mars’ moons, Phobos and Deimos. This partnership builds on NASA’s extensive history of exploring the Red Planet.

The primary objectives of the MMX mission are to characterize the two moons and determine their origin. Additionally, the mission is designed to deliver a sample, contributing to the scientific understanding of these celestial bodies.
summary: NASA is playing an important role in JAXA's MMX mission to advance understanding of Mars' moons. The mission aims to characterize and determine the origin of Phobos and Deimos while delivering a sample.
author: NASA News

content: A refurbished Ecobee thermostat is available for $120 through October 21, offering a way to upgrade heating routines for winter without purchasing the most advanced model. The deal provides a cost-effective option for consumers looking to make their home heating systems smarter.

title: Meta and Apple team up to make Muse AI models run better on Macs
content:
Meta announced the Muse Spark Open AI model, describing it as the "most capable US open-weight model to date." The company also stated that it is the first model in its class capable of running on a desktop using two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios equipped with the latest MLX framework.

Meta and Apple, typically rivals, collaborated on the launch and are publicly supporting one another. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg posted on X that the weights are releasing today and that the model runs well on the new Mac Studios due to work with Apple. title: Withings charges $100/year to sync new user data with third-party apps
content:
Withings has introduced a paid requirement for new users who wish to sync their health data with third-party applications such as Apple Health or Google Health. According to a discussion on the company’s support forums, accounts created on or after October 13, 2026, must subscribe to Withings Plus to access the "automatic sync to third-party apps" feature.

The Withings Plus subscription is priced at $9.95 per month or $99.50 per year. New device owners can access this syncing capability during a free one-month trial period included with their smartwatches or smart scales.
summary: New Withings accounts created from October 13, 2026, require a Withings Plus subscription to use automatic sync to third-party apps. The subscription costs $9.95 per month or $99.50 per year, though devices include a free one-month trial.
author: The Verge

title: Bluesky's Attie AI tool now enables users to create and share social games and apps
content:
Bluesky’s Attie AI tool has expanded its capabilities beyond building custom feeds to allow users to create small social apps, including games, polls, and dashboards. These applications can be shared with others as standalone websites. In an interview at TechCrunch Disrupt, Bluesky CEO Toni Schneider described Attie as “social vibe coding or vibe coding for your community.”

Users can generate Attie apps by entering a text prompt. The article notes that creating a simple poll about Pokémon Red and Pokémon Blue took a few minutes to generate. The Attie website currently highlights several examples of more full-featured applications.
summary: Bluesky's Attie AI tool has expanded its features to allow users to generate small social apps, including games, polls, and dashboards, that can be shared as websites. CEO Toni Schneider described the tool as "social vibe coding" that lets users build these applications by typing in a prompt.
author: The Verge

title: Trump posts AI-edited photo of White House restoration work
content:
President Donald Trump shared a series of images on Truth Social highlighting renovations to the White House, including a comparison of an old column and a "restored" version. However, the restored image appears to be modified with artificial intelligence, as it was flagged by Google’s AI detector as "made or edited with OpenAI."

Users on Reddit identified several discrepancies in the photograph, noting that the "restored" column features an uneven number of steps on both sides of the structure. The step count in the after image also does not match the one in the "before" photo, and the two images appear nearly identical in angle and detail.
summary: President Donald Trump posted a series of photos on Truth Social showing White House renovations, but one image appears to be modified with AI. The photo was flagged by Google's AI detector as made or edited with OpenAI, and users noted discrepancies in the number of steps shown.
author: The Verge

title: What did the Liberty Bell sound like? Science is on the case.
content: Researchers at Penn State Behrend investigated the acoustic properties of the Liberty Bell by conducting a modal analysis of a 20th-century replica. The study aimed to determine what the historic bell sounded like by examining the physical characteristics of the modern copy.
summary: Researchers hunted for clues in modal analysis of 20th-century replica bell at Penn State Behrend.
author: Ars Technica

title: Last chance to save up to $200 on TechCrunch Founder Summit pass: Early booking ends October 16
content:
TechCrunch is ending early‑booking discounts for its Founder Summit on Friday, October 16.  Attendees can save up to $200 on Founder and Investor Passes, but the savings will vanish after the deadline.

The summit will bring together about 1,000 founders and investors on November 4 at Boston’s SoWa Power Station.  Participants are encouraged to bring their toughest questions and make the day count for their businesses.
summary: Savings of up to $200 end October 16 for TechCrunch Founder Summit. The discount for Founder and Investor Passes ends after Friday, and the summit will be held on November 4 at Boston’s SoWa Power Station.
