title: David Silva to end retirement for one match with Hong Kong club Supreme Sha Tin
content:
Former Manchester City midfielder David Silva is set to make a brief return to professional football at the age of 40, agreeing to play a single match for Supreme Sha Tin. The former international will join a roster of notable players who have previously competed in the territory, including George Best, Bobby Moore, and Diego Forlán.

Hong Kong’s local Premier League has recently sought to elevate its profile, following years of attempts to maintain an independent football association while navigating its status as a special administrative region of China. Although efforts to place a local team in the Chinese Super League during a period of high spending did not materialize, the local league has continued to attract high-profile talent.

Silva’s appearance marks the latest addition to a long history of football in the city, which began during its time as a British colony and has persisted since 1997. The match offers the ambitious club a one-day opportunity to feature a former Premier League star on their team.
summary: Former Manchester City midfielder David Silva is coming out of retirement at age 40 to play a single match for the Hong Kong club Supreme Sha Tin. The article notes that Silva will join a long list of former international stars who have played in the territory.

title: Sunderland to face Torreense in Portugal after 53 years away from Europe
content:
Sunderland prepares to travel to Portugal on Thursday night to face Torreense in the Europa League, marking the club’s first competitive appearance on European soil in 53 years. The visit offers a symbolic parallel to the Black Cats’ last European outing, which was a second leg of a European Cup Winners’ Cup tie against Sporting in Lisbon. That previous encounter occurred when Sunderland were FA Cup holders competing in the Second Division.

Torreense, also a second-tier side, has generated surprise by securing a spot in the Europa League’s initial phase after defeating Sporting in the Portuguese Cup final last season. The Portuguese club’s campaign was further strengthened last month when they recorded a 2-1 victory over Lillestrom in Norway, boosting their prospects for advancing to next spring’s sudden-death rounds. This match provides Sunderland with a respite from a difficult start to their Premier League season.
summary: Sunderland will play Torreense in the Europa League, marking the club's first competitive European match in 53 years. The Black Cats are using this trip as a break from their difficult start to the Premier League season.

title: New biography details Renée Richards' 1977 US Open lawsuit and current stance
content:
In 1977, ophthalmologist Dr. Renée Richards sued for the right to compete in the women’s draw of the US Open following a sex-change operation. At the time, Richards had excelled as a male amateur player, and her legal battle dominated tennis headlines. The case was successfully argued by the firm of Roy Cohn, who is better known for prosecuting suspected communists during the red scare and mentoring Donald Trump.

A new biography titled Finding Renée Richards: The Groundbreaking Story of Tennis’s Trans Pioneer by Julie Kliegman explores this complex legacy. The book details the narrative of Richards’s 1977 lawsuit and highlights her current stance, as she now supports bans on trans athletes in women’s sports.
summary: A new biography by Julie Kliegman explores the complex legacy of tennis pioneer Renée Richards. The book covers her 1977 lawsuit to play in the US Open, where she was represented by Roy Cohn, and notes her current support for bans on trans athletes in women's sports.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England winger Feyi-Waboso on track for Nations Championship after hamstring tweak
content:
England’s game-breaking winger Manny Feyi-Waboso is on track to be fit for international duty next month, despite tweaking a hamstring during Exeter’s match against Newcastle on Sunday. Initial scans have not revealed any major damage, leading Exeter Chiefs director of rugby Rob Baxter to express hope that the 23-year-old will return to action soon.

Medical staff from both Exeter and England have reviewed the player's scans, confirming that Feyi-Waboso will be unavailable for his club’s opening Champions Cup pool fixture at Toulouse on Saturday. Early indications remain positive, with the winger expected to feature in England’s opening Nations Championship Test against Australia on 8 November.
summary: Manny Feyi-Waboso is expected to be fit for England's opening Nations Championship Test against Australia on 8 November despite a hamstring injury. Initial scans showed no major damage, but he will miss Exeter's Champions Cup match at Toulouse.

title: Infantino faces grilling at Fifa council meeting over World Cup sell-off and Trump prize
content:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino is set to face intense scrutiny from council members during a Thursday meeting at the organization’s headquarters in Zurich. The agenda includes his role in the abandoned World Cup sell-off plan, the Folarin Balogun affair, and the decision to award Donald Trump the inaugural FIFA peace prize. One attendee has predicted the discussions could be “explosive.”

This gathering marks Infantino’s first face-to-face encounter with his critics since he rejected repeated calls for an extraordinary general meeting of the council earlier in the summer. Those calls followed the emergence of the controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposals. Opponents are expected to press for an independent review during the session.
summary: Gianni Infantino will be questioned by Fifa council members regarding the aborted World Cup sell-off plan, the Folarin Balogun affair, and the awarding of the inaugural Fifa peace prize to Donald Trump. The meeting is expected to be heated, with opponents pressing for an independent review of these controversial decisions.

title: Peak District inn holds cricket memorabilia from Bradman and Australia
content:
Tucked away on a hillside in the Peak District, a local inn has accumulated a wealth of memorabilia and stories left behind by touring cricket teams. The article contrasts this historic setting with the modern travel habits of professional cricketers, who typically stay in chain hotels like the Crowne Plaza or Holiday Inn and spend their downtime playing golf.

Visitors can reach the area by taking a train to Grindleford, a station marked by homemade bunting along the platform fence that highlights books about trains during the national year of reading. The surrounding landscape features early morning rain and autumnal trees, with golden beech and rusty horse chestnut hues visible on the slopes of Padley Gorge and in the nearby valleys.
summary: A hotel in the Peak District is filled with memorabilia and stories left by touring cricket teams, including Don Bradman and Australia. The article contrasts this historic inn with modern hotel chains, describing the rural setting near Grindleford station.

title: Martínez Says Wilcox Failing as United Teammates Share Frustration
content:

The defender voiced his concerns following United’s 2-0 Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid on Tuesday. While teammates widely support Martínez’s assessment that Wilcox is failing, his outburst is also viewed as an effort to facilitate his own transfer, as he is out of contract next summer and intends to leave the club.

The recent loss leaves Manchester United with only two wins for the season. The team had previously secured six points from their first six Premier League matches, a start that marks the club’s poorest league opening in 40 years.
summary: Lisandro Martínez criticized director of football Jason Wilcox after Manchester United's 2-0 defeat at Atlético Madrid, a view teammates say reflects general dressing room frustration. Martínez is out of contract next summer and plans to leave the club.

title: Supreme Court to Decide Scope of 1988 Video Privacy Protection Act
content:
The Supreme Court will examine the scope of the 1988 Video Privacy Protection Act (VPPA) on Wednesday, assessing how this decades-old privacy law applies to modern digital tracking tools. The case has the potential to influence current and future litigation regarding consumer privacy protections.

The justices are considering whether the VPPA safeguards consumers who subscribe to any of a company’s products or only those specifically covered by the original statute. The ruling will clarify the reach of the law, which was originally designed to protect video rental records.
summary: The Supreme Court will examine whether the 1988 Video Privacy Protection Act protects consumers who subscribe to any of a company's products or only specific ones. The case could shape current and future lawsuits over digital tracking tools.

title: Marine Conservation Society urges shoppers to scale back on hake and coley
content:
The Marine Conservation Society (MCS) has advised UK shoppers to reduce their consumption of hake and coley due to declining stocks and increased fishing pressure. These two species, which are popular alternatives to cod, have received lower sustainability ratings in the charity’s Good Fish Guide.

Previously, consumers were encouraged to avoid UK-caught cod and purchase European hake or coley instead. However, the MCS now indicates that these alternative options are also facing sustainability challenges. The charity utilizes a traffic-light system in its guide to rate seafood based on fish stock health and environmental impact, assisting consumers and businesses in making informed choices.
summary: The Marine Conservation Society (MCS) has lowered the sustainability ratings for European hake and coley due to declining stocks and increased fishing pressure, following its earlier recommendation that UK shoppers avoid UK‑caught cod and buy these alternatives. MCS publishes its Good Fish Guide, which uses a traffic‑light system to rate seafood based on fish stock health and environmental impact.

A common gut bacterium produces a molecule that inhibits cholesterol production in the liver. Researchers administered this molecule to mice that are prone to artery disease to observe its effects on plaque accumulation.

The treated mice developed approximately half as much fatty plaque compared to untreated control animals.
summary: A common gut bacterium produces a molecule that slows cholesterol production in the liver. Researchers found that giving this molecule to mice prone to artery disease resulted in roughly half as much fatty plaque as untreated controls.

title: Researchers link Earth's two warmest periods to flowering plant diversification
content:
Researchers from Australia and Austria have linked the two warmest periods in Earth’s last 140 million years to both mass extinctions and rapid increases in plant diversity. Their study, published in Nature Plants, analyzed fossilized pollen and spores and found that extreme global warmth during the mid‑Cretaceous and early Cenozoic was central to plant evolution.  

The authors argue that these climate shifts helped explain how flowering plants came to dominate land plants. Their findings also suggest that the same warm intervals influenced the evolution of other major land plant groups.
summary: Researchers in Australia and Austria published a study in Nature Plants showing that the mid‑Cretaceous and early Cenozoic periods of extreme global warmth drove mass extinctions and explosive plant diversification, leading to the dominance of flowering plants. The study examined fossilized pollen and spores and indicates that these warm periods were central to the evolution of both flowering plants and other major land plant groups.

title: Ask HN: Will Senior Engineers Become Obsolete as LLMs Advance?
content:
A recent discussion on Hacker News explores the future trajectory of senior engineers, questioning when the need for human involvement in software design will diminish. The post argues that Large Language Models (LLMs), which have evolved from simple autocomplete tools in 2024 to agents capable of building "software factories," are being reinforced with data for tasks with clear right or wrong answers, such as coding and mathematics. The author suggests that companies like Anthropic and OpenAI could soon build datasets for software architecture, potentially making human guidance obsolete.

The post posits that business-wise, the need for actual software programming skills may decrease by 90% within a few years. It predicts that roles requiring people skills, such as product leads, will become more favored as agents handle the technical implementation. The author expresses skepticism toward the common industry assertion that humans will still be necessary for guiding agents and designing architecture, viewing the current era of human-driven coding as a "good run" that is coming to an end.
summary: The poster asks when the need for a human in the design loop will cease as LLMs become fully capable, and what currently stops LLMs from building datasets of good and bad architecture and RL‑ing that. They predict that the need for actual software programmer skills is 90% out in a few years, and that product lead roles will be favored more because they have more people skills.

title: Nonprofit Opens Free 3D Digital Leonardo da Vinci Museum
content:
The founder of a small nonprofit has launched Museum of Ages, a digital Leonardo da Vinci museum featuring a virtual tour with 17 stops. The free entrance includes close-to-real-size views of his paintings, 15 machines rebuilt in code, and 29 anatomy sheets. Visitors can also examine 207 selected manuscript pages in a virtual reading table, with 131 of those pages translated, and explore a reconstruction of da Vinci’s last house in Amboise.

The museum is available in seven languages and labels each stop with one of four grades: documented, reconstructed, conjectural, or not known. Detailed views allow users to inspect the sources for each element. The project utilizes Three.js for materials and runs on WebGPU, with WebGL2 as a fallback for unsupported browsers. Textures are derived from Creative Commons Zero photo scans and free 3D models.

The organization’s mission is to create walkable digital museums for individuals unable to visit physical locations due to illness, disability, cost, or distance. To ensure accessibility, the walk was pre-rendered to function on older phones and accommodate older users. The code is released under the AGPL-3.0 license, while texts and pictures are licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.
summary: The nonprofit Museum of Ages released a free virtual tour featuring 17 stops, including 15 rebuilt machines and 207 manuscript pages. The project uses WebGPU and Three.js to make museums accessible to people with disabilities or financial constraints.

The project aims to eliminate "magic" in the implementation process, with the developer noting that reimplementing concepts in a language other than Python helps clarify implementation nuances.

summary: A developer is building a ChatGPT-style model from first principles in TypeScript to gain a deeper understanding of transformers. The project covers dataloaders, embeddings, and the attention mechanism, with the developer seeking feedback on the implementation.

title: US military develops artificial blood to treat battlefield casualties
content: In February 2007, a dual-rotor casualty evacuation helicopter with the call sign Morphine 1-2 transported three wounded soldiers to a field hospital in Balad, north of Baghdad. While at the facility, the crew received an emergency mission order to fly through an insurgent-controlled area in broad daylight, a route that typically posed significant risks for such aircraft.

title: 28 Energy Drinks Ranked From Celsius To Black Rifle
content:
A 2026 ranking of 28 energy drinks, including Celsius and Black Rifle, has been released to identify the best options for increasing alertness. The evaluation focuses on beverages designed to transition consumers from a tired state to a wired one.

These energy drinks are characterized by their specific ingredient profiles, which include B vitamins, red dye, and taurine. The ranking serves as a guide for selecting products that effectively boost energy levels.
summary: The article ranks 28 energy drinks, including Celsius and Black Rifle. It describes the beverages as containing B vitamins, red dye, and taurine.

title: Nothing Launches Pro Headphones with Enhanced Design, Comfort, Sound, and EQ
content:
Nothing has unveiled its latest offering, the Nothing Headphone (1) Pro, positioning it as the company’s best headphones yet. The model is marketed as delivering studio‑quality sound.

According to the announcement, the headphones emphasize design, comfort, sound quality, and highly adjustable EQ settings.
summary: Nothing has released its best headphones yet. They double down on design, comfort, sound quality, and highly adjustable EQ settings.

title: Breville Eye Q Toaster Review: Optical Sensors, Toast Quality Needs Improvement
content:
Breville’s new Eye Q toaster employs optical sensors to measure the darkness of toast, a feature highlighted as “cool tech” in recent reviews.  

Despite the innovative sensor system, reviewers note that the overall toasting quality does not meet expectations, indicating room for improvement.
summary: The Breville Eye Q toaster uses optical sensors to measure the darkness of your toast. The toasting quality needs improvement.
author: Wired

title: Fairphone releases Fairbuds 2 earbuds with smaller case and double battery life
content:
Fairphone has released the Fairbuds 2, its second generation of repairable earbuds, with a complete redesign from the original model. The new earbuds are just as repairable as the first generation but offer improved audio performance and nearly double the battery life.

The Fairbuds 2 feature a stemmed design and are available in black or green. Their charging case is 37 percent smaller than the first‑generation case, yet the earbuds now provide 40 hours of playback without active noise cancellation.

The earbuds are currently available in the UK and Europe for £99 (€119). A U.S. launch is scheduled for November 2nd at $119.
summary: Fairphone has released the Fairbuds 2, its second generation of repairable earbuds, featuring a stemmed design and a case 37 percent smaller than the original. The new earbuds provide improved audio and about 40 hours of battery life, nearly twice the first generation, and cost £99/€119 in the UK and Europe with a US launch at $119 on November 2.
author: The Verge

title: Tesla Roadster Expected to Debut Production at Waco Event After Decade
content:
After nearly a decade since Elon Musk’s surprise announcement of plans for a next‑generation Roadster, Tesla is finally expected to present a production‑ready version of the model at an event in Waco, Texas.

The new Roadster, whose 2017 concept image featured a light bar, has taken an extended development period. Its debut arrives as the electric‑vehicle market contends with high energy prices, political turmoil and consumer uncertainty, following a post‑COVID surge driven by tax‑credit incentives that has since slowed.

The timing highlights that the vehicle, which could have remained vaporware, is moving toward production despite the challenging market conditions.
summary: Elon Musk announced plans for a next‑generation Tesla Roadster nearly a decade ago, and the vehicle is now expected to make its production‑ready debut at an event in Waco, Texas. The launch comes amid an EV market facing high energy prices, political turmoil, and consumer uncertainty.
author: The Verge

title: Scimplify raises $25M, revenue $200M as it eyes U.S. AI-driven expansion against China
content:
Scimplify announced a $25 million financing round aimed at using artificial intelligence to challenge China’s dominance over critical materials.  

The company reported that its annualized revenue run rate has tripled to $200 million as it prepares to expand operations in the United States.
summary: Scimplify's annualized revenue run rate has tripled to $200 million as it eyes U. S.
author: TechCrunch

title: Bank of England, IMF warn cyber attacks could erode trust in financial system
content:
The governor of the Bank of England, Andrew Bailey, and International Monetary Fund chief Kristalina Georgieva warned that a surge in cyber‑attacks could erode confidence in the financial system. Speaking on a panel about online fraud at the IMF and World Bank meetings in Bangkok, they said the growing threat may push people to abandon formal banking and keep money in “shoeboxes under their bed.”

Bailey highlighted recent headlines describing self‑replicating AI agents hijacking personal devices and a French supermarket hack that raised refrigerator temperatures to 50 °C. Both officials cautioned that such incidents illustrate how cyber‑crime could undermine trust in financial institutions.
summary: Bank of England governor Andrew Bailey and IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva warned that rising cyber-attacks could erode trust in the financial system. They cited examples such as self‑replicating AI agents hijacking personal devices and a French supermarket hack that heated fridges to 50°C.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Nvidia pledges $250m of computing power to UK for AI safety research
content:
Nvidia, the US chipmaker valued at $5.5 tn (£4.1 tn), announced a pledge of $250 million in computing power to the United Kingdom to support AI safety research.  

The five‑year donation comes as concerns about AI agents have risen, and follows the UK government’s confirmation that its AI Security Institute will be able to examine cutting‑edge technology from firms such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google before those models are released.  

The funding is intended to bolster the Institute’s testing of advanced AI models.
summary: Nvidia, valued at $5.5tn, is donating $250m of computing power to the United Kingdom to support AI safety research over a five‑year period. The UK government said its AI Security Institute will be able to examine cutting‑edge models from companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google before release.
author: Guardian Technology

title: World Risk Poll Finds Africa Leads Global Gains in Disaster Resilience
content:
A new study shows that Africa has recorded the world’s fastest gains in disaster resilience. The findings come from the World Risk Poll, which surveyed 143,000 people in 140 countries.  

The poll found that North Africa’s resilience score rose by five points, while Southern Africa’s increased by four points.  The improvements were attributed to expanding internet access and greater household preparedness.  

Despite these gains, the study notes that 220 million people affected by disasters in the past five years received no warning.
summary: The World Risk Poll surveyed 143,000 people in 140 countries and found North Africa up five points and Southern Africa up four in disaster resilience, driven by expanding internet access and household preparedness. However, 220 million people affected by disasters in the past five years received no warning.
author: Euronews

title: Trump criticized for posting video of UK man William Chapman killed by tiger
content:
Trump faces backlash after posting a “sick” video of a UK man killed by a tiger.  

The man in the real footage, identified by the BBC as William Chapman, later died from his injuries following the Saturday incident, police said.
summary: Trump faced backlash after posting a video that showed a UK man being killed by a tiger. Police said the man, identified by the BBC as William Chapman, later died from his injuries following the Saturday incident.
author: Euronews

title: Duane Davis sentenced to minimum 40 years for orchestrating Tupac Shakur's murder
content:
Duane Davis has been sentenced to a minimum of 40 years in prison for orchestrating the murder of Tupac Shakur.  

Shakur was a key figure in a hip‑hop rivalry pitting the US East Coast against the West Coast. He was just 25 when he was gunned down in Las Vegas.
summary: Duane Davis was sentenced to a minimum of 40 years in prison for orchestrating the murder of Tupac Shakur. Shakur, a 25‑year‑old key figure in the East Coast–West Coast hip‑hop rivalry, was gunned down in Las Vegas.
author: Euronews

title: Iran executes Ali‑Sina Mostafavi, accused of armed attacks during US‑Israeli strikes
content:
Iran has executed Ali‑Sina Mostafavi, a 38‑year‑old mountaineer and musician from Kerman, on charges of “enmity against God.”  

Mostafavi was accused of firing on civilians and soldiers during the opening months of the war.  He was also charged with participating in the January protests and sending footage.
summary: Ali‑Sina Mostafavi, a 38‑year‑old mountaineer and musician from Kerman, was executed in Iran on charges of “enmity against God.” He was accused of firing on civilians and soldiers during the opening months of the war, and of participating in the January protests and sending footage.

content:
On October 14th, 2026, the midday news bulletin offers a concise update on the most important stories from around Europe and beyond. The bulletin highlights the latest news and breaking news across a range of topics.

title: King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia visit Ceuta in first royal trip since 2007
content:
King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia arrived in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta on Tuesday, where cheering crowds waved Spanish flags as the royal couple made a diplomatically sensitive visit.  

The trip follows a surge of migrants from Morocco that entered Ceuta in July, and it marks the first time the monarchs have visited the city since 2007, when a diplomatic crisis erupted with neighbouring Morocco. Morocco claims sovereignty over Ceuta and Spain’s other North African territory, Melilla.  

The visit highlights Spain’s reaffirmation of its authority over the enclave.
summary: King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia arrived in Ceuta on Tuesday amid cheering crowds waving Spanish flags. The visit, the first by Spanish royals since 2007, came after a July migrant influx from Morocco and occurs despite Morocco’s claim of sovereignty over Ceuta and Melilla.
author: France 24

title: Ukrainian ex-military officer Serhii K. on trial in Germany for Nord Stream sabotage
content:
A Ukrainian ex‑military officer began a trial in Germany on Wednesday, charged with organising the covert operation that destroyed the Nord Stream gas pipelines in September 2022, cutting western Europe off from Russia’s largest natural‑gas source.  

The suspect, identified under German privacy rules only as Serhii K., is alleged to have led a team of Ukrainian agents that included divers and an explosives expert to carry out what officials describe as one of the biggest infrastructure sabotage operations of modern times.  

FRANCE 24’s Jörg Taszman reported the proceedings from Berlin.  

The case is being heard before a German court.
summary: A Ukrainian ex-military officer identified as Serhii K. is on trial in Germany on Wednesday for allegedly organising the operation that blew up the Nord Stream gas pipelines in September 2022. He is accused of leading a group of Ukrainian agents, including divers and an explosives expert, in the sabotage.
author: France 24

title: Winnie the Pooh celebrates 100th anniversary
content:
Winnie the Pooh, the world’s most famous and very greedy bear, is celebrating his centenary this year.

The character made his debut in a story titled “The Wrong Kind of Bees” that appeared in the London Evening News. The first collection of Pooh stories, illustrated by E. H. Shepard, was published as a book on October 14, 1926.
summary: Winnie the Pooh is marking his centenary this year. He first appeared in the story “The Wrong Kind of Bees” in the London Evening News, and the initial collection illustrated by E. H. Shepard was published on October 14, 1926.
author: France 24

title: Scientists suggest some Super-Earths could be more habitable than Earth
content:
Scientists note that there may be planets more habitable than Earth elsewhere in the galaxy, raising the prospect that some Super‑Earths could offer conditions superior to those on our planet.  

The possibility of such worlds has prompted questions about whether they could ever be reached, though no specific missions or timelines were mentioned.  

The discussion appears alongside other international news items, but the scientific observation remains that more habitable planets might exist beyond Earth.
summary: Science news reports that there might be planets more habitable than Earth. The piece appears in a press review that also covers Portuguese housing, a German robot assault, and a Cosmopolitan dating article.
author: France 24

title: Rwanda to host Africa's first F1 Grand Prix in early 2030s under decade-long deal
content:
Rwanda and Formula One announced on Tuesday that the East African nation will host Africa’s first Formula One Grand Prix since 1993, slated for the early 2030s. The agreement is a decade‑long deal between the circuit and Rwanda.

The plan follows years of Rwanda’s efforts to use sports such as football and basketball to boost its image and attract investment, and it would mark the continent’s return to the F1 calendar after a three‑decade hiatus.

Human rights group Amnesty International criticised the arrangement, accusing Formula One of offering Rwanda a “sportswashing prize.”
summary: Rwanda will host Africa's first Formula One Grand Prix since 1993 in the early 2030s after a decade-long deal was announced on Tuesday. Amnesty International accused Formula One of offering Rwanda a sportswashing prize.
author: France 24

title: Dangote refinery extends IPO as plant reshapes Nigeria's fuel market
content:
The initial public offering for the Dangote Refinery was extended by two weeks and will now close on October 27, 2026, after a “huge popular success,” according to FRANCE 24’s Chinwe Ossundu.  

The extension comes as the escalation of conflict in the Middle East and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz have driven up global crude prices and created supply shortages, prompting African and European countries to turn in mass to the refinery.  

The plant, operated by the leading African producer of crude oil, aims to transform its role into a regional hub for refining and petrochemicals.
summary: The Dangote refinery's IPO was extended for two weeks and will close on October 27, 2026 after a huge popular response. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz and rising crude prices have prompted African and European countries to turn to the refinery, which seeks to become a regional hub for refining and petrochemicals.
author: France 24

title: World leaders and Vatican cardinals pray for Pope Leo after lung cancer diagnosis
content:
World leaders, Catholics worldwide and senior cardinals at the Vatican gathered to pray for Pope Leo on Wednesday after doctors announced that the 71‑year‑old pontiff had been diagnosed with lung cancer and had part of one lung removed.

The diagnosis, which shocked many, comes less than a year after Pope Leo’s election in May 2025, a period during which he was noted for his relative youth and energetic demeanor.
summary: World leaders, Catholics worldwide and senior Vatican cardinals offered prayers for Pope Leo on Wednesday after doctors announced the 71‑year‑old pontiff was diagnosed with lung cancer and had part of one lung removed. The pope, elected in May 2025 and described as relatively young and energetic, caused shock with the diagnosis.
author: France 24

title: Republicans pour hundreds of millions into defending red-state seats ahead of midterms
content:
U.S. President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that Republicans face an equally difficult fight to retain control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate in November’s midterm elections, even as forecasts suggest a considerably tougher contest for the House.

Despite the outlook, the party is allocating hundreds of millions of dollars to defend congressional and state‑level seats that were once considered safely red. In states such as North Carolina and Georgia, Republicans appear to be scaling back their ambitions, shifting resources to other Republican strongholds where Democrats are mounting unexpected challenges, according to France 24 International Affairs commentator Douglas Herbert.
summary: US President Donald Trump said Republicans face an equally difficult fight to retain control of both the House and Senate in the November midterm elections, despite forecasts of a tougher House contest. The party is spending hundreds of millions of dollars to defend previously safe red congressional and state seats, while scaling back in North Carolina and Georgia to shift resources to other Republican strongholds where Democrats pose unexpected challenges.
author: France 24

title: Former DRC President Joseph Kabila joins political‑military front with Rwandan‑backed M23
content:
Former Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) President Joseph Kabila has joined a new political‑military front that brings together the Rwandan‑backed AFC/M23 coalition, a move that raises questions over peace in the country.

The front unites the AFC/M23 coalition, known to receive support from Rwanda, with Kabila’s participation indicating a shift in alliances. Observers note that this alignment could affect ongoing efforts to stabilize the DRC.
summary: Former DRC President Joseph Kabila has joined a new political‑military front. The front brings together the Rwandan‑backed AFC/M23 coalition.
author: DW World

title: Hardliners pressure Iran government, demand removal of Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi
content:
Iran’s political landscape is becoming increasingly fraught as hardliners intensify pressure on the government. The current climate of infighting is highlighted by calls for the removal of Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.

In addition to the push for Araghchi’s dismissal, the oil minister has resigned. Despite this leadership change, the pressure on President Masoud Pezeshkian has not eased.
summary: Hardliners are stepping up pressure on Iran's government and calling for Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi's removal. The oil minister resigned, but the move has done little to ease pressure on President Masoud Pezeshkian.
author: DW World

title: Trump announces new Super Intelligence taskforce with AI czar Jay Clayton
content: Trump announced a new Super Intelligence taskforce aimed at ensuring the United States maintains a leadership position in artificial intelligence development. The initiative is overseen by White House AI czar Jay Clayton, who will direct a group focused on advancing U.S. competitiveness in AI on the global stage. The announcement signals a renewed emphasis on national investment and coordination in the field of artificial intelligence.
summary: Trump announced a new Super Intelligence taskforce. The taskforce is led by White House AI czar Jay Clayton and is responsible for ensuring the US leads international competition in artificial intelligence development.
author: DW World

title: General Assembly adopts pandemic prevention declaration with 153 votes, three against
content:
The United Nations General Assembly adopted a political declaration on pandemic prevention, preparedness and response on Monday. The resolution passed with 153 votes in favour, three votes against, and two abstentions.

The three countries that voted against the declaration were Argentina, Israel and the United States. New Zealand and Paraguay abstained from voting.
summary: The General Assembly on Monday adopted a political declaration on pandemic prevention, preparedness and response. The vote was 153 in favour, three against (Argentina, Israel and United States) and two abstentions (New Zealand and Paraguay).
author: UN News

title: UN Special Representative urges stronger global action to protect children in crises
content:
The UN Special Representative on Violence Against Children warned that global action to end violence against children is lagging behind the growing risks faced by boys and girls in crises. The representative called for stronger worldwide efforts to protect children caught up in an increasing number of emergencies.

According to the statement, current measures are insufficient, leaving many children vulnerable to violence as crises multiply. The UN expert urged the international community to intensify its response to safeguard children worldwide.
summary: The UN Special Representative on Violence Against Children said current global efforts to protect children are insufficient. He called for stronger action to safeguard boys and girls affected by an increasing number of crises.
author: UN News

title: Disasters cause $228 billion in annual housing losses worldwide
content:
Disasters cost $228 billion in housing losses every year, a figure that highlights the financial burden communities around the world face when rebuilding after a disaster strikes.  

The $228 billion represents the amount of money communities must find annually to replace damaged or destroyed homes. This figure underscores the scale of the challenge in restoring housing following natural or man‑made disasters.
summary: Communities around the world face $228 billion in housing losses each year. The figure represents the cost of rebuilding homes after disasters strike.

title: Russian attacks kill residents and injure dozens in Kharkiv and Kyiv
content: Russian attacks on Ukraine’s two largest cities, Kharkiv and Kyiv, have again killed and injured civilians, damaging homes and civilian infrastructure, the UN aid coordination office (OCHA) said on Tuesday. The attacks occurred in recent days, according to the OCHA statement.
summary: Russian attacks on Ukraine’s two largest cities, Kharkiv and Kyiv, have killed residents and injured dozens of civilians. The attacks also damaged homes and civilian infrastructure, the UN aid coordination office (OCHA) said on Tuesday.
author: UN News

title: UN chief says need for UN never greater, proposes $3.3 billion budget for 2027
content:
Secretary‑General António Guterres told the United Nations on Tuesday that “the need for the United Nations has never been greater” as the organization confronts climate disruption, an AI revolution, war and growing hunger.

Guterres presented a programme budget proposal of $3.3 billion for the next year, which represents a reduction of $40.8 million from the previous level. The slimmer budget reflects the agency’s effort to align resources with the expanding challenges it faces.
summary: Secretary-General António Guterres said the need for the United Nations has never been greater amid climate disruption, an AI revolution, war and growing hunger. He presented a programme budget proposal of $3.3 billion for 2027, a cut of $40.8 million.
author: UN News

title: UN agency says fewer West African migrants reach Europe by sea, journey still unsafe
content:
Fewer people from West Africa are reaching Europe by sea, but the journey has not become safer, the UN migration agency (IOM) said on Tuesday.

The IOM noted that despite the decline in the number of migrants attempting the crossing, the risks associated with the sea voyage remain unchanged.
summary: The UN migration agency (IOM) said fewer people from West Africa are reaching Europe by sea. It added that the journey has not become safer.
author: UN News

title: UNDP warns 800 million young people in developing economies risk unemployment
content:
The head of the UN Development Programme (UNDP) warned on Tuesday that roughly 800 million young people entering the labour market in developing economies over the coming years will not find jobs unless countries act.  

The warning coincided with the agency’s launch of two initiatives aimed at boosting investment and employment.  

These initiatives are intended to address the projected employment gap for young people in developing economies.
summary: The head of the UN Development Programme (UNDP) warned on Tuesday that about 800 million young people entering the labour market in developing economies will not find jobs unless countries act. The agency also launched two initiatives to boost investment and employment.
author: UN News

title: UN says Taiz faces devastating humanitarian crisis as tensions raise food prices
content: Yemen’s southwestern city of Taiz is confronting a “devastating” humanitarian crisis amid a Houthi siege, a cholera outbreak and cuts to aid, the UN Spokesperson said on Tuesday. Escalating tensions are dramatically driving up food prices and causing shortages of supplies in the city. The combined pressures are putting civilians in the crosshairs of the crisis.
summary: The UN spokesperson said on Tuesday that Yemen’s southwestern city of Taiz is facing a devastating humanitarian crisis. Escalating tensions are dramatically driving up food prices and causing shortages of supplies.
author: UN News

title: Joni Mitchell, 82, becomes U.S. citizen after 62‑year journey
content:
Canada‑born singer‑songwriter Joni Mitchell, 82, announced she has become a United States citizen. The milestone follows her move to the United States in the mid‑1960s.

Mitchell shared video of her naturalisation ceremony on Instagram, accompanied by a photo beside an American flag and the caption, “A journey that began 62 years ago.” The new status grants her the right to vote in U.S. elections, a privilege she previously said she was unable to exercise.
summary: Canada‑born singer‑songwriter Joni Mitchell, 82, posted Instagram footage of her U.S. citizenship ceremony. The ceremony, following her move to the United States in the mid‑1960s, now allows her to vote in U.S. elections.

title: German authorities scramble fighter jets after false hijack alert on Corfu‑Nuremberg flight
content: A radio glitch triggered a false hijack alert, prompting German authorities to scramble fighter jets. The alert came after a pilot sent a hijack signal while flying a plane from Corfu to Nuremberg. Fighter jets were deployed to escort the aircraft as a precaution. The incident was later identified as a false alarm caused by the radio malfunction.
summary: Authorities scrambled fighter jets to escort a plane traveling from Corfu to Nuremberg. The scramble was triggered by a pilot’s hijack alert that was later found to be caused by a radio glitch.

title: Albanian students clash with police over education costs, university conditions and jobs
content:
Albanian students clashed with police while demonstrating against high education costs, poor university conditions and bleak job prospects.  

The confrontations occurred as the students protested what they described as inadequate funding for higher education and limited employment opportunities after graduation.
summary: Albanian students clashed with police while protesting education costs, poor university conditions and bleak job prospects. The protests highlighted concerns about high education expenses, inadequate university facilities and limited employment opportunities.

title: Japanese journalist Imai Yuki arrested on Sakhalin for alleged spying on Russian defence
content:
Japanese journalist Imai Yuki was detained on Russia’s Sakhalin island after the Federal Security Service (FSB) accused her of spying on Russian defence capabilities.  

The FSB said the arrest was made on suspicion of gathering intelligence related to Russia’s military.
summary: Japanese journalist Imai Yuki was arrested on Sakhalin. The FSB says the arrest was for allegedly spying on Russian defence capabilities.

content: US President Donald Trump announced on his Truth Social platform a plan to pursue oil, gas and mineral exploration in Greenland. title: Iran increases Hormuz surveillance as ship attacks surge and oil flows fall
content: Iran has increased surveillance of the Strait of Hormuz amid a surge in attacks on vessels. title: Kyiv says Starlink restrictions hamper front‑line operations in Ukraine
content:
Kyiv says that recent restrictions on Starlink are hampering front‑line operations in Ukraine.  

According to the statement, Elon Musk’s satellite system enables Kyiv to protect Ukrainian skies and to effectively guide drones toward Russian targets.  

The city’s officials argue that limiting access to the service undermines these defensive and offensive capabilities.
summary: Kyiv reports that restrictions on Starlink are affecting front‑line operations. The system enables Kyiv to protect Ukrainian skies and guide drones to Russian targets.

content:

summary: Alaric Jackson, an offensive lineman for the Los Angeles Rams, was suspended for punching an opponent. Harrison Mevis, the Rams' kicker, was released by the club.

title: Trump says Taiwan to buy 30% of Alaska pipeline gas for 20 years

President Trump announced on Tuesday that Taiwan has agreed to purchase 30 percent of gas from the Alaska pipeline over the next 20 years. The statement was made while he spoke at a campaign rally in Wasilla, Alaska.

title: Collins, Jackson Clash in Third Maine Senate Debate Ahead of Election
content:
Collins, Jackson duke it out in third Maine Senate debate: 3 takeaways

Republican Sen. Susan Collins (R) and Democrat Troy Jackson clashed Tuesday in their third Maine Senate debate, with just three weeks remaining until Election Day. The debate marked the third time the two senators faced off in a public forum.

The senators sparred on several topics, including the incumbent’s votes for and against the Iran war and their differing views on how to address cost‑of‑living issues. This was the third debate between the two senators.
summary: Republican Sen. Susan Collins (R) and Democrat Troy Jackson clashed in their third Maine Senate debate on Tuesday, with only three weeks left until Election Day. title: Trump pardons diesel mechanics for Clean Air Act violations at Alaska rally
content:
President Trump issued pardons at a campaign rally in Alaska on Tuesday for two diesel mechanics who had been charged with and pleaded guilty to violating the Clean Air Act.  

The president signed the pardons for Zachary Czubak and Patrick Fleming on stage at the campaign event in Wasilla after inviting them onto the stage.  

The action was taken during the rally, with Trump publicly granting the pardons to the two mechanics.
summary: President Trump pardoned two diesel mechanics, Zachary Czubak and Patrick Fleming, who had pleaded guilty to Clean Air Act violations. The pardons were signed on stage at a campaign rally in Wasilla, Alaska, on Tuesday.

title: Ossoff, Collins Clash in Second Georgia Senate Debate
content:
Sen. Jon Ossoff (D) and Rep. Mike Collins (R) traded barbs during a Tuesday‑night debate in Georgia, marking the second face‑to‑face contest between the two Senate candidates. The exchange covered a range of issues, including the Jeffrey Epstein files and the 2020 election, among other topics.

Ossoff, the only Senate Democrat running for reelection in a state President Trump won in 2024, tied Collins to the administration’s controversial tariffs and war. The debate underscored the broader political divide between the candidates on key policy matters.
summary: Sen. Jon Ossoff and Rep. Mike Collins traded barbs in a Tuesday night debate, arguing over the Jeffrey Epstein files and the 2020 election. Ossoff, the only Senate Democrat running for reelection in a state President Trump won in 2024, tied Collins to the administration’s tariffs and war.
