title: Review: Alex Gibney's 4-hour Musk documentary deemed compelling but overlong
content:
The 4‑hour documentary about Elon Musk, directed by Alex Gibney, has been reviewed as a provocative and compelling work that ultimately feels like two different films. The reviewer notes that the film is overlong.

According to the review, there is not much new material in the documentary for Ars readers.
summary: Alex Gibney's documentary about Musk runs four hours and is described as compelling but overlong. The review notes that it offers little new information for Ars readers.
author: Ars Technica

title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 focuses on building enduring AI-era companies
content:
TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 centers on a single question: “How do you build an enduring company in the AI era?” The event’s theme shapes every aspect of the conference.

According to the organizers, the programming and speaker lineup have been curated to reflect this focus, offering sessions and talks that explore strategies for long‑term success in the rapidly evolving AI landscape.
summary: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 is built around the question “How do you build an enduring company in the AI era?” Its programming and speaker lineup reflect that focus.
author: TechCrunch

title: Houthi strike hits Riyadh's King Khalid Airport, kills Pakistani resident, injures 11
content:
A fresh Houthi strike hit Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport on Sunday, Saudi authorities said. The attack killed a Pakistani resident and wounded 11 people.

The strike followed an earlier attack that killed at least 12 people and halted airport operations on Saturday. The Iran‑backed group has threatened further attacks on Saudi Arabia’s transit hubs.
summary: A Houthi strike hit Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport on Sunday, killing a Pakistani resident and wounding 11 people, Saudi authorities said. The attack followed a strike that killed at least 12 people and halted airport operations, and the Iran‑backed group warned of further attacks on Saudi transit hubs.
author: France 24

title: Airstrikes on Sudan-Egypt border gold mine kill at least 72 workers, rights group claims
content:
At least 72 workers were killed in airstrikes on a gold mine on the Sudan‑Egypt border on Saturday, a Sudanese rights group said on Sunday.  

The Emergency Lawyers organisation accused Egypt’s air force of carrying out the attack.  

AFP was unable to independently verify the account, and Egypt has issued no official comment.
summary: At least 72 workers were killed in airstrikes on a gold mine on the Sudan‑Egypt border on Saturday, the Sudanese rights group Emergency Lawyers said. AFP could not independently verify the account and Egypt has issued no official comment.
author: France 24

title: NATO top commander Alexus Grynkewich to warn Russia alliance can counter any attack
content:
NATO’s top military commander is slated to warn Russia on Monday that the alliance can counter any attack, officials said. The warning will be delivered by U.S. General Alexus Grynkewich, who is set to outline his “theory of victory” at a security conference in Warsaw.

The remarks come amid Western concerns about what officials describe as Moscow’s alleged campaign of sabotage and interference aimed at Ukraine’s wartime backers.
summary: NATO’s top military commander is expected to warn Russia on Monday that the alliance can counter any attack. US General Alexus Grynkewich will outline his “theory of victory” at a Warsaw security conference amid Western concerns over Moscow’s alleged sabotage and interference against Ukraine’s wartime backers.
author: France 24

title: North Korea launches multiple ballistic missiles off east coast, Seoul reports
content:
North Korea launched multiple ballistic missiles off its east coast on Monday, according to South Korea’s military. The launches occurred amid heightened tensions following border landmine explosions that injured three South Korean soldiers last month.

Seoul said the missiles were fired from Pyongyang and that it has increased surveillance of the area. Japan also confirmed that at least one of the missiles was a suspected ballistic missile.
summary: North Korea fired multiple ballistic missiles off its east coast on Monday, according to South Korea’s military. Seoul said the missiles were launched from Pyongyang and increased surveillance, while Japan confirmed at least one suspected ballistic missile.
author: France 24

title: El Nino drives Pacific sea surface temperature record of 29.70°C in September
content:
An intensifying El Nino pushed sea surface temperatures in a key Pacific monitoring region to a record 29.70 °C in September, the EU’s Copernicus climate service said Monday.

Forecasters expect the weather pattern, which raises drought and flood risks and exacerbates global warming, to become the strongest ever recorded this year.
summary: An intensifying El Nino raised sea surface temperatures in a key Pacific monitoring region to a record 29.70 °C in September, according to the EU’s Copernicus climate service. Forecasters expect the weather pattern to become the strongest ever recorded this year, raising drought and flood risks and exacerbating global warming.
author: France 24

title: Iran says US reply inadequate as Riyadh airport hit again
content:
Iran’s foreign ministry said the United States had accepted some of Tehran’s peace proposals but described the American response as “inadequate,” while a second strike hit Riyadh’s airport.  

The ministry’s statement came as reports confirmed that the airport in Saudi Arabia’s capital was hit again, adding to the series of attacks linked to the ongoing regional conflict.  

Iran emphasized that, although the United States had taken up part of its terms, the reply fell short of what Tehran considers acceptable.
summary: Iran says the US has accepted some of its peace terms but called the reply inadequate. Riyadh airport was hit again.
author: Al Jazeera

title: King Felipe VI visits Ceuta and Melilla, highlighting Spain-Morocco territorial dispute
content:
Felipe VI made his first royal trip to the Spanish enclaves of Ceuta and Melilla, a visit that has revived Spain’s long‑standing territorial dispute with Morocco.  

The king’s arrival underscores the contested status of Ceuta, also known by its Arabic name Sebta, and the neighboring city of Melilla, both of which are claimed by Morocco but remain under Spanish administration.
summary: King Felipe VI made his first visit to the Spanish cities of Ceuta and Melilla. The trip renewed attention on the territorial dispute between Spain and Morocco.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Hurricane Isaias devastates US Gulf Coast, sparks massive cleanup in Florida, Alabama
content:
Hurricane Isaias has left a trail of destruction across the U.S. Gulf Coast, plunging hundreds of thousands of residents into darkness.

Crews are rallying for a massive cleanup effort in Florida and Alabama as the storm’s impact forces extensive recovery work in the two states.
summary: Crews rally for a massive cleanup effort in Florida and Alabama. Isaias leaves hundreds of thousands in the dark across the Gulf Coast.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Iran's foreign minister offers to mediate Saudi-Houthi talks after strikes
content:
Iran’s foreign minister called Saudi Arabia’s foreign minister to urge diplomatic solutions during a recent conversation between the two officials.  

Tehran said it was ready to help arrange talks between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthi movement after a series of deadly strikes hit the kingdom. The offer aims to open a diplomatic channel following the attacks.
summary: Iran's foreign minister urged diplomacy during a call with his Saudi counterpart. Tehran offered to facilitate talks between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis after deadly strikes on the kingdom.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UK PM Andy Burnham says Russia interfered in 2016 Brexit vote
content:
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said it is “clear” that Russia interfered in the 2016 vote to leave the European Union.  

Burnham’s statement marks the first occasion a British prime minister has publicly acknowledged Russian interference in the Brexit referendum.
summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said it is clear that Russia interfered in the 2016 Brexit vote. The claim marks the first time a UK prime minister has publicly acknowledged Russian interference in the vote to leave the EU.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Bridge washed away by flash floods on Nepal's Budhi Gandaki River
content:
Flash floods along Nepal’s Budhi Gandaki River have washed away a bridge, as reported in recent observations of the torrent’s impact. The surge of water also swept away homes in the affected area.

Residents were forced to flee to higher ground as the river’s floodwaters continued to damage infrastructure and displace families.
summary: Flash floods along Nepal’s Budhi Gandaki River swept away homes and bridges. Residents fled to higher ground.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Kimi Antonelli says he can taste F1 glory after Singapore GP podium
content:
Kimi Antonelli said he can finally dare to dream of a Formula One world championship after finishing third at the Singapore Grand Prix. Max Verstappen led the race at Marina Bay from start to finish and won with a dominant drive.

Antonelli’s podium puts him in a position to become F1’s youngest champion at the age of 20 if he wins the next round in Austin. He leads Mercedes teammate George Russell by 102 points and Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton by 111 points.

With six meetings remaining and 25 points for each race winner, Antonelli will take the title if he wins in Austin and Russell finishes ninth or lower while Hamilton finishes fifth or lower.
summary: Kimi Antonelli finished third at the Singapore Grand Prix, and if he wins the next race in Austin and his rivals finish below set positions, he could secure the Formula One title and become the youngest champion at 20. Antonelli leads teammate George Russell by 102 points and Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton by 111, while Max Verstappen won the Singapore race from start to finish.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Maresca hails City after 3-0 Anfield win
content:
Manchester City secured a 3‑0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield, their first match since the club was found guilty on 114 charges relating to Premier League financial rules. Enzo Maresca praised the side for “making their own noise” and said, “You cannot imagine how happy I am … I’m here to win.” The win came as City brushed aside the controversy and threats surrounding the club.

The result kept City’s unbeaten start to the season intact, with goals from Erling Haaland, Jérémy Doku and Rayan Cherki. It marked a sixth successive league win for the team and preserved their position at the top of the Premier League table.

With the victory, Maresca equalled the best start to a managerial reign in Premier League history, maintaining the club’s 100 % record in the league to date.
summary: Manchester City beat Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield, maintaining a perfect start to the season with goals from Erling Haaland, Jérémy Doku and Rayan Cherki. Enzo Maresca praised the team for “making their own noise” amid controversy and threats surrounding the club.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Aston Villa eye Real Madrid striker Endrick in transfer talks
content:
Aston Villa are reportedly exploring a move for Real Madrid striker Endrick, according to Monday’s football gossip.

Liverpool are also weighing up a potential transfer for Barcelona’s Marc Bernal, while Everton are leading the chase for Rennes striker Esteban Lepaul.
summary: Aston Villa are looking at signing Real Madrid striker Endrick. Liverpool are weighing up a move for Barcelona's Marc Bernal, while Everton are leading the chase for Rennes striker Esteban Lepaul.
author: BBC Sport

title: Man City’s 3-0 win over Liverpool leaves Premier League in limbo amid points deduction
content:
On Match of the Day, former Manchester City defenders Toby Alderweireld and former England striker Wayne Rooney explained why the club’s 3‑0 win over Liverpool has left the Premier League in a state of uncertainty.  

They said the victory has intensified the debate around City’s pending disciplinary review, as the club awaits a possible punishment that could include a points deduction. The club was found guilty of financial breaches, which is the basis for the potential sanction.  

Manchester City remains in limbo while the Premier League considers the outcome of the punishment.
summary: Toby Alderweireld and Wayne Rooney said Manchester City's 3-0 win over Liverpool leaves the Premier League in limbo. The club awaits a potential punishment, which could include a points deduction, after being found guilty of financial breaches.
author: BBC Sport

title: Manchester City record statement win at Liverpool, but its weight questioned
content:
Manchester City secured what they consider a statement win at Liverpool, but the result may feel inconsequential amid a Premier League season in limbo, Phil McNulty has said.

McNulty questions whether the victory carries any weight, given the uncertainty surrounding the league’s current status.
summary: Manchester City recorded a statement win at Liverpool. Phil McNulty asks whether the win carries weight during a Premier League season in limbo.
author: BBC Sport

title: El-Sayed Addresses Past Obama Criticism, Affirms Democrats Stand on Giants' Shoulders
content:
On Sunday, Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El‑Sayed (D) addressed past criticism he had made about former President Barack Obama. He said that he and other Democratic candidates “stand on the shoulders of giants” like the former president.

During the interview, “Meet the Press” host Kristen Welker of NBC News asked El‑Sayed about his earlier remarks on Obama.
summary: Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed (D) addressed past criticism he made about former President Obama. He said he and other Democratic candidates 'stand on the shoulders of giants' like the former president.
author: The Hill

title: Tillis Criticizes Trump’s Russia Deal for Tarnishing Lindsey Graham’s Sanctions Efforts
content:
Sen. Thom Tillis (R‑NC) criticized President Trump’s recent diesel deal with Russia on Sunday, citing the United States’ ongoing energy struggles. Tillis said the agreement, which involves pursuing Russian oil, was undermining efforts to enforce sanctions.

In his remarks, Tillis urged the president to move forward with the sanctions bill that the Senate had sent him. He added that the Russia deal was “essentially, I think, tarnishing Sen. Lindsey Graham’s (R‑SC) efforts to try and get…” (statement cut short).
summary: Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N. C.) criticized President Trump’s diesel deal with Russia, saying it undermines the sanctions bill he sent the president. He said the agreement tarnishes Sen. Lindsey Graham’s (R-S. C.) efforts to advance sanctions.
author: The Hill

title: North Carolina Democrats gain momentum in Senate race
content:
Democrats have the wind at their backs in North Carolina, especially in the upcoming Senate race. Former Governor Roy Cooper, a Democrat, is challenging Republican political operative Michael Whatley to replace retiring Senator Thom Tillis (R‑NC).  

Polling, nonpartisan ratings, and recent campaign shifts suggest that Cooper is poised to win the seat. The contest is seen as a key battleground for control of the U.S. Senate.
summary: Former Gov. Roy Cooper, a Democrat, is running for Senate against Republican Michael Whatley to replace retiring Sen. Thom Tillis. Polls, ratings, and campaign shifts suggest Cooper is poised to win.
author: The Hill

title: Texas Democratic Party Chair Confident in Talarico’s Campaign After Flu Recovery
content:
The chair of the Texas Democratic Party, Kendall Scudder, said Sunday that he is confident in the campaign of Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico after the candidate’s recent flu recovery.  

Scudder told reporters, “We’re full steam ahead. And, of course, you’re going to see people in the swamps of the internet making up conspiracy theories. That’s what they always do.”  

The statement was made in the context of Talarico’s return to campaigning following his illness.
summary: Kendall Scudder, chair of the Texas Democratic Party, said he is confident in Democratic senate candidate James Talarico’s campaign after Talarico’s illness. Scudder warned that conspiracy theories would arise on the internet.
author: The Hill

title: FTC says $15.8 million to be sent to cash‑advance app users in over 2 million payments
content:
The Federal Trade Commission says it is distributing $15.8 million to users of a cash‑advance app.  

According to the agency, the disbursement will be made through more than 2 million individual payments.  

The FTC provided the figures in its recent announcement.
summary: The FTC announced that $15.8 million will be sent to users of a cash‑advance app. The payments will total more than 2 million individual transactions.
author: The Hill

title: Seven Senate Foreign Relations lawmakers condemn Trump's Russian oil sanctions deal
content:
A bipartisan group of seven lawmakers from the Senate Foreign Relations Committee issued a statement condemning President Trump’s recent agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The deal would lift sanctions on Russia and allow its oil to enter the global economy.

The lawmakers argued that Congress explicitly banned Russian energy imports in 2022 to prevent American dollars from financing Putin’s actions.
summary: Seven bipartisan members of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee condemned President Trump's agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin that would lift sanctions and allow Russian oil into the global economy. They cited that Congress had banned Russian energy imports in 2022 to prevent American dollars from financing Putin.
author: The Hill

title: Reform would suspend asylum system for parliamentary term if in government
content:
A proposed reform would suspend the asylum system for the duration of a parliamentary term if the proposing party enters government. Under this plan, all new asylum applications would be rejected, and existing applications would be voided.

Consequently, all claimants would be marked for deportation.
summary: All asylum applications would be rejected and existing ones voided, with all claimants marked for deportation.
author: BBC Politics

title: Blood proteins may reveal gut health clues in celiac disease
content:
Blood proteins may offer new clues to gut health in celiac disease

New research suggests that blood proteins could help illuminate gut health in people with celiac disease. Celiac disease is an autoimmune condition in which the immune system reacts adversely to gluten. Eating gluten triggers inflammation in the gut, which can damage the intestine and impair its ability to absorb nutrients.
summary: Celiac disease is an autoimmune condition where the immune system reacts adversely to gluten. Eating gluten causes gut inflammation that damages the intestine and impairs nutrient absorption.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Swedish study casts doubt on folic acid's role in reducing suicide risk
content:
Recent research has suggested that folic acid (vitamin B9) supplementation may reduce the risk of suicide attempts.  

A nationwide Swedish study, presented at the European College of Neuropsychopharmacology (ECNP) annual congress, challenges this view. The study indicates that folic acid appears to affect different sexes and age groups differently, raising doubts about its overall benefit in suicide prevention.
summary: Recent research suggests folic acid supplementation may reduce suicide attempts. A nationwide Swedish study presented at the ECNP annual congress questions this benefit, noting that folic acid effects differ by sex and age.
author: Medical Xpress

title: LSD microdosing may boost sustained attention in women, not in men
content: A pilot study presented at the European College of Neuropsychopharmacology (ECNP) annual congress in Munich found that low doses of LSD may improve sustained attention in women but not in men. The researchers reported that the effects were gender‑specific, with women showing potential gains in sustained attention while men showed no such improvement. The findings are preliminary and were shared at the congress, adding to growing evidence that individuals may respond differently to psychedelic microdosing.
summary: A pilot study indicates low doses of LSD may improve sustained attention in women but not in men. The results were presented at the ECNP annual congress in Munich and are preliminary.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Very severe long COVID linked to distinct mouth and lung microbiome differences
content:
A study of more than 700 people with long COVID, published in the European Respiratory Journal, found that the mix of bacteria in their mouths and lungs differs from that of people without the condition.  

The research shows that these distinct bacterial communities in the lung microbiome are associated with the respiratory symptoms that patients experience. It also links the microbiome differences to the cognitive and digestive problems that are commonly reported in long COVID.
summary: A study of more than 700 people found that patients with very severe long COVID have distinct differences in the bacteria that live in their mouths and lungs. These differences in the lung microbiome are associated with respiratory symptoms as well as the cognitive and digestive problems known to occur in long COVID.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Roofing Scammers Convince Homeowners to Pay for Unfinished or Poor Work
content:
Roofing scammers are reportedly defrauding homeowners, with Citizens Advice reporting that one in ten scams involve fraudsters charging for work not done or done badly.  

The scams target homeowners who are charged thousands of pounds for roofing work that is never performed or is performed poorly.
summary: Roofing scammers are convincing homeowners to pay for work that is not done or is done poorly. One in ten scams reported to Citizens Advice involve fraudsters charging for work not done or done badly.
author: BBC Business

title: Debt advice may increase your debt as credit card payments slip
content:
People are increasingly falling behind on credit card repayments, according to the article. The piece highlights the growing challenge of keeping up with credit card debt.

In response, it offers readers the best way to get debt advice, aiming to help those struggling to manage their repayments.
summary: People are falling behind on credit card repayments. The article provides the best way to obtain debt advice.
author: BBC Business

title: Trump faces bipartisan criticism for plan to import Russian diesel
content:
Trump faces growing backlash over plans to import diesel from Russia.  

Both Republican and Democratic lawmakers have criticised the deal, which was announced weeks before the US midterm elections.  

The criticism came from lawmakers on both sides of the aisle.
summary: Trump’s plan to import diesel from Russia has drawn growing backlash. Republican and Democratic lawmakers have criticised the deal, which was announced weeks before the US midterm elections.
author: BBC Business

title: Institute for Fiscal Studies warns Iran war threatens Healey's budget plans
content:
The Institute for Fiscal Studies has warned that the Iran war could jeopardise the government’s spending plans.  The think tank said the conflict poses significant risks to the fiscal outlook that underpins Prime Minister Rishi Sunak’s budget proposals.  

These risks threaten the budget plans outlined by Finance Secretary Jeremy Healey, according to the Institute’s assessment.  No further details were provided.
summary: The Institute for Fiscal Studies says the Iran war poses significant risks for the government’s spending plans. The think tank warned that the war could jeopardize Healey's budget plans.
author: BBC Business

title: DNA Typewriter maps cell family tree in developing mouse embryo
content:
Scientists have used a “DNA typewriter” to map the lineage of cells in a developing mouse embryo. The technique allowed researchers to record the relationships among cells from the moment the fertilized egg divided into two cells through to the formation of the body and its organs.

The reconstructed family tree covers a developmental window of 13.5 days, after which the embryo’s major structures were in place. For context, a full mouse gestation lasts 19 to 21 days.
summary: Scientists used a DNA Typewriter to reconstruct the family tree of cells in a developing mouse embryo. The recorded lineage spans the first 13.5 days of development from the initial cell split to organ formation.
author: Phys.org

title: American ranchers face soaring costs while staying loyal to Trump
content:
American ranchers are confronting soaring costs while expressing continued loyalty to President Trump, according to a recent report.  

Many farmers in states that backed the president say they are being hit from all sides, and the crucial midterm elections are only weeks away.
summary: Many farmers in states that backed the president say they are being hit from all sides. They face soaring costs as the crucial midterm elections approach in a few weeks.
author: BBC Science

content:
A remote employee was terminated after she declined her employer’s request to submit 160 webcam photographs each day, according to an article published on Inc.com.

The employee’s refusal to meet the daily photo quota led her employer to fire her, as reported in the headline of the Inc.com story.

Google Data Centers around the world

title: Elgin Community College requests Flock to remove cameras; Flock refuses
content:
Elgin Community College in Illinois sought to end its contract with Flock, a company that provides safety cameras, but the company refused to comply.

In April 2025, the college installed six Flock safety cameras to “enhance the safety and security of students.” By September of that year, administrators raised concerns that Flock was sharing data with Customs and Border Patrol, that camera feeds were not properly secured, and that both law enforcement and Flock employees were abusing access to the data. In October 2025, Elgin’s president, Peggy Heinrich, formally requested that Flock remove its cameras.

Flock rejected the college’s request, stating that it had not violated its contract.
summary: Elgin Community College asked Flock to remove six safety cameras installed in 2025 because the school was concerned that Flock was sharing data with Customs and Border Patrol, that camera feeds were not properly secured, and that both law enforcement and the company's employees were abusing access to the data. Flock refused the request, saying it had not violated its contract, according to President Peggy Heinrich.
author: The Verge

title: Apple Reveals Name and Launch Date for HomeView Smart Home Product
content:
Apple has been the subject of multiple reports over the past couple of years indicating that it was developing a new smart‑home product. Recent information now confirms that the product has been named HomeView and that a launch date has been set.

The naming and scheduling of HomeView suggest Apple is positioning the device as a potential first success in its smart‑home portfolio. The product’s official name and launch timeline have been disclosed, though further details have not been provided.
summary: Apple has named its new smart home product HomeView. The company has also announced a launch date for the product.
author: TechCrunch

title: UK Strengthens Cyber Defences, AI Minister Urges Firms to Boost Safety
content:
The UK will strengthen its cyber defences and urge AI firms to step up safety measures, the government said.  Kanishka Narayan, the AI minister, will speak on the need for greater safeguards in advanced AI systems.

Narayan will argue that Britain cannot rely entirely on technology companies to police their own models.  He will call for the UK to build more of its own AI infrastructure to ensure safer development.

The announcement reflects rising global concern over AI dangers.
summary: Kanishka Narayan, the UK’s AI minister, said Britain cannot rely solely on tech companies to police AI models and called for increased safety efforts from frontier AI developers. He also announced a strengthening of Britain’s cyber defences and urged the country to build more of its own AI infrastructure.
author: Guardian Technology

title: UK PM Andy Burnham warns French and German voters of Russian influence after Brexit
content:
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham warned French and German voters on Sunday that Russian political influence could be a factor in upcoming elections. He made the remarks in an interview with The Rest is Politics podcast, released on Sunday.

Burnham cited what he described as “clear” interference in Britain’s 2016 referendum on European Union membership. Russia has denied any meddling in the Brexit vote, and former British leader Boris Johnson in 2020 also said there was no evidence of interference.
summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham warned French and German voters that Russia could try to influence upcoming elections, citing what he described as clear interference in the 2016 Brexit referendum. He made the remarks in a Sunday interview on The Rest is Politics podcast, noting that Russia has denied meddling and former British leader Boris Johnson said there was no evidence of interference.
author: France 24

title: Slovenia rejects bill expanding parliamentary inquiry powers in referendum
content:
Slovenians rejected a bill that would have expanded parliamentary inquiry powers in a referendum held on Sunday, delivering a setback to nationalist Prime Minister Janez Jansa.

With 99 percent of votes counted, 51 percent of voters opposed the proposal while 49 percent backed it. The opposition has described Jansa’s reform agenda as “authoritarian.”
summary: Slovenians voted against a bill to expand parliamentary inquiry powers in a Sunday referendum. With 99% of votes counted, 51% opposed the proposal and 49% supported it, dealing a blow to nationalist Prime Minister Janez Jansa’s reform agenda.
author: France 24

title: Air strikes kill 72 gold miners in disputed Sudan‑Egypt border area
content:
Air strikes on the Sudan‑Egypt border have killed dozens of gold miners, according to a Sudan‑based rights group.

The group reported that 72 people were killed in a remote, disputed area known for illegal gold mining. No additional details were provided.
summary: Air strikes killed dozens of gold miners on the Sudan‑Egypt border. A Sudan‑based rights group said 72 people were killed in a remote, disputed area known for illegal gold mining.
author: DW World

title: Air strike on Sudan gold mine near Egypt border kills at least 72
content:
A deadly air strike has struck a gold mine near Sudan’s border with Egypt, killing dozens of workers.  

The attack resulted in at least 72 deaths and injured more than 50 people on the site.  

The incident highlights the ongoing risk to civilians in conflict‑affected areas.
summary: An air strike hit a gold mine near Sudan’s border with Egypt. The attack killed at least 72 people and injured more than 50.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UK Greens leader Zack Polanski urges rule changes after party labels Zionism racism
content:
UK Greens leader Zack Polanski is urging the party to amend its internal rules so that leaders have greater control over policy, following the party’s recent vote to declare Zionism a form of racism.  

Polanski’s proposal seeks rule reforms that would increase leadership authority over the party’s policy decisions in the wake of the Zionism vote.
summary: Zack Polanski, the UK Greens leader, is calling for internal rule reforms to give party leaders greater control over policy. He made the appeal after the party voted to declare Zionism as racism.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Construction crews use excavators to block waves hitting California homes
content: Waves crashed into homes along California’s coast as construction crews used excavators to try to block the water from entering the properties. The crews were observed working on the shoreline in an effort to protect the residences from further damage. No additional details on the extent of the damage or response efforts were provided.
summary: Waves were crashing into homes along California's coast. Construction crews were seen using excavators to try to block the waves.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US Homeland Security secretary says livestreamed execution poses no risk
content:
The U.S. Department of Homeland Security secretary said there is no “risk” associated with the decision to livestream the execution of Nidal Hasan.  

The move to broadcast the execution has sparked harsh criticism and warnings that such a livestream could encourage further violence.
summary: The US Homeland Security secretary said there is no risk from the livestreamed execution. The decision to livestream Nidal Hasan's execution has drawn harsh criticism and warnings that it could encourage violence.

title: Pakistani national killed in second Houthi strike on Riyadh airport
content: A Pakistani national was killed in a second Houthi strike on Riyadh’s airport, Saudi authorities reported. The attack also left several people injured, according to officials. This follows an earlier strike on the same airport, marking a repeat of the assault. Saudi authorities confirmed the casualties but provided no further details.
summary: Saudi authorities said a Pakistani national was killed in a second strike on Riyadh's airport. Several people were injured in the attack.

content:
Former President Donald Trump claimed to have brokered an “energy ceasefire,” a proposal that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Kyiv would support.  

Zelensky welcomed the idea, indicating Ukraine’s willingness to back such a truce, while Moscow has not offered any comment on the proposal.

content:
The NFL week five slate featured a wild finish as the Jaguars stunned the Eagles, alongside matchups between the Bears and Packers and the Raiders and Patriots. The live coverage also included a photo retrospective on legendary Bears head coach Mike Ditka and reports of players being ejected following a brawl in London.

title: Manchester City beat Liverpool amid Anfield taunts
content:
Manchester City secured a win at Liverpool after a “cracker” from Cherki capped the match, even as Anfield supporters continued to taunt the visitors.  

The atmosphere at Anfield was dominated by a persistent soundtrack from the Liverpool fans, first ringing out before kick‑off and then punctuating the game at regular intervals. City’s victory came amid a backdrop of new reality for the club, shaped by the guilty verdicts handed to them by an independent commission on virtually all of the 115 charges they have faced for breaking Premier League financial rules. City maintain their innocence and have appealed.  

The match ended with Manchester City victorious over Liverpool.
summary: Manchester City defeated Liverpool at Anfield, with the crowd taunting the visitors. City maintain innocence over financial rule breaches and have appealed.

title: Harry Benjamin rates drivers after Singapore Grand Prix
content: Harry Benjamin, the BBC Radio 5 Live Formula 1 commentator, gave his driver ratings for the Singapore Grand Prix. In his assessment, Max Verstappen was described as “perfect,” while Lando Antonelli was called “hugely mature.” Benjamin’s comments were part of his overall review of the drivers’ performances during the race.
summary: BBC Radio 5 Live F1 commentator Harry Benjamin provided driver ratings for the Singapore Grand Prix. He commented on each driver's performance during the race.

title: Hamilton Apologizes to Ferrari After Singapore Strategy Error, Antonelli Nears Title
content:
Lewis Hamilton apologised to Ferrari after a strategy call he made at the Singapore Grand Prix proved incorrect.  

The decision gave Kimi Antonelli a chance to win the world title at the next race in Austin.  

No further details were provided.
summary: Lewis Hamilton apologized to Ferrari after an incorrect strategy call at the Singapore Grand Prix. The mistake allowed Kimi Antonelli to be in position to win the world title at the next race in Austin.

title: Liverpool vs Manchester City Premier League player ratings released
content:
Player ratings were released for the Premier League match between Liverpool and Manchester City. The assessments evaluate each side’s performers following the game.

The ratings highlight a player singled out as needing improvement, echoing the question posed in the headline: “Who ‘simply has to do better’?”
summary: Player ratings for Liverpool and Manchester City were published after their Premier League match. The ratings evaluate each team's individual performances in the game.

title: Manchester City beat 10-man Liverpool 3-0 to extend perfect start
content:
Manchester City secured a comfortable 3-0 victory against Liverpool at Anfield, a match that marked their first appearance since being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules. The win extended City's perfect start to six matches, moving them three points clear at the top of the Premier League.

The match featured a performance by Doku and saw Liverpool reduced to 10 men, contributing to City's cruise to the win.
summary: Manchester City defeated Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield in their first match after being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules. The victory extended City's perfect start to six matches, moving them three points clear at the top of the league.

title: Hamilton Calls Vance’s Religious Attacks ‘Really Sad’ and ‘Pathetic’
content:
Kansas Senate candidate Adam Hamilton (D) responded to Vice President Vance’s criticisms of his religious beliefs on Sunday, describing the attacks as “really sad” and “pathetic.” Hamilton, who is a moderate pastor, made these comments during an interview with ABC’s Jonathan Karl in Kansas.

The exchange occurred after Vance had been vocal about Hamilton’s religious beliefs, a topic he has addressed since prior to the current campaign period.
summary: Kansas Senate candidate Adam Hamilton (D) responded to Vice President Vance's attacks on his religious beliefs, calling them "really sad" and "pathetic." ABC's Jonathan Karl interviewed Hamilton in Kansas and asked him about Vance, who has been outspoken about his religious beliefs.
author: The Hill

title: Zelensky Awaiting U.S. Details on Trump-Announced Energy Ceasefire
content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated on Sunday that Kyiv is awaiting specific details from Washington regarding an energy ceasefire with Russia. This response introduces uncertainty over the agreement, which U.S. President Trump had previously claimed had already taken effect.

Zelensky emphasized that Ukraine supports the ceasefire and noted that it is important for Russia to support it as well. The Ukrainian leader’s comments highlight the current status of negotiations, with Kyiv waiting for further information from the United States to proceed.
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Kyiv is waiting for details from Washington about an energy ceasefire with Russia that President Trump announced. Zelensky stated Ukraine supports the ceasefire and wants Russia to support it as well.
author: The Hill

title: Officials urge U.S. AI policy to protect American data from China
content:
Former officials Juan Caro and Peter Brown contend that U.S. artificial intelligence policy needs to be reformed to safeguard sensitive personal data from foreign adversaries, specifically China. They argue that current approaches risk allowing American data to empower foreign nations rather than protecting domestic interests.

According to the officials, a balanced strategy is required to foster technological innovation while ensuring that Americans' personal information remains secure. They emphasize that AI should ultimately empower Americans, not provide a competitive advantage to China through data access.
summary: Former officials Juan Caro and Peter Brown argue that U.S. AI policy must protect Americans' sensitive personal data from foreign adversaries like China. They assert that this protection is necessary while fostering technological innovation.
author: The Hill

title: Massie backs Trump’s diesel deal with Russia
content:
Rep. Thomas Massie (R‑Ky.) publicly endorsed President Trump’s diesel deal with Russia on Sunday, a rare stance given the two politicians’ prior disagreements.  

Massie, who voted against Russia sanctions in 2022, cited concerns that U.S. citizens would face higher prices. He said he was glad to see Trump “came around to that reality this week” and added that sanctions should be lifted.  

The statement was made on Sunday.
summary: Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) backed President Trump’s diesel deal with Russia on Sunday, despite their past conflict. He had voted against Russia sanctions in 2022, pointing out that U. S. Citizens would suffer from higher prices, and now calls for lifting sanctions.
author: The Hill

title: Russia Hits Kharkiv Power Plant After Trump Announces Energy Ceasefire
content:
President Trump announced on Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an “energy ceasefire,” but Russia subsequently struck a power plant in eastern Ukraine, contradicting the claim. A local official told ABC News that a thermal power plant in Kharkiv was hit twice and is currently on fire.

Ukrainian President Voldoymyr Zelensky confirmed the attack on the facility.
summary: Russia struck a thermal power plant in Kharkiv twice, setting it on fire. Ukrainian President Voldoymyr Zelensky confirmed the attack, which came after President Trump announced an energy ceasefire earlier Sunday.
author: The Hill

title: Backlash grows against Russia diesel deal as Trump claims Ukraine energy ceasefire
content:
Growing backlash emerged on Sunday against President Trump’s agreement with Russia to allow the country’s diesel into the U.S. and global markets. The deal was intended to have Russia immediately release 300,000 tons of diesel to address concerns over rising energy costs due to global fuel shortages.

Prior to the backlash, the president announced an energy ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia.
summary: President Trump’s deal with Russia to permit the country’s diesel into the U. S.

title: Justice Department Investigates TV Networks for Possible Anti-Trust Violations
content: The U.S. Justice Department has launched an investigation into TV networks, citing potential anti-trust violations. This action marks an escalation in the conflict between the Trump administration and the press. The move occurs amid an ongoing court battle involving the administration’s efforts to bar CNN, Politico, and MS NOW from the White House.
summary: The Justice Department is investigating TV networks citing possible anti-trust violations. This action escalates Trump's fight with the press amid a court battle over barring CNN, Politico, and MS NOW from the White House.

title: US Study Maps Childhood Lead Exposure Risk by Neighborhood
content:
Mapping childhood lead exposure risk in the US, neighborhood by neighborhood

No amount of lead exposure is considered safe for children, and even low levels of lead in a child's blood can cause serious health problems and developmental delays.  

However, data on lead exposure are sparse at the neighborhood level in the United States, leaving significant gaps in knowledge about where lead exposure may be occurring.  

These gaps highlight the need for more detailed mapping of lead exposure risk across neighborhoods.
summary: No amount of lead exposure is considered safe for children, even low levels can cause serious health problems and developmental delays. Data on lead exposure are sparse at the neighborhood level in the United States, leaving gaps in knowledge about where exposure may be occurring.
author: Medical Xpress

title: U.S. adults and youth experience high rates of mental illness
content:
Study finds positive parenting teaches children how to experience joy—and could lead to better mental health

More than one in five adults in the U.S. experience mental illness each year, according to data from the National Alliance on Mental Illness. Among young people ages 6–17, over one in seven report a mental health disorder, with 50% of all lifetime mental illness beginning by age 14 and 75% by age 24.
summary: More than one in five adults in the U. S. Experience mental illness each year, according to data from the National Alliance on Mental Illness. More than one in seven young people ages 6–17 experience a mental health disorder, with 50% of all lifetime mental illness beginning by age 14 and 75% by age 24.
author: Medical Xpress

title: South Korean Ship Completes Arctic Route Trial Amid Middle East Conflict
content: South Korea completed a trial of an Arctic shipping route when a South Korean container ship returned on Sunday after a voyage through the Arctic. The ship tested an alternative route that has opened as sea ice melts. The trial was prompted by disruptions to global shipping caused by conflict in the Middle East. The vessel’s return marks the end of the test voyage.
summary: A South Korean container ship returned on Sunday after completing a trial voyage through the Arctic. The voyage tested an alternative shipping route opened by melting sea ice amid disruptions caused by conflict in the Middle East.
author: Phys.org

title: Jurassic fossil shows mammalian milk‑drinking structures evolved 165 million years ago
content:
An international team of researchers has published new evidence in Nature that sheds light on the evolutionary origins of a defining mammalian feature: the ability to suckle and consume milk during infancy.  

The study indicates that key anatomical structures necessary for mammalian suckling, swallowing, and breastfeeding behaviors evolved nearly 165 million years ago, well before the appearance of modern mammals.  

These findings extend the known timeline for the development of mammalian feeding mechanisms.
summary: An international team of researchers published findings in Nature showing that key anatomical structures for mammalian suckling, swallowing, and breastfeeding evolved nearly 165 million years ago. The evidence indicates that the ability to suckle and consume milk during infancy originated long before modern mammals appeared.
author: Phys.org

title: Cyclone Isaias Claims Four Lives in Southeast U.S. as It Moves Northward
content:
At least four people died in the southeastern United States as post‑tropical cyclone Isaias struck the region. The storm, which had made landfall on Florida’s Gulf Coast, moved northward on Saturday, bringing flooding and tornado risks to the area.

Isaias continued to pose significant hazards as it advanced, threatening additional flooding and tornadoes across the southern United States.
summary: Four people died in the southeastern United States as post-tropical cyclone Isaias posed flooding and tornado risks. The cyclone moved northward after making landfall on Florida's Gulf Coast.
author: Phys.org

title: Indonesia Releases Eight Orangutans from Borneo Fires into Protected Forest
content:
Indonesia has released eight orangutans that were rescued from recent fires into a protected forest, Indonesian authorities and rescuers said on Sunday.

The animals had been rescued in recent weeks from blazes that tore through Borneo island. The release marks the final step in their recovery after the fires.

The statement confirmed the release and the involvement of both Indonesian authorities and rescuers.
summary: Eight orangutans rescued from recent Borneo fires have been released into a protected forest. The release was announced by Indonesian authorities and rescuers on Sunday.
author: Phys.org

title: Conservation groups condemn dolphin death after transfer from France to Spanish park
content: Conservation groups on Sunday condemned the death of a dolphin that had been transferred from France to a Spanish marine park, saying the loss adds to recent fatalities among sea mammals moved to Spain from Canada. The groups highlighted the pattern of deaths following the relocation of marine mammals to Spanish facilities.
summary: Conservation groups on Sunday condemned the death of a dolphin transferred from France to a Spanish marine park. They said the incident adds to the deaths of other sea mammals recently moved to Spain from Canada.
author: Phys.org

title: Quantum 'birthmarks' hold lasting traces of a system's past
content: Certain classical physical systems can transition through multiple configurations over time, eventually reaching a state where their long-term behavior no longer reflects their initial conditions. This process, in which the system samples available configurations according to a specific statistical distribution, is known as ergodicity.
summary: Some classical physical systems explore many configurations until their long-term behavior no longer reveals starting conditions. The sampling of available configurations according to the appropriate statistical distribution is a property called ergodicity.
author: Phys.org

content:

content:
A Canadian YouTuber has built a “Flock‑like” camera system that can exclusively track police vehicles. The device, according to a Tom’s Hardware article, prompted police officers to visit the creator’s home to discuss privacy concerns.

title: NASA releases 800GB of Artemis II science data online
content:
NASA has released more than 800 GB of science data, images, and videos from the Artemis II mission on its “Artemis II: Sights & Sounds of Science” website.  

The archive contains over 11,000 photos and videos, more than 8.5 hours of audio, and crew‑annotated images that mark where the crew observed impact flashes on the Moon’s dark side.  

Among the new material is footage of the Artemis II crew describing their observation of impact flashes to the ground team in Houston.  

The collection offers an unprecedented inside view of the historic space mission.
summary: NASA posted more than 800GB of science data, images, and videos from the Artemis II mission on its Sights & Sounds of Science site. The archive contains over 11,000 photos and videos, 8.5 hours of audio, and crew-annotated images marking impact flashes on the dark side of the Moon.
author: The Verge

title: Apple TV Rumors: Built-in Mic and Speaker-Enabled Remote
content:
Apple’s next‑generation Apple TV is rumored to include a built‑in microphone, while its upgraded remote is expected to feature a speaker. The microphone would allow users to control the set‑top box with Siri without speaking into the remote or a connected HomePod device.  

The added voice capability could also enable the Apple TV to act as a simple smart‑home hub, controlling thermostats and locking doors without the need to locate the remote.  

If the remote is misplaced, the integrated speaker is said to play an audio alert to help users find it, whether it has fallen under the couch or been hidden by a child.
summary: The new Apple TV is rumored to include a built-in microphone and a remote equipped with a speaker. The microphone would allow Siri voice control without the remote or HomePod, and the speaker could emit an audio alert to help locate a misplaced remote.
author: The Verge

title: Elon Musk says he'll rename SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI after Trump's AI rebrand push
content:
President Donald Trump announced a plan to rebrand artificial intelligence as “super intelligence,” urging the public to adopt the new terminology.

In response, several leading figures in Silicon Valley have begun to align with the president’s effort. Elon Musk quickly pledged to rename SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI in support of the proposed change.

The move reflects an emerging trend among tech executives to follow Trump’s call for the terminology shift, though broader adoption remains uncertain.
summary: President Donald Trump announced plans to rebrand artificial intelligence as "super intelligence". Elon Musk said he will rename SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI, joining other Silicon Valley leaders who are supporting the rebrand.

title: Prime Video debuts Blade Runner 2099 full trailer at NYCC
content:
Prime Video presented the full trailer for the upcoming series “Blade Runner 2099” during its appearance at New York Comic Con (NYCC).  

In addition, a new trailer was shown for “Godzilla Minus Zero,” identified as the sequel to Takashi Yamazaki’s film “Godzilla Minus One.”
summary: Prime Video unveiled the full trailer for Blade Runner 2099 at NYCC. A new trailer for Godzilla Minus Zero, the sequel to Takashi Yamazaki’s Godzilla Minus One, was also released.

content: On the program Equity, a debate was held about the AI industry’s approach to data center opposition. Participants examined the impact of data‑center moratoriums and questioned whether the industry has a communication problem. The discussion also raised the possibility that removing nondisclosure agreements could help persuade opponents of new data centers. The conversation highlighted these concerns as central to the industry’s outreach strategy.

content:

content:

title: Nepal orders evacuations along Budhi Gandaki River after flash flood
content:
Ne​pal orders evacuations after Budhi Gandaki flash flood

Ne​pal’s authorities ordered residents along the Budhi Gandaki River to evacuate on Sunday, 11 October, after a sudden flash flood swept away homes and other buildings in the country’s mountainous north‑central region.  

The flood, which struck the Budhi Gandaki River corridor, caused significant damage to local structures and prompted immediate evacuation orders from officials.  

The incident highlights the vulnerability of the region’s mountainous communities to rapid water events.
summary: Nepal’s authorities ordered residents along the Budhi Gandaki River to evacuate on Sunday, 11 October. A sudden flash flood swept away homes and other buildings in the north‑central mountainous region.
author: Euronews

title: Zelensky says he was surprised by Trump's Ukraine-Russia energy ceasefire announcement
content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he was surprised by U.S. President Donald Trump’s announcement of a Ukraine‑Russia “energy ceasefire.” Speaking to the digital news outlet Axios on Sunday, Zelensky indicated that he would be willing to accept the ceasefire whenever it begins.

The remarks were reported by Axios correspondent Gulliver Cragg.
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told Axios on Sunday he was surprised by US counterpart Donald Trump's announcement of a Ukraine‑Russia "energy ceasefire." He said he would accept the ceasefire whenever it begins.

title: Saudi‑led coalition says projectile attack on Riyadh airport causes fire
content:
The Saudi‑led coalition in Yemen reported that an “unidentified projectile” struck Riyadh’s international airport on Sunday, igniting a fire. The incident occurred the day after a strike that killed 12.

The projectile caused a blaze at the airport, but no casualties were mentioned. Hours earlier, Iran‑backed Houthis had warned airlines and travellers to stay away from Saudi airports.

David Smith, The Guardian’s Washington bureau chief, reports on the incident.
summary: An unidentified projectile targeted Riyadh's international airport on Sunday, causing a fire, according to the Saudi‑led coalition in Yemen. The incident occurred hours after Iran‑backed Houthis warned airlines and travelers to stay away from Saudi airports.
author: France 24

title: Delhi detains hundreds protesting India election chief; court releases Abhijeet Dipke
content:
Police detained hundreds of protesters in Delhi for a second day on Sunday as sporadic protests broke out demanding that India's election chief quit.

A court ordered the release of “cockroach” movement founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other senior leaders.
summary: Police detained hundreds of protesters in Delhi for a second day as sporadic protests demanded India's election chief quit. A court ordered the release of "cockroach" movement founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other senior leaders.

title: Raphaël Glucksmann wins French left-wing primary with 66% of vote
content: Raphaël Glucksmann has been chosen as the centre‑left candidate for France’s 2027 presidential election after winning the party primary on Sunday. He secured 66.13 % of the vote, a decisive margin that cemented his position as the left’s primary alternative to hard‑left leader Jean‑Luc Mélenchon. The victory positions Glucksmann as the main contender for voters seeking a moderate left‑wing platform in the upcoming election.
summary: Raphaël Glucksmann will be the centre-left candidate for France's 2027 presidential election following a crushing victory on Sunday, with 66.13% of the vote, positioning himself as the left's main alternative to hard-left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon.
author: France 24

title: Hurricane Isaias Leaves 396,000 Without Power in Florida Panhandle and Southern Alabama
content:
As what remained of Hurricane Isaias moved north on Sunday, nearly 396,000 customers in the Florida Panhandle and southern Alabama were left without electricity. The storm’s remnants continued to bring moderate to heavy rainfall across the central Appalachians and the mid‑Atlantic region.

At least four deaths have been linked to the storm, and the National Weather Service warned that flash‑flooding could extend into the Appalachians. Heavy rain may also produce isolated flash floods, strong wind gusts, downed trees and power lines, and scattered outages across the southeastern United States, especially near the southern Appalachians.

Life‑threatening surf and rip‑current conditions were expected to persist along the Gulf and southeastern Atlantic coasts.
summary: Nearly 396,000 customers in the Florida Panhandle and southern Alabama are without power as Hurricane Isaias moves north. The storm also caused at least four deaths and threatens flash flooding, strong winds, and life‑threatening surf along the Gulf and Atlantic coasts.
author: Guardian World

title: Saudi Arabia says Houthis killed 12, injured 300 in King Khalid Inter attack
content: Saudi Arabia has accused Yemen’s Houthi forces of carrying out an attack on Saturday that targeted King Khalid Inter. The Saudi government says the strike resulted in the deaths of 12 people and injured 300 others. The accusations were made public by Saudi officials following the incident.
summary: Saudi Arabia has accused Yemen’s Houthis of killing 12 people in Saturday's attack on King Khalid Inter. The attack also injured 300 people.

content:

content:
Polish police detained a man suspected of planning an assassination of Prime Minister Donald Tusk.  

The arrest came after authorities received credible information about possible attacks targeting Tusk and his defence minister.  

Police acted on the tip to prevent any further threat.

content:

The Yemeni Houthi group said its operations over the weekend killed 13 people in Riyadh and included attacks on two airports and oil facilities.

content:
Blue Origin has moved forward with the rebuild of Launch Complex 36 (LC‑36) in preparation for a New Glenn return to flight by year‑end. The company’s update comes four months after the New Glenn rocket exploded on the launch pad.

The information was reported by NASASpaceFlight.

title: Taylor Knibb Wins Ironman World Title After Løvseth Collapses
content:
American triathlete Taylor Knibb secured her first Hawaiian Ironman world title in a dramatic finish at Kona. With a mile remaining in the race, Norwegian defending champion Solveig Løvseth held a lead of more than a minute over Knibb. Løvseth had established her advantage by taking the lead from Knibb within the final 10 kilometers of the 42.2-kilometer marathon run.

In the final kilometer, Knibb overtook Løvseth, who collapsed while leading the race. This performance marked one of the most dramatic finishes in the event's history for Knibb.

In the men's competition, France’s Vincent Luis claimed the world title during his debut at Kona.
summary: American triathlete Taylor Knibb won her first Hawaiian Ironman world title in Kona. Defending champion Solveig Løvseth collapsed while leading, allowing Knibb to overtake her in the final kilometer.
author: Guardian Sport

title: ‘That’s when I begin to scream’: Mick Fanning on punching a great white shark
content:
Australian surfing champion Mick Fanning recounts his 2015 encounter with a great white shark in an excerpt from his memoir, All Heart. The incident occurred during the final of a world tour event at Jeffreys Bay in South Africa, where Fanning was competing against fellow Australian Julian Wilson. The attack was broadcast live on television.

In the memoir, Fanning describes being locked onto his take-off spot in the lineup, scanning the horizon while assessing his position against the oncoming set. As he moved slightly further inside, he heard a big splash behind him. Glancing over his left shoulder, he caught a glimpse of a huge dark shape in the water, a sight that gripped him with a jolt of fear.
summary: The Australian surfing champion was famously monstered by a great white shark while competing against fellow Aussie Julian Wilson in the 2015 world tour event final at Jeffreys Bay in South Africa. The attack was broadcast live on TV.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Resurgent Verstappen holds off Leclerc to seal dominant F1 Singapore GP win
content:
Max Verstappen secured his second consecutive Formula 1 victory by winning the Singapore Grand Prix at the Marina Bay circuit. The Red Bull driver delivered a commanding performance from pole position to the checkered flag, marking his first win at this venue during his 250th career race. He comfortably finished ahead of Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc, who took second place.

In the championship battle, Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli finished third to extend his lead in the standings. His teammate George Russell recovered from a 19th-place grid start to finish ninth. Other notable results included McLaren’s Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri finishing fourth and fifth, respectively, while Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton placed sixth.
summary: Max Verstappen won the Singapore Grand Prix from pole, his first victory at Marina Bay circuit and his 250th race, with Charles Leclerc second and Kimi Antonelli third. Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri finished fourth and fifth for McLaren, Lewis Hamilton sixth for Ferrari, and George Russell finished ninth after starting 19th.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Southampton 1-0 Portsmouth in Premier League match
content:

title: Vanderbilt researchers uncover longevity secret in 194‑year‑old tortoise Jonathan
content:
A team of researchers from Vanderbilt Health, led by a neurologist and specialists in advanced genomics, has uncovered a key factor contributing to extreme longevity by studying a 194‑year‑old giant tortoise named Jonathan.  

The international collaboration focused on extracting biological clues from Jonathan, whose age makes him one of the oldest living animals. By analyzing his genetic material, the team identified a component that may explain how he has maintained health for nearly two centuries.  

The findings highlight the potential of genomics research in understanding longevity and may guide future studies on aging in humans and other species.
summary: An international collaboration led by a neurologist and genomics experts at Vanderbilt Health has coaxed one of the secrets of extreme longevity from Jonathan, a 194‑year‑old giant tortoise. Jonathan may hold the secret to a long, healthy life.

title: LLM-inspired study reveals how brain cells encode word meanings
content:
A new LLM‑inspired study sheds light on how brain cells encode the meaning of words.  

The research underscores that understanding how the human brain processes and represents spoken language remains an important goal for neuroscientists.  

It highlights that grasping spoken words involves more than simply recognizing sounds; the brain must also decipher the meaning of words and how those meanings change with context.
summary: The study examines how the brain processes and represents spoken language. It shows that understanding spoken words requires deciphering word meanings and how those meanings shift with context.

title: Managing high blood pressure could prevent >500K CVD deaths annually in 20 countries
content:
Managing high blood pressure could prevent more than 518,000 annual deaths from cardiovascular disease worldwide, according to preliminary research presented at the American Heart Association’s Hypertension Scientific Sessions 2026. The title of the report notes that the potential benefit applies to over 500,000 deaths annually in 20 countries.

The research was presented at the AHA meeting held in Arlington, Virginia, from Oct. 7–11, 2026. The conference focuses on recent advances in basic and clinical research on high blood pressure and its relationship to cardiac and kidney disease, stroke, obesity, and genetics.

The findings underscore the global impact of hypertension and the importance of effective management strategies to reduce cardiovascular mortality.
summary: Effective management of high blood pressure could prevent more than 518,000 cardiovascular deaths each year, according to preliminary research. The findings were presented at the American Heart Association's Hypertension Scientific Sessions 2026 in Arlington, Virginia, Oct. 7–11, which highlighted recent advances in basic and clinical research on high blood pressure and its links to cardiac, kidney, stroke, obesity and genetics.

title: Republicans revive Reagan-era tax‑cut promise with AI‑driven growth claims
content:
US’s Reagan‑era economic promises return as Trump’s AI‑fueled growth fantasy

Republicans have revived the Reagan‑era claim that tax cuts would pay for themselves by spurring economic growth and filling the government’s coffers. The article notes that this promise has historically failed, with tax cuts since the Gipper’s day on increasing the budget deficit.

The current iteration of the promise is wrapped in artificial intelligence. A quoted statement—“Even if AI supercharged the economy, its impact on the government’s finances would be muted”—suggests that the AI‑fueled growth fantasy is unlikely to change the outcome.

The article concludes that the promise is expected to fail again.
summary: Republicans have repeatedly claimed that tax cuts will pay for themselves by spurring growth and filling the government’s coffers, a promise dating back to Ronald Reagan’s era. The piece notes the promise has never succeeded, has added to the budget deficit, and is now being revived with artificial‑intelligence rhetoric, which it says will fail again.

title: Chinese researchers use spinach nanoparticles to aid failing rat hearts
content:
Researchers in China have created spinach‑derived nanoparticles that incorporate part of a leaf’s photosynthetic machinery and introduced them into rat heart cells. The aim was to determine whether “borrowed” photosynthesis could supply chemical energy to an overworked heart.

The experiment leveraged the natural ability of spinach leaves to convert light into chemical energy, a capability that failing heart tissue lacks. By delivering the plant components to the cardiac cells, the scientists tested whether the added photosynthetic function could assist the struggling hearts.
summary: A spinach leaf can turn light into chemical energy, while a struggling heart cannot. Researchers in China introduced part of the leaf’s energy‑making machinery into rat heart cells to test whether borrowed photosynthesis could help an overworked heart.

title: NYU Abu Dhabi researchers develop algorithm to forecast Arctic sea ice nine months ahead
content:
Researchers at the Mubadala Arabian Center for Climate and Environmental Sciences (ACCESS) at NYU Abu Dhabi have created an algorithm that can forecast Arctic sea‑ice extent up to nine months in advance. The new tool provides a way to anticipate changes in the Arctic that may influence the global climate system.

The findings were published in the journal Scientific Reports.
summary: Researchers at the Mubadala Arabian Center for Climate and Environmental Sciences (ACCESS) at NYU Abu Dhabi have developed a new algorithm that can forecast Arctic sea ice extent up to nine months in advance. The research was published in the journal Scientific Reports.

title: Los Angeles faces worst mosquito season as heatwaves and El Niño boost West Nile cases
content:
Heat and humidity have produced one of the worst mosquito seasons in recent history, with West Nile virus cases reaching a decade high. Los Angeles, traditionally known for its blue skies and beaches, has been identified as the most mosquito‑infested city in the United States for several years.

This year’s conditions have been especially severe, driven by a series of heatwaves and an extra‑powerful El Niño. Residents describe the season as a “living hell,” noting clouds of mosquitoes swarming backyards and forcing diners on open‑air patios to scratch their ankles.

The surge in mosquito activity and associated health risks underscore the impact of the extreme weather patterns on the city’s public health.
summary: Heat and humidity have produced one of the worst mosquito years in recent history, with West Nile virus at a decade high. Los Angeles, now the most mosquito‑infested city in America, has seen swarms intensified by heatwaves and an extra‑powerful El Niño, leading locals to call the summer a “living hell.”

content:

title: LeapPad's rise and fall explored on Version History podcast
content:
Why the LeapPad couldn’t survive the iPad

The LeapPad, a smart book that played sounds, responded to taps, and helped children learn to read, was the hottest toy in the United States for multiple years. Its interactive features made it a popular choice among parents, though its high price and unexpected parenting questions added complexity to its appeal.

In a recent episode of Version History, David Pierce joined The Verge’s Andru Marino and Jennifer Pattison Tuohy to explain how the LeapPad worked, why it was so enticing to both kids and adults, and why the company that made it could never quite follow it. The episode is part of the fifth season of Version History, which is almost finished. The full story is available on The Verge.
summary: The LeapPad was a smart book that played sounds, responded to taps, and helped children learn to read, becoming a popular U.S. toy despite its high price. In a Version History episode, David Pierce, The Verge's Andru Marino, and Jennifer Pattison Tuohy discuss how the device worked, its appeal, and why its maker could not sustain it after the iPad.

title: Resident Evil Requiem sells 8 million copies, 14th best‑selling Capcom game
content:

Resident Evil, a survival‑horror franchise that has existed for 30 years, saw its latest installment, Resident Evil Requiem, sell 8 million copies since its February launch, making it the 14th best‑selling game in Capcom’s history. At the same time, a reboot of the Resident Evil film series is being developed by Weapons director Zach Cre.  

The Stepback, a weekly newsletter that breaks down a single tech‑industry story, arrives in subscribers’ inboxes on Sundays at 8 a.m. ET. Readers can follow Andrew Webster for additional coverage of horror’s growing influence and opt in to receive the newsletter.  

The full story was published on The Verge.
summary: Resident Evil has been around for 30 years and its latest game, Resident Evil Requiem, has sold 8 million copies since its February launch. The sales make it the 14th best‑selling game ever released by Capcom.

content:

title: Startup Vurt aims to make vertical videos a TV genre
content:
A new startup called Vurt is positioning vertical video as its own genre, aiming to move the format from smartphones to widescreen televisions. The company argues that while major streaming services such as Disney Plus and HBO Max are experimenting with vertical content to counter the rise of video‑focused social platforms like TikTok and Instagram, most existing vertical series platforms remain focused on mobile viewing.

Vurt’s approach differs by targeting TV screens, seeking to evolve vertical micro‑dramas and series beyond the small‑screen experience that dominates current offerings. The startup’s strategy reflects an industry‑wide “arms race” for viewers’ attention as streaming services grapple with the perceived threat from social media video formats.
summary: Vurt says vertical videos should be treated as a distinct genre. Unlike other vertical micro‑drama platforms that focus on mobile, Vurt plans to deliver vertical series on widescreen televisions.

content:

content:
At least 139 migrants died when a boat capsized off Djibouti, the United Nations said. The UN’s International Organization for Migration (IOM) confirmed the death toll in the incident.

The IOM notes that tens of thousands of migrants travel from the Horn of Africa through Djibouti each year, seeking to cross the Bab el‑Mandeb Strait to Yemen and ultimately reach Gulf countries.
