title: Trump calls Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El‑Sayed “terrible” on Truth Social
content:
President Donald Trump criticized Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed on Wednesday, labeling him a “terrible candidate” in the midst of a closely contested race against former Representative Mike Rogers. The progressive Democrat is competing in the Wolverine State, where the election has drawn significant attention.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump referred to El-Sayed as “Mohammed El-Sayed” and described him as a “terrible Candidate for the Dumocrats,” using his characteristic nickname for the Democratic Party. The candidate’s full name is Abdulrahman Mohamed.
summary: President Trump called Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El‑Sayed (D) a terrible candidate on Truth Social. The progressive candidate, whose full name is Abdulrahman Mohamed, is running against former Rep. Mike Rogers (R) in a closely contested race in Michigan.
author: The Hill

title: Trump media ban lawsuit returns to D.C. court; WH science summit honors Musk, Huang
content:
A lawsuit filed by CNN, MS NOW, and Politico against the Trump administration’s ban on these media outlets from White House grounds is set to return to D.C. Federal Court on Thursday morning. The legal action follows a judge’s ruling two weeks ago that determined the outlets should be permitted access to the complex for pool duties.

Despite the court order, the president has routinely blocked the media organizations. On Wednesday, Trump addressed the situation, though specific details of his remarks were not included in the provided text.
summary: CNN, MS NOW, and Politico's lawsuit against the Trump administration's media ban returns to D.C. Federal court on Thursday. The White House science summit includes awards for Musk and Huang.
author: The Hill

title: Survey: 30% of Trump voters very enthusiastic about midterms
content: A new Reuters/Ipsos survey released Thursday indicates that fewer voters who supported President Trump in 2024 than those who voted for Vice President Kamala Harris report being “very enthusiastic” about casting ballots in November. The polling found that 30 percent of Trump voters expressed this level of enthusiasm for voting in the midterms.
summary: A new Reuters/Ipsos survey found that 30 percent of Trump voters are very enthusiastic about casting ballots in the midterms. This figure is lower than the percentage of voters who backed Vice President Kamala Harris in 2024 who expressed similar enthusiasm.
author: The Hill

title: Bessent criticizes Wall Street Journal report on Treasury department strife
content:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized The Wall Street Journal on Wednesday following a report detailing strife within his department. In response to the article, Bessent stated, “Look, the Wall Street Journal is a shadow of its former self, and I think it’s a disgrace for you to say that they’re like TMZ.”

Bessent added that he believes the publication has declined in quality, contrasting it with TMZ, which he noted “does a good job of what they do.”
summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized The Wall Street Journal for a report regarding tensions and turnover within his department. He described the newspaper as a shadow of its former self and a disgrace.
author: The Hill

title: Alex Gibney's 'Musk' documents expose tech billionaire's rise
content: A collection of documents and interviews with individuals close to tech billionaire Elon Musk has revealed a critical perspective on his ascent to become one of the world’s wealthiest and most influential figures. The material provides a detailed account of his rise in power and wealth.
summary: A collection of documents and interviews with individuals close to Elon Musk reveals a critical picture of his ascent. The material highlights his growth into one of the world's richest and most powerful men.
author: NPR Politics

title: Crypto regulator staffing and enforcement drop as new market rules are drafted
content: The regulatory agency responsible for overseeing crypto and prediction markets has experienced a significant reduction in staffing and enforcement actions. This decline has occurred during the second Trump administration, a period when the agency is simultaneously tasked with developing new regulations for these expanding sectors.
summary: The agency is tasked with creating new rules for crypto and prediction markets while its staffing and enforcement actions have declined sharply. These reductions in resources have occurred during the second Trump administration.
author: NPR Politics

title: NPR: 60 tight House districts key to 2026 control
content: An NPR analysis indicates that both political parties are investing significant resources in approximately 60 House districts that may determine control of the chamber in the 2026 elections. These specific districts are characterized by the fact that Donald Trump won them by an average margin of nine points in the 2024 election.
summary: An NPR analysis identifies roughly 60 House districts as critical to deciding control of the chamber. Both parties are spending heavily in these districts, where Trump won by an average of nine points in 2024.
author: NPR Politics

title: ICE Quietly Used North New Jersey Warehouse as Detention Facility All Summer
content:
Residents in North New Jersey have reported rumors circulating throughout the summer that Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has been using a local warehouse as a detention facility. The reports suggest the agency has been operating the site quietly.

NPR has investigated these claims to determine the extent of the warehouse's use as a detention center.
summary: Neighbors in North New Jersey say rumors have circulated throughout the summer that ICE has been using a warehouse as a detention center. NPR investigated these claims regarding the facility's quiet operation.
author: NPR Politics

title: Premier League clubs worry about political interference in Man City appeal
content:
Premier League clubs have expressed concern over potential political interference in Manchester City’s appeal following comments made by Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

The clubs say they are worried that the Prime Minister’s remarks could influence the outcome of the appeal, raising questions about the independence of the decision‑making process.
summary: Premier League clubs are concerned about political interference in Manchester City's appeal. The concerns stem from comments made by Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
author: BBC Politics

title: COP31 President Murat Kurum says 1.5°C limit vital for Pacific after Tuvalu visit
content:
Pre-COP events have drawn renewed focus on the climate crisis facing the Pacific, with COP31 President Murat Kurum visiting Tuvalu’s shrinking land.  

During the visit, Kurum stressed that the global 1.5 °C warming limit is “a matter of survival” for Pacific nations.  

The story was first published by Climate Home News.
summary: COP31 President Murat Kurum visited Tuvalu’s shrinking land. He said the global 1.5°C warming limit is a matter of survival for the Pacific.
author: Climate Home News

title: July 2026 Wildfires Hit Record 624 Incidents in England, Including Sizewell B Blaze
content:
July 2026 was the worst month on record for wildfires in England, provisional data shows. The summer’s record‑setting fire activity highlights a clear upward trend in the total number of wildfires recorded across the country.

A devastating blaze near the Sizewell B nuclear power station in Suffolk was one of 624 wildfires that occurred in July. The high number of incidents underscores the severity of the month’s fire outbreak.

The summer’s hot and dry weather turned large parts of the countryside into a tinderbox, a stark reminder of the United Kingdom’s vulnerability to climate breakdown.
summary: England recorded a record 624 wildfires in July 2026, the worst month on record. A devastating blaze near the Sizewell B nuclear power station in Suffolk was among the incidents.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Chicago woman turns home into monarch butterfly sanctuary
content:
Claudia Galeno‑Sánchez has turned her family home in Chicago’s Pilsen neighborhood into a sanctuary for monarch butterflies. She has planted native milkweed and wildflowers to support the insects during their fall migration.

The brightly colored house, painted with the help of neighbors, her two children, and muralist Héctor Duarte, also serves as an educational space where Galeno‑Sánchez shares her experience with visitors.

Her efforts provide a local refuge for monarchs and a learning opportunity for the community.
summary: Claudia Galeno‑Sánchez has transformed her family home in Chicago’s Pilsen neighborhood into a monarch butterfly sanctuary by planting native milkweed and wildflowers. She painted the house with the help of neighbors, her children, and muralist Héctor Duarte.
author: Guardian Environment

title: AI Search Tools Fail to Consistently Identify Validated Home Blood Pressure Monitors
content:
Preliminary research presented at the American Heart Association’s Hypertension Scientific Sessions 2026 in Arlington, Virginia, found that three of four leading artificial intelligence (AI) search tools accurately identified home blood pressure monitors that met validated clinical standards only 63 – 83 % of the time.

The study was presented at the conference held Oct. 7–11.
summary: Three of four leading artificial intelligence (AI) search tools accurately identified home blood pressure monitors that met validated clinical standards only 63–83% of the time. The preliminary research was presented at the American Heart Association's Hypertension Scientific Sessions 2026 in Arlington, Virginia, Oct. 7–11.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Potassium-rich DASH diet safe for adults on blood pressure meds
content: A preliminary study presented at the American Heart Association’s Hypertension Scientific Sessions 2026 in Arlington, Virginia, found that increased consumption of potassium‑rich foods from the DASH diet does not raise blood potassium to dangerous levels in adults taking medications to lower blood pressure. The research was discussed during the conference held from Oct. 7–11.
summary: Preliminary research presented at the American Heart Association's Hypertension Scientific Sessions 2026 found that potassium-rich DASH diet foods did not raise blood potassium levels to dangerous levels in adults taking blood pressure medications. The study was presented in Arlington, Virginia, from Oct. 7–11.
author: Medical Xpress

title: FDA-Cleared Urine Test Delivers Hours-Long Results for Invasive Aspergillosis
content:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has cleared a new urine test that can deliver results for invasive aspergillosis within hours.  

Investigators at Johns Hopkins Medicine, whose work has been supported by the National Institutes of Health, have advanced understanding of ways to better detect the infection.  

Invasive aspergillosis is caused by mold. The infection is uncommon in the general population but can pose significant health risks for people with underlying conditions that affect or weaken their immune systems.
summary: The FDA-cleared urine test provides results for invasive aspergillosis within hours. Researchers at Johns Hopkins Medicine, supported by the National Institutes of Health, have advanced detection methods for the mold-caused infection.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Longer Sleep Linked to Higher Risk of Kidney Disease in Type 2 Diabetes
content:
A recent study published in the Journal of the Endocrine Society suggests that people with type 2 diabetes who sleep longer may face an increased risk of developing or worsening diabetic kidney disease.

The research highlights a potential link between extended sleep duration and the progression of kidney complications in individuals with type 2 diabetes.
summary: People with type 2 diabetes who sleep longer may have an increased risk of developing or worsening diabetic kidney disease. The study was published in the Journal of the Endocrine Society.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Australians with Diabetes Show Remarkable Strengths
content:
From 'what's wrong?' to 'what's strong': Exploring the personal strengths of people living with diabetes

More than 1.5 million Australians live with diabetes—a relentless, demanding condition with day‑to‑day challenges that can affect their emotional well‑being.  

Yet people living with diabetes demonstrate remarkable strengths, resilience and adaptability every day.
summary: More than 1.5 million Australians live with diabetes, a relentless, demanding condition that can affect their emotional well‑being. Yet people living with diabetes demonstrate remarkable strengths, resilience, and adaptability every day.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Survey finds endless TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts feeds hard for ADHD users
content:
A survey found that endless video feeds leave users with ADHD struggling to stop.  

Short‑form video platforms such as TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts use an effective tactic to maximize the time their users spend on the platforms: they feed one video after another into an algorithmically generated feed.  

As users scroll, new content loads automatically, creating an endless loop of ever‑changing content with no discernible end.
summary: A survey found that users with ADHD have difficulty stopping when using endless short‑form video feeds. Platforms such as TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts continuously load new videos in an algorithmic feed, creating an endless loop of content.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Oil and gas prices jump on Middle East shipping attacks, sending bond yields higher and stocks lower – business live
content:
Oil and gas prices surged following shipping attacks in the Middle East, which also triggered a rise in bond yields and a decline in stocks. Brent crude oil exceeded $105 per barrel, a move attributed to attacks on tankers and a reduction in US oil output in the Gulf of Mexico as storm Isaias approached.

The sell-off in bond markets placed pressure on the euro, pushing the currency to close near a 17-month low.
summary: Brent crude tops $105 a barrel amid attacks on tankers and squeeze on US oil output in Gulf of Mexico as storm Isaias approachesHere’s our wrap of the moves in markets:The sell-off in bond markets has put the euro under pressure, pushing to close to a 17-month low. Continue reading...
author: Guardian Business

title: Chrysler Building to Restore Crown After Sale
content:
The Chrysler Building in Manhattan is set to undergo a major renovation following its recent sale. The project will focus on restoring the skyscraper’s distinctive crown.

In addition to the restoration work, the renovation plans include creating a new supply of office space within the building.
summary: The Chrysler Building will have its crown restored after being sold. The building will undergo a major renovation and provide a new supply of offices.
author: BBC Business

title: Strong reading skills help teens resist online misinformation
content: A new study from the Brown School at Washington University in St. Louis indicates that students with stronger reading skills are better equipped to identify misinformation online. The research suggests these literacy skills are particularly significant for teenagers from disadvantaged backgrounds.
summary: A new study from the Brown School at Washington University in St. Louis found that students with stronger reading skills are better able to spot misinformation online. These skills may be especially important for teenagers from disadvantaged backgrounds.
author: Phys.org

title: DNA testing reveals greater gliders eat wider plant range
content:
Research from the University of the Sunshine Coast indicates that DNA testing of fecal samples reveals greater gliders consume a wider variety of plants than previously believed. This method eliminates the need for guesswork or manually analyzing the animals' waste to identify their diet.

Associate professor Dominique Potvin and her colleagues developed this approach to streamline the identification process. While the shortened title of their latest paper is "The future is faeces," the team aims to make the task less of a hands-on, hit-and-miss job.
summary: DNA testing of fecal samples shows greater gliders eat a wider variety of plants than previously thought, according to research from the University of the Sunshine Coast. Associate professor Dominique Potvin and colleagues published the findings in a paper titled "The future is faeces", aiming to reduce guesswork in identifying the animals' favorite snacks.
author: Phys.org

title: High-resolution global atmospheric model erases 'popcornlike' rain
content:
A new high-resolution atmospheric model developed by a team at the University of Tokyo has narrowed the standard grid spacing used in global climate and weather forecasting to just 220 meters (720 feet). This advancement contrasts with typical predictive models, which divide Earth's atmosphere into grid sections covering tens to hundreds of kilometers.

The increased resolution of the new model eliminated instances of "popcornlike" rain, a phenomenon characterized by bursts of heavy rain that appear in simulations but do not occur in real life. By removing these inaccuracies, the model provides more precise predictions of extreme local weather from a global framework.
summary: Global climate and weather forecasting use predictive models that divide Earth's atmosphere into a grid, with each section typically covering tens to hundreds of kilometers. Now a new model, run by a team at the University of Tokyo, has narrowed this grid spacing to just 220 meters (720 feet).
author: Phys.org

title: Pottery styles reveal contrasting paths to social complexity in Neolithic Europe
content:
Two researchers from the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine (NASU) and the Leibniz-Zentrum für Archäologie (LEIZA) in Germany have investigated the factors driving societal changes in Neolithic Europe, a period spanning approximately 8,000 to 4,000 years ago. The study highlights that societal evolution during this era did not follow a linear path.

To examine the dynamics of social complexity, the researchers utilized a mathematical model to analyze the interplay between population size, production capacity, and information exchange.
summary: Researchers from the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine (NASU) and the Leibniz-Zentrum für Archäologie (LEIZA) examined Neolithic Europe, approximately 8,000 to 4,000 years ago, using a mathematical model to analyze the interplay between population size, production capacity, and information exchange. Their findings indicate that societal changes in this period do not follow a linear path.
author: Phys.org

title: 253-Year Coral Core at Olowalu Reef Reveals Two Centuries of Environmental Change
content: New research led by the University of Hawai‘i Sea Grant College Program, the UH Mānoa School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST), and the U. S. Geological Survey analyzed a 253‑year‑old core from a massive coral colony at Olowalu Reef off West Maui. The core was used to reconstruct how Olowalu has changed over time, what has driven those changes, and what restoring healthy connections between land and sea may mean for the reef’s future.
summary: Researchers from the University of Hawai'i Sea Grant College Program, UH Mānoa SOEST, and the U.S. Geological Survey analyzed a 253-year-old core from a massive coral colony at Olowalu Reef off West Maui. The study reconstructs how Olowalu has changed over time, identifies drivers of those changes, and explores the implications of restoring healthy land‑sea connections for the reef's future.
author: Phys.org

title: Prepare for the unexpected: The coming super El Niño and NZ's ocean weather
content:
Residents of Te Whanganui‑a‑Tara Wellington are accustomed to preparing for any weather, carrying sunglasses, a raincoat and at least one extra layer. This “be prepared for anything” mindset is now being applied to Aotearoa’s ocean conditions amid this year’s super El Niño.  

Forecasts for the super El Niño are described as fickle, with unexpected outcomes likely. Authorities emphasize that preparation is needed to cope with the changing ocean weather.  

The message remains that residents should stay ready for the unpredictable effects of the super El Niño.
summary: Residents of Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington know it is always wise to prepare for any weather—to pack sunglasses, a raincoat and at least one extra layer. This "be prepared for anything" approach can equally be applied to Aotearoa's ocean weather during this year's "super" El Niño.
author: Phys.org

title: International Team Discovers 70 New Gravitational Lenses Using DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys
content:
A team of international scientists has identified 70 new gravitational lenses using data from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys and artificial intelligence. The lenses are rare cosmic alignments that act as natural magnifying glasses.

The discovery expands one of the largest collections of confirmed gravitational lenses to date. The new lenses will enable researchers to study dark matter, galaxy evolution, and the structure of the universe.
summary: An international team of scientists used data from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys and artificial intelligence to discover 70 new gravitational lenses. These lenses expand one of the largest collections of confirmed lenses and will help study dark matter, galaxy evolution, and the structure of the universe.
author: Phys.org

title: OpenAI Releases Hundreds of Papers on Major Mathematical Problems
content:
OpenAI has released 722 new research papers, a number that places the company among the most prolific in the field of mathematics. The papers claim to make progress on the biggest open problems in the discipline.

Among the hundreds of studies, a selection is highlighted for its potential to advance mathematical knowledge. The company’s focus on these high‑impact papers underscores its commitment to tackling some of the most challenging questions in the field.
summary: OpenAI has released hundreds of papers claiming progress on major open problems in mathematics. The article highlights those with the most potential.
author: New Scientist

title: El Niño forecast to end June next year after smashing all records
content:
The world may never go back to how it was after this monster El Niño.

El Niño is forecast to end around June next year after smashing all records. Its impacts could persist indefinitely in some parts of the world.
summary: The El Niño is forecast to end around June next year. Its impacts could persist indefinitely in some parts of the world.
author: New Scientist

title: Record El Niño threatens Great Barrier Reef
content:
Researchers have expressed concern over the potential impact of the strongest‑known El Niño on the Great Barrier Reef. The event could trigger significant ecological changes in the World Heritage Area.

Scientists are questioning whether any measures can be taken to prevent the reef’s possible demise.
summary: Researchers are worried about the impact the strongest-known El Niño will have on the Great Barrier Reef. They are questioning whether anything can be done to avert the World Heritage Area’s demise.
author: New Scientist

title: Study links Brexit, Truss mini‑budget, Covid lockdowns to UK mental health decline
content:
A recent study has identified five major events that have caused serious damage to mental wellbeing across the United Kingdom. The research notes that Brexit, Liz Truss’s mini‑budget, and other shocks over the past decade have led to a lasting deterioration in the population’s mental health.  

The study also found that Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, as well as the first and second COVID‑19 lockdowns, triggered significant rises in psychological distress, measured by increases in the number of people experiencing depression and anxiety.  

The findings highlight the cumulative impact of these events on the UK’s mental health over the last ten years.
summary: Researchers found that five events, including Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, Brexit, Liz Truss’s mini‑budget, and the first and second Covid lockdowns, caused serious damage to mental wellbeing across the UK. The study reports a serious and lasting deterioration in the UK population’s mental health over the last 10 years, with big rises in depression and anxiety during those shocks.
author: Guardian Science

title: All the news and science from the 2026 Nobel prizes – podcast
content:
The 2026 Nobel Prizes in chemistry, physics and physiology or medicine highlighted breakthroughs that have shaped modern science and medicine. The awards recognized work that has helped develop countless drugs, enabled physicists to observe a mysterious particle, and created a tool that could act as an on‑off switch for brain cells.

In medicine, the prize was awarded for research into the mysteries of the brain. The physics prize went to Francis Halzen for his work at the South Pole on neutrinos. The chemistry prize honored research on mirror‑image molecules.

Madeleine Finlay discussed the prizes with science editor Ian Sample and correspondents Nicola Davis and Linda Geddes.
summary: This year’s Nobel prizes in chemistry, physics and physiology or medicine have celebrated work that has been used to develop countless drugs and transform modern medicine, allowed physicists to observe one of the most mysterious particles, and provided a tool that could act as an on/off switch for brain cells. To find out more, Madeleine Finlay talks to our science editor, Ian Sample, and correspondents Nicola Davis and Linda GeddesNobel prize in medicine 2026 awarded for research into mysteries of brainNobel prize in physics goes to Francis Halzen for south pole work on neutrinosNobel prize in chemistry awarded for work on mirror-image molecules Continue reading...
author: Guardian Science

title: MIT computer scientist Margaret Hamilton, Apollo 11 software pioneer, dies at 90
content:
MIT announced on Wednesday that Margaret Hamilton, the computer pioneer whose software powered the first moon landing, has died at the age of 90.  

Hamilton led the development of software for the Apollo 11 mission and was a recipient of the Presidential Medal of Freedom. She learned to program under the tutelage of a renowned MIT meteorologist.  

She died on 30 September.
summary: Margaret Hamilton, a MIT computer scientist, led the development of the software that powered the Apollo 11 moon landing. She died on 30 September at the age of 90.
author: Guardian Science

title: TypeScript compiler, checker, and LSP ported to Rust by LLM
content:
A new open‑source project has ported the TypeScript compiler, type checker, and language‑server protocol (LSP) to Rust, created by the LLM team. The work is hosted on GitHub at https://github.com/pingdotgg/ts-rust.

The project has attracted attention on Hacker News, where it received 91 points and 167 comments. The discussion can be viewed at https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50000676.
summary: The TypeScript compiler, checker, and LSP have been ported to Rust by LLM. The project is hosted on GitHub at https://github.com/pingdotgg/ts-rust and has received 91 points and 167 comments on Hacker News.

title: Industrial AI Enters New Phase with Foundation, Physical, and Agentic Models
content:
Industrial AI is entering a new phase. After decades of predictive analytics and other specialized applications, advances in foundation models, physical AI, and agentic AI are making it possible to automate more complex tasks across industrial environments.  

Unlike AI that operates purely in the digital world, industrial AI can interact directly with physical systems, enabling deeper integration into manufacturing and other industrial processes.  

These developments suggest a shift toward more autonomous and physically capable AI solutions in industry.
summary: Industrial AI is entering a new phase as advances in foundation models, physical AI, and agentic AI enable automation of more complex tasks across industrial environments. Unlike digital-only AI, industrial AI can directly interact with physical systems.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Human‑shaped robot seen in videos; AI breakthroughs unlikely to change life soon
content:
AI breakthroughs in robotics won’t change your life any time soon

The article is a collaboration between MIT Technology Review and Aventine, a non‑profit research foundation that creates and supports content about how technology and science are changing the way we live.

A robot shaped like a human—white with a black head and torso—has been popping up on video feeds. Perhaps you’ve seen it dance or appear in other online videos.

content:
MIT Technology Review released its 2026 Climate Tech Companies to Watch list this week. The list is an annual project compiled by the MIT Technology Review team.

The goal of the list is to highlight promising, interesting advances and firms that the team believes are worth paying attention to in the world of climate and energy technology.
summary: MIT Technology Review released its 2026 Climate Tech Companies to Watch list this week. The list is part of an annual project aimed at highlighting promising advances and firms in climate and energy technology.

title: AI roadblocks for humanoids and portable rubber dams
content:
The Download is a weekday newsletter that delivers a daily snapshot of developments in technology. This edition focuses on advances in robotics, particularly the recent AI breakthroughs that have generated significant attention.

The newsletter notes that, despite the hype, these AI-powered robotics innovations are unlikely to change everyday life in the near term. It highlights the growing excitement around humanoid robots, describing the enthusiasm as “reaching fever pitch.” The article attributes this surge in interest to the belief that the same AI technologies can be applied across a range of robotic platforms.
summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, a weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. AI breakthroughs in robotics won’t change your life any time soon, and the hype around humanoid robots is reaching fever pitch.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Center for Humane Technology Lays Off Most Staff, Becomes Founder‑Led
content:
Tristan Harris’ tech nonprofit, the Center for Humane Technology, is laying off most staff and will operate in a founder‑led model.  

The organization helped spark a movement against excessive screen time, but internal tensions over its direction and strategy have simmered for years, sources tell WIRED.
summary: Tristan Harris’ tech nonprofit, the Center for Humane Technology, is laying off most staff and becoming founder‑led. The nonprofit had sparked a movement against excessive screen time, but internal tensions over direction and strategy have simmered for years.
author: Wired

title: WIRED Highlights 2026 Midterm Races to Watch
content:
WIRED reports that the 2026 midterm elections are the most noteworthy in recent memory, citing a focus on data centers, Elon Musk funding, and the AI lobby. The publication highlights these themes as central to its coverage.

WIRED is monitoring a set of candidates closely, though specific names and positions are not detailed in the source.
summary: WIRED describes the 2026 midterms as the most WIRED elections yet, highlighting data centers, Elon Musk funding, and the AI lobby. The article lists the candidates that the publication is following closely.

title: WIRED Tests Best Reusable Water Bottles of 2026
content:
WIRED recently tested a range of reusable water bottles for durability and usability. The review process included dropping the bottles, tossing them in bags, and cleaning their fiddly lids to assess everyday handling and maintenance.

After the tests, WIRED identified a selection of bottles that performed best. The publication recommends these models as the top choices for consumers seeking reliable, reusable hydration solutions.
summary: WIRED tested reusable water bottles by dropping them, tossing them in bags, and cleaning their fiddly lids. The article lists the recommended bottles.
author: Wired

title: Henri Kagan and Kensō Soai Awarded 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for Asymmetric Reaction
content:
In 2026, the Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to Henri Kagan and Kensō Soai for their pioneering work in asymmetric chemistry.  

Kagan and Soai designed chemical reactions that produce only one of the two mirror‑image forms of a molecule, a breakthrough in controlling molecular handedness.  

Their discovery is significant for the synthesis of pharmaceuticals and other biological substances.
summary: Henri Kagan and Kensō Soai were awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for designing chemical reactions that produce only one of the two mirror-image forms of a molecule. This discovery is significant for the synthesis of pharmaceuticals and other biological substances.
author: Wired

title: WIRED Partners with Neal Agarwal to Visualize Elon Musk’s Trillion-Dollar Fortune
content: WIRED has partnered with Neal Agarwal of Neal to create a visualization of Elon Musk’s massive wealth. The project was designed to illustrate the scale of Musk’s trillion‑dollar fortune. The collaboration brought together WIRED’s editorial resources and Neal Agarwal’s expertise in data visualization.
summary: WIRED partnered with Neal Agarwal of Neal to create a visualization of Elon Musk’s massive wealth. Here’s how it came together.

title: Amazon Launches Aluminum Alexa Tablets 12 Pro, 11, and 8 Running Android
content: Amazon has announced three new aluminum Alexa Tablets – the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, Alexa Tablet 11 and Alexa Tablet 8. All three models run Android and provide full access to the Google Play Store. The lineup also includes versions designed for children.
summary: Amazon's new aluminum Alexa Tablets 12 Pro, 11, and 8 run Android and provide full access to the Google Play Store. The lineup includes versions designed for children.

title: CBS procedural 'Cupertino' uses tech satire to address AI and industry issues
content:
CBS’s new procedural “Cupertino,” starring Ella Stiller, Mike Colter and Rachel Keller, tackles the tech backlash through a fictionalized lens. The series opens with a tentative tone but quickly finds its footing, weaving in satirical versions of real‑world tech phenomena such as the Zizians, Polymarket, Jeff Bezos’s alleged looks‑maxxing obsession, OpenAI’s purported use of Scarlett Johansson’s voice, and debates over AI guardrails.

By framing these contemporary issues within the familiar format of broadcast television, “Cupertino” aims to capture the sense of helplessness many feel amid rapid technological change that reaches far beyond the San Francisco Bay Area. The show’s creators use the medium’s “outdated” tools to deliver a timely commentary on the evolving tech landscape. The full story appears on The Verge.
summary: The CBS show “Cupertino” stars Ella Stiller, Mike Colter and Rachel Keller. The series blends a procedural format with satirical takes on tech topics such as AI guardrails, OpenAI, Jeff Bezos, Polymarket and other contemporary issues.
author: The Verge

title: Xbox Launches XP Division for Films, TV, and More
content:
Xbox has announced the creation of a new division called “XP,” which will focus on Xbox‑related experiences that are not video games. The division will handle films, television adaptations, consumer products, live events, and partnerships with creators and brands.

According to a blog post by Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball, XP will formalize four investment areas. The first, XBOX PICTURES, is aimed at bringing Xbox worlds and characters to new audiences through film, television, and other linear storytelling. The second, XBOX PRODUCTS, is intended to create products that are authentic to the fandom. The remaining two areas are not named in the provided text.

The information was released in a blog post by Matthew Ball, and the full story is available at The Verge.
summary: Xbox has created a new division called XP to handle non‑game Xbox experiences such as films, television, consumer products, live events, and brand partnerships. The division will bring together existing teams and formalize four investment areas, including XBOX PICTURES and XBOX PRODUCTS, as outlined by chief strategy officer Matthew Ball.
author: The Verge

title: Joe Rogan and Spotify renew $250 million podcast deal
content:
Spotify has renewed its multi-year licensing agreement with Joe Rogan, valuing the deal at approximately $250 million. The podcast, The Joe Rogan Experience, remains the number one show on the platform and globally. The renewed contract permits new episodes to be released weekly on Spotify and distributed across other platforms.

This renewal expands upon the initial exclusive streaming agreement signed in 2020. In 2024, Spotify permitted the show to be distributed to additional networks, including YouTube and Apple, as part of a previous deal with Rogan.
summary: Spotify has renewed its multi-year licensing agreement with Joe Rogan for a reported value of around $250 million. The deal allows new episodes of The Joe Rogan Experience to appear on Spotify and other platforms each week.
author: The Verge

title: Amazon Launches Alexa Tablets, New Android-Based Lineup
content:
Amazon is launching a new line of devices branded as Alexa Tablets, marking a significant departure from its previous hardware offerings. Unlike the Fire tablets that have defined the company’s market presence for the last 15 years, these new devices are designed to integrate the Alexa Plus assistant into the center of a user’s computing experience while functioning as standalone, high-quality tablets.

A key differentiator for the new lineup is its operating system, which runs full Android with support for Google Play. This allows users to access a wide range of third-party applications, a capability not previously available on Amazon’s standard tablet hardware. The devices also include preloaded Amazon applications and built-in features for quick access to Prime Video content and shopping services.
summary: Amazon is launching a new lineup of tablets called Alexa Tablets that run Android and include full Google Play support. The devices are designed to center Alexa Plus in users' computing life and provide quick access to Prime Video and Amazon shopping.
author: The Verge

title: Amazon Launches $499 Alexa Tablet 12 Pro with Full Google Play Access
content:
Amazon has unveiled a new Android tablet, the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, priced at $499. The device is part of a small group of new Android tablets announced by Amazon today, and it is positioned as a more desirable option than the company’s existing Fire lineup.

Unlike Fire tablets, the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro runs a full version of Android and provides unrestricted access to the Google Play app store, avoiding the Amazon‑centric app ecosystem and ads that appear on Fire devices. It is available with either 8 GB or 12 GB of RAM and is powered by a MediaTek Dimensity 8400 8‑core CPU.

The Verge has reported on the launch, noting the tablet’s specifications and its departure from Amazon’s typical low‑cost, Amazon‑centric tablet strategy.
summary: Amazon released a $499 Alexa Tablet 12 Pro that offers full Google Play access and comes with either 8GB or 12GB of RAM powered by a MediaTek Dimensity 8400 8‑core CPU. Unlike Fire tablets, it does not run a modified Android with Amazon ads.
author: The Verge

title: GTA VI Leaker Cyberleek Releases 25‑Minute Nude Gameplay Video
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI leaks continue with a new 25‑minute gameplay video that is almost as long as the game’s official “extended look” on Netflix. The clip focuses on the character Jason, who is shown running around Vice City almost entirely naked, including while riding a motorbike and at a beac… (source).

According to Kotaku, the video was released by GTA leaker Cyberleek, who previously cashed out on a memecoin and appeared to disappear earlier this year. The clip suggests that players will be able to play through GTA VI with their characters completely unclothed.

The full story is available at The Verge.
summary: Cyberleek posted a 25‑minute GTA VI gameplay video in which the character Jason is naked for almost the entire duration. The video shows Jason running around Vice City, including on a motorbike, and suggests players could play the game unclothed.
author: The Verge

title: Amazon Launches Kids Tablets with Parental Controls for Google Play
content:
Amazon has announced a new line of Kids Tablets that expand its Alexa Tablet family. The devices run Android and provide full access to the Google Play store, while adding parental controls that let parents restrict the software and content their children can access.

The Kids Tablets come in two styles of colorful cases featuring characters from Paw Patrol, Barbie, and SpongeBob. A thicker, more protective case is aimed at pre‑kindergarten children, while a thinner case is intended for kids aged six and up. Both tablet models are available in two sizes and feature lightweight aluminum designs and 8‑core processors.
summary: Amazon is introducing kid versions of its Alexa Tablets that run Android and allow parents to limit software and content on the Google Play store. The Amazon Kids Tablets come in two sizes with lightweight aluminum designs and 8‑core processors, and feature colorful cases with Paw Patrol, Barbie, and SpongeBob characters, offering a thicker protective option for pre‑kindergarten children and a thinner one for kids aged six and up.
author: The Verge

title: Vesta Raises $30M to Deploy Agent Swarms for Mortgage Lenders
content:
Vesta, an AI‑native software startup that helps lenders originate mortgages, has secured a $30 million funding round. The round was led by Conversion Capital.

The investment will support Vesta’s efforts to deploy swarms of agents for mortgage lenders, expanding its technology platform in the mortgage origination market. No additional investors or terms were disclosed.
summary: Vesta, an AI-native software startup that helps lenders originate mortgages, announced a $30 million funding round. The round was led by Conversion Capital.
author: TechCrunch

title: Amazon unveils Alexa tablets with Alexa+ and Google Play Store access
content:
Amazon announced a new line of Alexa tablets that feature Alexa+ and access to the Google Play Store.  

The lineup comprises three models: the Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, the Amazon Alexa Tablet 11, and the Amazon Alexa Tablet 8.
summary: Amazon unveiled a new lineup of Alexa tablets that include Alexa+ and Google Play Store access. The lineup consists of the Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, Amazon Alexa Tablet 11, and Amazon Alexa Tablet 8.
author: TechCrunch

title: TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026 seeks volunteers for Boston event on Nov. 4
content:
TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026 is set to return to Boston on November 4, and organizers have issued a final call for volunteers.  

The announcement invites “exceptional volunteers” to assist with the event’s operations, emphasizing limited availability of volunteer spots. Interested individuals are encouraged to act quickly to secure a role and gain insight into the inner workings of tech events.
summary: TechCrunch Founder Summit will return to Boston on November 4, 2026. The organizers issued a final call for volunteers, noting that spots are limited.
author: TechCrunch

title: China’s Manus raises over $500M in first post‑Meta funding round
content:
China’s Manus has raised over $500 million in its first funding round since its split with Meta.  

The round was led by Boyu Capital and IDG Capital, with participation from existing shareholders including Tencent, HSG (formerly known as Sequoia China), ZhenFund and other investors.
summary: China’s Manus raised over $500 million in its first funding round since splitting with Meta. The round was led by Boyu Capital and IDG Capital, with existing shareholders Tencent, HSG (formerly Sequoia China), ZhenFund and others also participating.
author: TechCrunch

title: Google launches AI Edge Foresight, an offline meeting note‑taker competing with Granola
content:
Google has launched a new local‑first application called AI Edge Foresight, positioning it as a competitor to Granola. The app is designed to operate offline and focuses on meeting note‑taking.

AI Edge Foresight can transcribe conversations, generate notes and answer questions using on‑device artificial intelligence.
summary: Google has introduced the AI Edge Foresight app, a local‑first tool that takes on Granola. The app works offline to transcribe conversations, generate notes, and answer questions using on‑device AI.
author: TechCrunch

title: Kenyan refugee camp workers do AI‑assisted translation gigs for uncertain low pay
content:
Refugee gig workers in Kenya are performing low‑paid tech tasks for overseas companies, often without knowing the client, purpose or payment. In a portable building at Kakuma refugee camp near Kenya’s northern border with South Sudan, a woman identified only as Grace used ChatGPT to research translations of Christian hymns in languages she does not speak.

Grace, who said she cannot work legally in Kenya, prompted the AI to translate an English hymn into an assigned East Asian language, then searched for existing versions and gathered details about the translator, author and Christian denomination. She submitted the compiled information to AOP Connect, a crowdsourced research platform owned by British AI enterprise software firm RWS.
summary: In Kakuma refugee camp near Kenya’s border with South Sudan, refugees are hired as gig workers by tech firms to translate Christian hymns using ChatGPT and submit research to AOP Connect. The workers, who cannot legally work in Kenya, receive uncertain, low pay for the tasks.
author: Guardian Technology

title: EU ends sponsorship of Disinfo2026 conference after Trump officials' request
content:
The European Union’s diplomatic service ended its sponsorship of the #Disinfo2026 conference after pressure from officials in the Trump administration, the Guardian reports.

According to the report, the Trump administration also urged Canada and Lithuania to pull their support, and both countries, along with the EU diplomatic service, subsequently withdrew their sponsorship. Days before the event, the conference’s website had its logos removed.

#Disinfo2026, organized by the Brussels‑based non‑profit EU Disinfo Lab, is scheduled for Wednesday and Thursday in a hotel in Vilnius, Lithuania. The annual gathering brings together hundreds of researchers, journalists, technologists and policymakers from Europe’s counter‑disinformation community.
summary: The Trump administration pressured multiple countries, leading the EU diplomatic service, Canada and Lithuania to withdraw their sponsorship of the #Disinfo2026 conference. The conference, run by the Brussels non‑profit EU Disinfo Lab, is being held Wednesday and Thursday in Vilnius with hundreds of researchers, journalists, technologists and policymakers attending.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Molly Russell’s father to say Instagram ‘killed’ daughter in UK cinema ad
content:
Ian Russell, father of Molly Russell, will address UK cinema audiences in a 30‑second advertisement shown before screenings of the new documentary The Social Reckoning. In the spot, released on Friday, Russell says “Instagram helped kill my daughter” and adds that “too little has changed” since his child’s death.

Molly Russell, 14, died by suicide in 2017 after viewing harmful content on Instagram. The ad will appear prior to the film about Mark Zuckerberg’s social media empire, linking her death to the platform’s impact.
summary: Ian Russell will appear in a 30‑second advertisement shown before UK screenings of the film The Social Reckoning. In the ad he says Instagram helped kill his 14‑year‑old daughter, Molly Russell, who died by suicide in 2017 after viewing harmful content.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Co-op Legal Services puts staff under AI call‑monitoring system
content:
Co-op Legal Services has rolled out an AI‑driven listening system that records and scores every probate‑related phone call made by its agents, prompting a whistleblower to describe the practice as “oppressive and dystopian.”  

The automated technology analyses interactions between staff and customers seeking advice on probate, wills and estates, assigning a percentage score to each call.  

The whistleblower’s comments underscore concerns that the new system places workers under continuous AI surveillance.
summary: Co-op Legal Services is using AI models to record, analyze and assign a percentage score to every probate, wills and estates phone call between agents and customers. A whistleblower described the system as oppressive and dystopian, saying it places workers under AI surveillance.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Asos breach involved more personal data than initially reported, BBC says
content: ASOS has issued an update after the BBC reported that cyber criminals contacted the broadcaster claiming the recent breach involved more than “basic contact details.” The retailer’s statement acknowledges the new information provided by the attackers, indicating that the scope of personal data taken may be broader than initially disclosed.
summary: Asos said its recent cyber breach involved more personal information than initially disclosed. The BBC reported that the hackers told the outlet the breach went beyond basic contact details.
author: BBC Technology

title: Christa Pike regains consciousness after surviving two lethal pentobarbital doses
content:
Christa Pike regained consciousness after surviving two allegedly lethal doses of pentobarbital administered during a botched execution.  

Her attorney reported that medical staff had considered Pike brain dead and were preparing to discontinue life support when she unexpectedly woke up and began speaking.
summary: Christa Pike regained consciousness after surviving two supposedly lethal doses of pentobarbital during a botched execution. Her lawyer said she had been considered brain dead and near removal from life support before she unexpectedly woke and began speaking.
author: Euronews

title: Dry wells and shrinking water holes as drought grips Sri Lanka
content:
A prolonged drought in central Sri Lanka is leaving wells dry, according to reports. The water shortage is harming farmers’ livelihoods as they lose access to essential irrigation.

The scarcity is also forcing wildlife to gather around the few remaining water holes, which are shrinking as the drought persists.
summary: Prolonged drought in central Sri Lanka is leaving wells dry, hurting farmers’ livelihoods and pushing wildlife to crowd shrinking water holes.
author: Euronews

title: Midday news bulletin covers Europe and global stories on October 8, 2026
content:
A news bulletin titled “Latest news bulletin | October 8th, 2026 – Midday” was released, inviting readers to catch up with the most important stories from Europe and beyond on that date.

The bulletin promises coverage of the latest breaking news across World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture and Travel, summarising developments from the day’s events.
summary: The bulletin presents the most important stories from around Europe and beyond on October 8, 2026. It features latest news in world, business, entertainment, politics, culture and travel.
author: Euronews

title: Donald Trump claims he deserves Nobel Peace Prize after settling eight wars
content: Donald Trump asserted that he deserves the Nobel Peace Prize, claiming he “settled eight wars.” The former president said his claim is based on his efforts to resolve international conflicts. He highlighted these diplomatic achievements as justification for the award. No further details about the specific conflicts or any official nomination were provided.
summary: Donald Trump says he deserves the Nobel Peace Prize. He cited his efforts to resolve international conflicts, saying he settled eight wars.
author: Euronews

title: South Korea recalls ambassador to Ukraine over dispute on North Korean POW repatriation
content: South Korea has recalled its ambassador to Ukraine amid a diplomatic row over the handling of two North Korean prisoners of war. Seoul said Kyiv’s public disclosure of the repatriation of the two prisoners endangered their families in North Korea, where relatives of those who fall into enemy hands face punishment. Ukraine has rejected South Korea’s accusations.
summary: Seoul said Kyiv's public disclosure of the repatriation of two North Korean prisoners endangered their families in North Korea, where relatives of those who fall into enemy hands face punishment. Ukraine has rejected South Korea's accusations.
author: Euronews

title: Ethiopian drones strike Eritrean vehicles near Adigrat amid diplomatic break
content:
Ethiopian drones carried out strikes on Eritrean vehicles around the northern city of Adigrat overnight.  

Witnesses said the attacks destroyed several lorries and caused Eritrean troops to retreat from the area.  

The incident occurred days after Ethiopia expelled Eritrean diplomats and Eritrea responded by severing diplomatic ties.
summary: Ethiopian drone strikes hit Eritrean forces, accused of backing rebels in Tigray, around the northern city of Adigrat overnight. Witnesses reported destroyed lorries and retreating troops, days after Ethiopia expelled Eritrean diplomats and Eritrea severed ties.
author: Euronews

title: Iran strikes two vessels off Qatar and Fujairah, extending operations beyond Hormuz
content:
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) reported that two commercial tankers were struck within a 24‑hour period, signaling an expansion of attacks beyond the Strait of Hormuz.  

One vessel was hit off the coast of Qatar, marking the first such incident in that area in six months. The second vessel was struck off Fujairah in the Gulf of Oman.  

IRGC‑affiliated outlets said the attacks demonstrate Tehran’s extension of operations beyond the crucial strait.
summary: Two commercial vessels were hit within 24 hours, one off Qatar—the first attack there in six months—and one off Fujairah in the Gulf of Oman. IRGC‑affiliated outlets suggested the strikes show Tehran extending operations beyond the crucial strait.
author: Euronews

title: Boston Ballet performs at Paris’s Théâtre des Champs‑Elysées, featuring Ekman and Khan
content:
Boston Ballet is set to perform this week at the historic Théâtre des Champs‑Elysées in Paris, marking a return to the French capital for the company.  

Artistic director Mikko Nissinen discussed the significance of the engagement and previewed the program, which will feature works by choreographers Alexander Ekman and Akram Khan.  

Nissinen said the Paris audience can anticipate the distinct styles of Ekman and Khan as part of the company’s effort to build a lasting legacy in the city.
summary: Artistic director Mikko Nissinen says the Boston Ballet’s return to Paris this week includes performances at the historic Théâtre des Champs‑Elysées. The program will feature works by choreographers Alexander Ekman and Akram Khan for the French audience.
author: France 24

title: Three killed in Houthi attacks on Saudi international airports, including Riyadh
content:
Saudi authorities reported that three people were killed in attacks on two of the kingdom’s international airports, including the facility in Riyadh, after Yemen’s Houthis said they had fired on both transport hubs.  

The Iran‑backed Houthis have said they are carrying out a wave of attacks on Saudi civilian infrastructure in recent weeks, coinciding with a Riyadh‑backed counter‑offensive aimed at reversing the group’s territorial gains.  

France 24’s Philip Turle examined the Houthis’ objectives in the conflict.
summary: Saudi authorities said Wednesday three people were killed in attacks on two international airports, including Riyadh, after Yemen's Iran‑backed Houthis claimed to have fired on both transport hubs. The Iran‑backed Houthis have claimed a wave of attacks on Saudi civilian infrastructure in recent weeks as Riyadh‑backed forces pressed a counter‑offensive against the group's territorial gains.
author: France 24

title: French PM Sebastien Lecornu says government will present plan for student protests by end of October
content:
French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu told viewers in a televised address on Wednesday evening that France could not remain “indifferent” to the concerns of high‑school students protesting across the country. He said the “anger of young people does not come from nowhere” and denied that security forces have been given orders to confront the demonstrators.

Lecornu announced that the government will unveil a plan to address the crisis at the end of October, though no specific measures were detailed in the address. France 24’s Rochelle Ferguson Bouyahi will examine what steps the government may introduce and whether they could calm the protests.
summary: Sebastien Lecornu told a televised address that France cannot be indifferent to the concerns of protesting high school students and denied security forces have orders to confront them. He said the government will present a plan to respond to the crisis at the end of October.
author: France 24

title: Paris exhibition at Irish Cultural Centre highlights Ireland's housing crisis
content:
A new contemporary art exhibition at the Irish Cultural Centre in Paris is turning its focus to Ireland’s housing crisis. The show, announced in conjunction with interviews conducted by Perspective with the museum’s director and one of the participating artists, aims to reflect the scale of the problem through artistic works.

The exhibition arrives amid broader European concerns about housing shortages, highlighted by recent large‑scale demonstrations in Spain. Experts cited in the exhibition’s background note that Ireland would need 12 houses for every street of 10 to meet demand, underscoring the severity of the issue.
summary: A new exhibition at the Irish Cultural Centre in Paris is examining Ireland's housing crisis through contemporary art. Experts say Ireland needs 12 houses for every 10 built, and the museum's director and a participating artist were spoken to about the show.
author: France 24

title: 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal, eviction protest figure, dies after forced removal
content:
Maricarmen Abascal, an 87‑year‑old pensioner, has died after her eviction last month sparked nationwide protests in Spain.  

Abascal was forced out of a home she had lived in for more than 70 years after the property was purchased by an investment fund, an action that ignited demonstrations across the country.  

Some of the protesters who took to the streets said they believe the stress of the eviction contributed to her death.
summary: Maricarmen Abascal, an 87-year-old pensioner, died after being evicted from her home of more than 70 years. Her eviction last month, after the property was bought by an investment fund, sparked nationwide housing protests, and some protesters say the stress contributed to her death.
author: France 24

title: 30 killed in Russian strike on public bus in eastern Ukraine
content:
Thirty people were killed and at least 18 injured by Russian strikes in eastern Ukraine, including an attack on a public bus, authorities said Thursday.

The casualties occurred as part of an intensive pre‑winter wave of attacks that continued across the region.
summary: Thirty people were killed and at least 18 were injured by Russian strikes in eastern Ukraine that included an attack on a public bus, authorities said Thursday. The attack occurred as an intensive pre‑winter wave of attacks continued.
author: France 24

title: Microsoft unveils PC‑run AI coding model and security tech, challenging Apple
content:
Microsoft announced on Wednesday a new AI coding model that operates directly on personal computers, alongside security technology designed to block AI agents from accessing data without permission.  

The company said the on‑device model enables developers to write code using artificial intelligence without relying on cloud services, while the accompanying security feature aims to safeguard user data from unauthorized AI access.  

Microsoft’s moves are positioned as a challenge to Apple’s efforts to integrate more artificial‑intelligence capabilities into its own personal devices.
summary: Microsoft unveiled on Wednesday an AI coding model that can run directly on personal computers. It also introduced security technology to block AI agents from accessing data without permission, positioning the moves against Apple's push to add more AI to personal devices.
author: France 24

title: EU seeks more Middle Corridor trade; drone attacks off Bulgaria raise security concerns
content:
The European Union is seeking to boost trade through the Middle Corridor, viewing the route as a potential gateway for Asian imports that could bring significant benefits to Bulgaria.

However, drone attacks on commercial ships off the Bulgarian coast on Tuesday serve as a stark reminder of the security risks that could affect the corridor’s viability.
summary: The EU wants to increase trade via the Middle Corridor, which could bring big benefits for Bulgaria. Recent drone attacks on commercial ships off the Bulgarian coast underscore the security risks involved.
author: DW World

title: Russia intensifies attacks on Ukrainian data centers, but internet remains resilient
content:
Russia has intensified attacks on Ukraine’s data centers, prompting concerns about the country’s online connectivity.  

Experts note that Ukraine’s internet infrastructure is sufficiently robust to avoid a total shutdown, though the heightened targeting could lead to higher costs for online services.
summary: Russia is targeting Ukraine's data centers more frequently. Experts say Ukraine's internet system is too robust to be shut down entirely, though services could become more expensive.
author: DW World

title: South Korea to recall its ambassador to Ukraine over UN POW disclosure
content:
South Korea announced that it will recall its ambassador to Ukraine. The decision follows Seoul’s protest over the public disclosure at the United Nations of a transfer involving North Korean prisoners of war.

Seoul said it had demanded an apology for the disclosure, but it has not received one, prompting the recall of the ambassador.
summary: South Korea announced it will recall its ambassador to Ukraine. Seoul said it is upset that a transfer of North Korean prisoners of war was disclosed at the UN and that it has not received an apology.
author: DW World

title: Two ships sink off Bulgaria, Romania after drone attacks; Bulgaria avoids blaming Russia
content:
Two ships sank off the coasts of Bulgaria and Romania after drone attacks in recent days.  

Bulgaria’s government in Sofia has refrained from publicly attributing the attacks to Russia.  

The incidents have prompted questions about the security situation in the Black Sea region and Europe’s broader defense posture.
summary: Two ships have sunk off the coasts of Bulgaria and Romania after drone attacks in recent days. Sofia has held back on pointing the finger at Russia.
author: DW World

title: South Korea warns of AI‑assisted hacking after bank data breach
content:
Seoul officials have issued a warning after a recent breach of South Korean banks’ cyber defenses that reportedly involved AI‑assisted hacking. The incident has raised alarm over the potential for similar tactics to be employed against other sectors.

Authorities cautioned that the same AI‑driven methods could also be directed at government agencies, underscoring concerns about broader vulnerabilities in the country’s digital infrastructure.
summary: Agents in Seoul said a recent breach of South Korean banks' cyber defenses involved AI‑assisted hacking. They warned the same techniques could also target other sectors and government agencies.
author: DW World

title: Kenya races to trace contacts after first Ebola death, WHO says
content:
Kenya’s first Ebola death has sparked an urgent effort to trace every person the victim may have contacted. The World Health Organization’s top official in the country told UN News that authorities are racing to identify all contacts.

The United Nations and its partners are providing full support for the tracing operation, according to the WHO official’s first interview on the case. The coordinated response aims to contain the virus and prevent further transmission.
summary: Kenya’s first Ebola death has triggered a race to trace everyone the victim came into contact with. The WHO’s top official in Kenya told UN News in her first interview on the case that the United Nations and partners are providing full support.
author: UN News

title: New data reveals harsh treatment of child migrants traveling to Europe
content:
New data on child migrants were released on Wednesday, drawing attention to the severe conditions many face while journeying to Europe.  

The report emphasizes that numerous children endure harrowing treatment as they travel in search of work and shelter across the continent.
summary: New data on child migrants was published on Wednesday. The data highlighted the harrowing treatment many face while traveling to Europe in search of work and shelter.
author: UN News

title: Russia says no plague case in Siberia after lab technician death reported
content:
World Health Organization officials said on Wednesday that health authorities in Russia have confirmed there is “no plague case” in Siberia.  

The statement followed reports from the previous week that a laboratory technician in the region had died of pneumonia of an unknown origin.
summary: Health authorities in Russia said there is “no plague case” in Siberia. The statement followed reports that a lab technician had died of pneumonia of an unknown origin in the region, WHO officials said on Wednesday.
author: UN News

title: UN urges end to civilian attacks after overnight Russian strikes kill 19 in Chernihiv
content:
The United Nations has condemned the latest attacks in Ukraine and urged the protection of civilians.  

On Wednesday, the UN Humanitarian Coordinator for Ukraine called for an end to attacks against civilians after overnight strikes by Russian forces reportedly killed at least 19 people in the Chernihiv Region.  

The call follows the most recent wave of strikes in the area.
summary: The UN Humanitarian Coordinator for Ukraine called for an end to attacks against civilians. The call followed overnight Russian strikes that reportedly killed at least 19 people in the Chernihiv Region.
author: UN News

title: Canadian Poet Anne Carson Wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
content:
Anne Carson has been awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature, the Swedish Academy announced. The Canadian poet and essayist is recognized for her genre‑crossing works, including Autobiography of Red.

The Academy praised Carson’s “bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature.” The prize acknowledges her contributions to modern literary forms.
summary: The Swedish Academy awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature to Canadian poet and essayist Anne Carson. Carson's bold and inventive oeuvre, which engages in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature.
author: Guardian World

title: Sri Lanka arrests former first lady Shiranthi Rajapaksa in graft case
content:
Sri Lanka has arrested former first lady Shiranthi Rajapaksa, the wife of former President Mahinda Rajapaksa, in a corruption case.

The arrest was made in connection with a graft investigation, but no further details about the allegations or the legal proceedings have been released.
summary: Shiranthi Rajapaksa, the former first lady of Sri Lanka and wife of Mahinda Rajapaksa, has been arrested. The arrest is in a corruption case.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Italian law proposes bonus seats for election winners, drawing criticism
content:
Italian lawmakers are considering a new law that would grant bonus seats to the coalition that wins the most votes in national elections. The proposal has sparked controversy.

Critics argue the measure is undemocratic and could give the winning coalition outsized power in parliament.
summary: The proposed Italian law would give bonus parliamentary seats to the coalition that wins an election. Critics say the measure is undemocratic and could grant the winning coalition outsized power in parliament.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UK’s Burnham open to Germany joining GCAP fighter jet programme
content: UK defence minister Grant Burnham said he is “open” to Germany joining the GCAP fighter‑jet programme. The GCAP pact, a collaboration between the United Kingdom, Italy and Japan to build a new fighter jet, welcomed Canada as an observer in July. Burnham’s comments come as the UK continues to expand the partnership, which now includes a potential German participant. The programme remains focused on joint development and procurement of advanced fighter aircraft.
summary: Burnham said the UK is open to Germany joining the GCAP fighter jet programme. The GCAP pact between the UK, Italy and Japan to build a new fighter jet welcomed Canada as an observer in July.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Two killed as building partially collapses in Istanbul's Maltepe district
content:
Two people were killed when a building partially collapsed in Istanbul’s Maltepe district, Turkiye.  

Rescue teams pulled eight survivors from the rubble, but operations were slowed by concerns that the structure could collapse further.  

The incident left authorities focused on securing the site and attending to the victims.
summary: Two people died when a building partially collapsed in Istanbul's Maltepe district. Eight survivors were rescued from the rubble, and operations were slowed by fears of further collapse.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Teacher Mochamad Subchi Azal Tsani returned to Indonesian jail after secret parole
content:
A teacher convicted of sexually abusing a pupil has been returned to prison in Indonesia following a BBC investigation. The offender, identified as Mochamad Subchi Azal Tsani, had been secretly released on parole in 2025 after serving less than half of his sentence.

The BBC’s inquiry prompted authorities to re‑incarcerate Tsani, overturning the earlier parole decision. No further details about the case or the length of the new custodial term were provided.
summary: Mochamad Subchi Azal Tsani, a teacher who sexually abused a pupil, is back in an Indonesian jail following a BBC investigation. He had been secretly released on parole in 2025 after serving less than half his sentence.
author: BBC World

title: Christa Pike walking after failed execution, lawyer says
content:
Christa Pike, the woman convicted of murdering Colleen Slemmer, is reportedly walking in her hospital room after surviving a failed execution by lethal injection in the United States, her lawyer told the BBC.

The lawyer said Pike has moved around the hospital room following two lethal injections that did not result in death. No further details about her condition or the circumstances of the execution were provided.
summary: Christa Pike, the murderer of Colleen Slemmer, survived two lethal injection attempts. Her lawyer told the BBC she is now moving around her hospital room.
author: BBC World

title: Israel says most UK diplomats will leave East Jerusalem consulate, Miliband says vital services stay
content:
Israel announced that most United Kingdom diplomats will depart the consulate in East Jerusalem. The statement also noted that, according to Miliband, essential services at the consulate will continue to operate.

Israel said in September it would take action in response to UK sanctions targeting illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank. The diplomatic withdrawal follows that earlier declaration.
summary: Israel said most UK diplomats will leave the East Jerusalem consulate. Miliband said vital services will remain, and Israel said it would act in September in response to UK sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank.
author: BBC World

title: Russian blaze on buses kills at least 30 in Kramatorsk
content:
A Russian strike on buses in the frontline city of Kramatorsk killed at least 30 people, officials said, as deadly attacks on Ukraine increase.  

Ukraine accused Russia of deliberately targeting the crowded vehicles in Kramatorsk in order to maximize civilian deaths.  

The incident underscores the surge in lethal attacks across the country.
summary: Officials say a Russian strike on buses in the frontline city of Kramatorsk killed at least 30 people. Ukraine says Russia targeted the crowded vehicles to maximize civilian casualties.
author: BBC World

title: Brendan Venter likens Premiership Rugby media duties to autocratic practice
content:
Brendan Venter, a player for Saracens, likened the media obligations of Prem Rugby to “something from an autocratic land” after reluctantly speaking at a press conference.  

Venter made the comparison during the event, noting his discomfort with the compulsory nature of the media duties. The statement was made in the context of the press conference where he was asked to comment on the team’s media responsibilities.
summary: Saracens' Brendan Venter said Prem Rugby's media obligations were like something from an autocratic land. He made the comment after reluctantly speaking at a press conference.
author: BBC Sport

title: Top Fuel Drag Racing: Only Elite Motorsport Where Women Often Win Major Titles
content:
Top Fuel drag racing stands out as the only elite motorsport class in which women regularly outperform men for major titles.  

The sport, known for its extreme speed and power, has seen a consistent pattern of female competitors securing championships that are traditionally dominated by male drivers.  

This trend highlights the unique competitive dynamic of Top Fuel drag racing within the broader motorsport landscape.
summary: Top Fuel drag racing is the only elite motorsport class where women frequently beat men to major titles. Women have repeatedly won major titles in this class.
author: BBC Sport

title: Trump to award Elon Musk National Medal of Science at White House summit
content:
President Trump will award the National Medal of Science to Elon Musk and other prominent tech executives Thursday, a White House official confirmed to The Hill’s broadcast partner, NewsNation.  

Musk, the head of SpaceX and Tesla, will receive this high honor at the White House’s “Science: A New Golden Age” summit. Three other tech leaders will also receive the medal.
summary: President Trump will present the National Medal of Science to Elon Musk and other tech executives on Thursday. Musk, who leads SpaceX and Tesla, will receive the award at the White House’s “Science: A New Golden Age” summit.
author: The Hill

title: Trump doubles down on California comments: ‘Let them hit San Diego, let them hit Los Angeles’
content:
President Trump reaffirmed his previous remarks suggesting Iran could strike Los Angeles and San Diego during a rally in Texas on Wednesday. He stated that the United States would not allow such a scenario to occur, despite his earlier provocative comments.

"You want to see trauma? You want to see problems? And I said it the other day, let them hit…" Trump said, doubling down on the assertion that Iranian attacks could target California cities.
summary: President Trump reiterated his comments suggesting Iran could attack Los Angeles and San Diego during a rally in Texas. He added that the United States would not let such a scenario play out.
author: The Hill

title: Hinson, Turek debate health care, agriculture in Iowa Senate race
content:
U.S. Rep. Ashley Hinson (R-Iowa) and state Rep. Josh Turek (D-Iowa) faced off in their first debate for the U.S. Senate on Wednesday night. The two candidates, who are running to replace retiring Sen. Joni, engaged in a discussion that highlighted significant disagreements on key policy areas.

Health care cuts and agriculture emerged as major topics during the exchange. The candidates also addressed each other’s voting records and attendance in their current roles, with the debate featuring notable sparring over these performance-related issues.
summary: U.S. Rep. Ashley Hinson (R-Iowa) and state Rep. Josh Turek (D-Iowa) faced off in a Wednesday night debate for a seat in the Iowa Senate. The debate focused on health care cuts, agriculture, and each candidate’s voting record and attendance in their current roles.
author: The Hill

title: FDA delays mifepristone safety review publication until March
content:
The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced in a Wednesday court filing that it will not publish its safety review of the abortion drug mifepristone until March. The agency also said it will not impose any new restrictions on the pill before that time.

The decision was disclosed in a court document and is expected to further frustrate anti‑abortion activists, who have been losing patience with the FDA’s handling of the medication.
summary: The FDA disclosed in a court filing that it will not publish its safety review of mifepristone until March. The agency stated it will not impose new restrictions on the drug before that time.
author: The Hill

title: Shapiro and Garrity Clash Over Measles, Voter ID, and Data Centers in Gov Debate
content: Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro (D) and State Treasurer Stacy Garrity (R) engaged in their first and only scheduled debate on Wednesday evening, addressing key issues including an ongoing measles outbreak, voter ID reform, and data centers. The event, which featured the parties’ nominees to lead the commonwealth, was hosted by ABC27, a local affiliate of Nexstar, the parent company of The Hill.
summary: Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro (D) and state Treasurer Stacy Garrity (R) sparred over an ongoing measles outbreak, voter ID reform, and data centers during their first and only scheduled debate on Wednesday evening. The debate was hosted by ABC27, a local affiliate of The Hill’s parent company, Nexstar.
author: The Hill

title: Trump Criticizes Cuellar for Staying Democrat After 2025 Pardon
content: President Trump criticized Rep. Henry Cuellar (D-Texas) on Wednesday evening for remaining a Democrat after receiving a presidential pardon in 2025. The president’s comments, made in a Truth Social post prior to a campaign rally in San Antonio, marked the latest escalation in a feud that has intensified since Cuellar announced his reelection bid.
summary: President Trump attacked Rep. Henry Cuellar (D‑Texas) on Wednesday evening for refusing to change parties after receiving a presidential pardon in 2025. The criticism follows a feud that has escalated since Cuellar announced his reelection bid and was posted by Trump on Truth Social ahead of a campaign rally in San Antonio.
author: The Hill
