title: Amazon Prime Big Deal Days: Top Discounts on Recommended Gear
content:
Amazon Prime Big Deal Days have begun, and the latest coverage highlights the most attractive discounts available during the event.  

The report notes that the team has identified the best price reductions across a wide range of gear.  

All of the discounted items are those recommended by the team, offering shoppers a curated selection of high‑value products.
summary: Amazon Prime Big Deal Days are here. We have tracked down the best discounts on all the gear our team recommends.
author: Wired

title: Meta Quest 3S drops to $297.49 during Amazon October Prime Day sale
content:
The Meta Quest 3S is available for $297.99 for the 128GB model at Amazon, Walmart, and Best Buy until the end of Amazon’s October Prime Day sale. This price represents a discount from the usual $349.99. The headset features inside-out tracking for standalone functionality and utilizes the same chipset as the pricier Quest 3, though it retains the lenses and screen resolution of the Quest 2.

In addition to the hardware discount, the deal includes three months of Horizon Plus, which provides access to a large library of games. The Meta Quest 3S is a battery-powered standalone VR headset that can play titles from the Meta Store or connect to a gaming PC for experiences like Half-Life Alyx.

Customers purchasing the headset from Amazon will also receive the “Cardboard Monkenaut” cosmetic set for Gorilla Tag VR and 2,000 “Shiny Rocks” for in-game items. Gorilla Tag is a free-to-play multiplayer game on Quest headsets where players chase friends or matchmade opponents through trees in a tag-style game.
summary: Amazon, Walmart, and Best Buy are selling the 128GB Meta Quest 3S for $297.49, down from its usual price of $349.99, until the end of the October sale. Purchases from Amazon include three months of Horizon Plus, a "Cardboard Monkenaut" cosmetic set for Gorilla Tag VR, and 2,000 in-game "Shiny Rocks."
author: The Verge

title: Microsoft tests Surface Laptop Ultra in Redmond lab to build MacBook Pro competitor
content:
Microsoft rigorously tests its new laptop before it reaches consumers.  The process takes place in a windowless, warehouse‑like lab on the company’s Redmond, Washington campus.

In the lab, the Surface device team programs robots to press the laptop’s buttons thousands of times, exposes the devices to radio waves from giant antennas, and builds contraptions that drop objects from increasingly daring heights to assess durability.

The latest laptop under test is the Surface Laptop Ultra.  According to the report, it is not merely a high‑end configuration of the Surface Laptop but the debut platform for Microsoft’s new line.
summary: Microsoft’s Surface Laptop Ultra is being tested in a windowless lab on its Redmond campus, where robots repeatedly press buttons, devices are exposed to radio waves, and objects are dropped from increasing heights. The lab’s rigorous testing ensures the laptop can withstand real‑world conditions before its public release, positioning it as Microsoft’s competitor to the MacBook Pro.
author: The Verge

title: Microsoft upgrades Copilot with local file access and OS actions at Windows event
content:
At its Windows and Surface event, Microsoft announced an upgrade to its Copilot AI system that grants the tool access to local files and the capability to perform actions across the operating system. This development is part of a concept Microsoft refers to as “Hybrid Intelligence,” which utilizes a combination of local and cloud AI models to execute tasks efficiently.

Jacob Andreou, Microsoft’s EVP of Copilot, demonstrated the functionality of Hybrid Intelligence during a video presentation on stage. In the demo, Andreou asked the Autopilot tool to assist with filing taxes, specifically instructing the AI agent to retrieve information from an email received from his accountant.
summary: Microsoft upgraded Copilot at its Windows and Surface event to access local files and perform actions across the OS. Jacob Andreou, EVP of Copilot, demonstrated the new Hybrid Intelligence feature by having Autopilot help with filing taxes after receiving an email from his accountant.
author: The Verge

title: Microsoft Announces Surface Laptop Ultra with Nvidia RTX Spark, $2,599 Starting Price
content:
Microsoft concluded a large Windows and Surface‑focused keynote in San Francisco, announcing several new products and updates.  

The centerpiece was the Surface Laptop Ultra, a laptop powered by Nvidia’s RTX Spark Arm‑based chip. It will start at $2,599 for a configuration with an 8‑core CPU, 24 GB of RAM and 512 GB of storage, and is scheduled for release on October 16. The device includes built‑in magnetic USB‑C charging instead of the proprietary Surface Connect magnetic charging port. The Verge’s Tom Warren has published a deep dive on the new laptop.  

Microsoft also revealed the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, a mini PC for developers that is available for preorder at $5,999 and will ship in November. In addition, Microsoft shared updates for Windows, including “Hybrid Intelligence” features that let Copilot use files on a Windows PC to take actions, a new search experience that allows quick actions from the search bar, and the arrival of Muse on Windows. The first Nvidia RTX Spark laptops are priced up to $7,000.
summary: Microsoft unveiled the Surface Laptop Ultra, a new laptop powered by Nvidia's RTX Spark Arm‑based chip, with an 8‑core CPU, 24 GB of RAM, 512 GB of storage, a starting price of $2,599, built‑in magnetic USB‑C charging, and a release date of October 16. The event also announced the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, available for preorder at $5,999 with shipping in November, and revealed Windows updates featuring Hybrid Intelligence Copilot and a new search experience that allows quick actions from the search bar.
author: The Verge

title: First Nvidia RTX Spark Laptops Priced up to $7,000
content:
The first Nvidia RTX Spark laptops, priced up to $7,000, are positioned to compete with high‑end MacBook Pros. The new RTX Spark chip powers a lineup that includes the flagship Surface Laptop Ultra and models from Dell, Lenovo, MSI, HP, and Asus.

The lowest‑priced configurations start at $2,599 and feature an 18‑core CPU, 24 GB of unified memory, and 512 GB of storage. This price point is close to a similarly specced 14‑inch MacBook Pro equipped with an M5 Pro chip, though the Apple model includes 1 TB of storage.

Prices for both RTX Spark and Apple laptops rise sharply above the entry level. Of the pricing seen so far, a kitted‑out Asus ProArt P16 RTX Spark …
summary: Nvidia's first RTX Spark laptops, including the 15‑inch Surface Laptop Ultra, are available from Dell, Lenovo, MSI, HP, and Asus and start at $2,599 for models with an 18‑core CPU, 24 GB of unified memory, and 512 GB of storage. The most expensive configurations can reach up to $7,000.
author: The Verge

title: OpenAI launches Intelligent UI in ChatGPT, adding interactive visuals
content:
OpenAI has launched a new “Intelligent UI” feature for ChatGPT that lets the chatbot answer questions with interactive visuals. The update is rolling out to all users at the same time as GPT‑6.

The feature allows ChatGPT to combine a text response with diagrams, charts, forms, tappable buttons, and other visual elements. In a blog post, OpenAI explained that GPT‑6 was trained to generate interactive visuals instead of plain text and to format them correctly in its replies.

An example provided by OpenAI shows how ChatGPT could display a diagram of a seven‑speed bicycle when asked about its design, complete with interactive buttons that highlight differences.
summary: OpenAI is launching a new Intelligent UI feature in ChatGPT that lets the chatbot answer questions with interactive visuals such as diagrams, charts, forms, and tappable buttons. The update is rolling out to all users alongside GPT-6, and OpenAI trained GPT-6 to generate and format these visuals over text.
author: The Verge

title: Roku Pro Series OLED TVs up to $400 off during Prime Day, 55‑inch $699
content:
Roku’s new Pro Series OLED televisions are on sale during the final day of October Prime Day, with discounts of up to $400 off the list price. The 55‑inch model is listed at $699.99 on Amazon, a 30 percent reduction, while the 65‑inch version is $799.99, also a $400 discount.

Both sizes feature a native 120‑Hz refresh rate, four HDMI 2.1 ports for full‑refresh 4K gaming, and support for Dolby Vision and HDR10 Plus. Buyers receive a backlit Roku remote control with each television.

These are the lowest prices on OLED models reported for Prime Day, offering a budget option for consumers seeking high‑contrast picture quality for movies or gaming.
summary: The 55‑inch Pro Series OLED is $699.99 on Amazon, about 30 % off its list price. The 65‑inch model is $799.99, $400 off its list price, and both TVs have a native 120 Hz refresh rate, four HDMI 2.1 ports, Dolby Vision and HDR10 Plus support, and a backlit Roku remote.
author: The Verge

title: CTA Estimates Trump's Reshoring Push Could Cost Tech Firms $230 Billion
content:
Trade group CTA has estimated that President Donald Trump’s aggressive reshoring push could cost technology firms $230 billion.  

The estimate reflects the cost of a policy that would require 100% of technology to be made in the United States, according to CTA.
summary: The trade group CTA estimates that Trump's aggressive reshoring push could cost tech firms $230 billion. CTA's estimate highlights the significant financial impact of the policy.
author: Ars Technica

title: Jaguar Type 01 Debuts While Electric Ferrari Is Forgotten
content: Jaguar has unveiled its new Type 01 model, a move that has drawn attention amid a broader trend of heated online discussions about car design. The release comes at a time when electric vehicles (EVs) are particularly polarizing, with many enthusiasts and critics voicing strong opinions on the internet.
summary: The Jaguar Type 01 has debuted, but the electric Ferrari has been largely forgotten. Car design is causing controversy online, especially for electric vehicles.
author: Ars Technica

title: Fraudster jailed 18 months for AI bot scheme that outstreamed Taylor Swift, stealing $8M
content:
A fraudster was sentenced to 18 months in prison after a scheme that used 10,000 bots and AI-generated songs to outstream Taylor Swift and steal $8 million in music streaming royalties.

The scheme involved the use of bots and AI songs to manipulate streaming counts, resulting in the theft of $8 million in royalties.
summary: A man was sentenced to 18 months in prison for an AI scheme that used 10K bots and AI songs to outstream Taylor Swift. The scheme stole $8M in music streaming royalties.
author: Ars Technica

title: Pediatricians renew call to ban raw milk, cite heating benefits
content:
Pediatricians have renewed a call to ban raw milk amid concerns that anti‑science rhetoric is gaining traction. The push underscores the importance of pasteurization in protecting public health.

In a renewed policy, pediatricians review the benefits of heating milk to kill germs, highlighting the risks associated with consuming unpasteurized dairy.
summary: Pediatricians have renewed their call to ban raw milk. They review the benefits of heating milk to kill germs.
author: Ars Technica

title: Healthleap raises $38M, including $30M Series A led by Hummingbird Ventures
content:
Healthleap announced it has raised a total of $38 million to develop its artificial‑intelligence platform that identifies hospital patients who may require additional attention.

The funding round comprises an $8 million seed investment co‑led by Sequoia Capital and First Round Capital, followed by a $30 million Series A round led by Hummingbird Ventures.
summary: Healthleap raised $38 million to develop its AI that flags hospital patients who may need a closer look. The financing includes an $8 million seed round co-led by Sequoia Capital and First Round Capital and a $30 million Series A led by Hummingbird Ventures.
author: TechCrunch

title: Meta launches AI tools to detect ads linking to child sexual abuse material
content:
Meta announced the rollout of new artificial‑intelligence tools designed to identify advertisements that appear benign but secretly direct users to child sexual abuse material. The company said the tools were developed after it discovered such ads on its platforms.

The AI systems will scan ads for patterns that could lead users to harmful content hosted elsewhere on the internet, aiming to block the ads before they reach audiences. Meta indicated that the initiative targets the removal of covert pathways to illegal material.
summary: Meta has launched new AI tools to detect ads on its platforms that appear normal but may direct users to harmful content. The tools target ads that could lead to child sexual abuse material.
author: TechCrunch

title: CIA officer David Rush pleads guilty to fake program that stole over $190M and gold
content:
CIA officer David Rush admitted to creating a fake top‑secret government program that was used to steal more than $190 million, including gold bars.  

Rush, who had worked on highly sensitive intelligence programs, was caught siphoning money and gold through a fabricated government contract. He subsequently reached a plea deal with U.S. prosecutors.
summary: CIA officer David Rush, who worked on highly sensitive intelligence programs, admitted creating a fake top‑secret government program to steal money and gold bars. He reached a plea deal with U.S. prosecutors after being caught siphoning over $190 million and gold through the fake contract.
author: TechCrunch

title: Greenairy builds smart plant towers to clean office air
content:
Greenairy is developing “smart plant towers” designed to clean the air in office environments. The company says the towers use leafy greenery to address “stuffy, chemical‑infused office air.”

According to the announcement, the plant‑based system is intended to serve as a cure for indoor air quality problems by integrating living plants into a tower format. Greenairy’s solution targets the improvement of office air through natural filtration.
summary: Greenairy is building smart plant towers designed to clean the air in offices. The towers use leafy greenery to address stuffy, chemical‑infused office environments.
author: TechCrunch

title: X expands Gametime from NFL to include MLB as first new sport
content: X is expanding its Gametime feature, previously centered on the NFL, into a year‑round sports hub. The platform will now incorporate Major League Baseball content as the first step beyond football. X says additional professional leagues are slated to join the Gametime offering in the future.
summary: X is turning its NFL-focused Gametime feature into a year‑round sports destination. The expansion will start with MLB and later include other professional leagues.
author: TechCrunch

title: ChatGPT for Teens keeps teens engaged even during mental health crises
content:
ChatGPT for Teens, a version of the chatbot designed with safeguards for vulnerable users, has been found to keep teens engaged even during mental‑health crises.  

New testing indicates that, despite the intended protections, the AI continues to encourage ongoing conversation when users are in crisis and may foster unhealthy relationships with the technology.  

The findings highlight a tension between the platform’s safety goals and its actual impact on teen users.
summary: New testing shows ChatGPT’s teen safeguards still encourage continued engagement during crises. The findings also suggest the chatbot may foster unhealthy relationships with the AI.
author: TechCrunch

title: Meta's Muse AI assistant launches on iPad a month after mobile debut
content:
Meta has released its AI agent Muse for iPad, expanding the tool’s platform availability. The rollout comes just one month after Muse debuted on mobile devices.

The iPad launch is part of Meta’s rapid effort to broaden the assistant’s reach and integrate it across more hardware. Muse is now accessible to iPad users as the company continues to extend the service.
summary: Meta’s AI agent Muse is now available on iPad. The iPad release follows just a month after its mobile debut as Meta expands the assistant’s reach and integrations.
author: TechCrunch

title: Jaguar launches 5.2m Type 01 EV in New York, too long for UK parking
content:
Jaguar unveiled its new Type 01 electric vehicle in New York on Tuesday night, positioning the model toward younger American consumers.  

The Type 01 measures more than 5.2 metres in length and 2 metres in width, lacks a rear window, and is priced from £130,000 (approximately $172,000), with Jaguar targeting affluent buyers in the U.S. tech sector.  

Because of its dimensions, the vehicle will not fit into a standard UK parking space, underscoring its unsuitability for the British market.  

The launch marks the culmination of a two‑year rebrand for Jaguar.
summary: Jaguar unveiled its Type 01 electric vehicle in New York, a model over 5.2 metres long and 2 metres wide with no rear window. Priced from £130,000 ($172,000), it is aimed at rich tech industry buyers in the United States and will not fit in a UK parking space.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Mumsnet denies using AI after AI prompt posted on its forum
content:
Mumsnet has denied that it uses artificial intelligence to produce content after a detailed AI prompt was posted on one of its message boards. The prompt, which offered step‑by‑step instructions for an AI model to draft a response to a popular “am i being unreasonable” (AIBU) post, appeared in a thread where a user was seeking advice about a family dilemma involving a neurodivergent uncle and a sick child.

Members of the long‑established forum, known for its frank discussions of family tensions, rejected the site’s explanations and expressed frustration that the AI instructions were published publicly. Mumsnet maintains that it does not employ AI to generate forum content.
summary: Mumsnet denied using AI to produce content after a detailed AI prompt was posted on its message board. Users rejected the site’s explanations, saying they were vexed by the prompt that appeared in response to a post about a family dilemma involving a neurodivergent uncle and a sick child.
author: Guardian Technology

title: OpenAI releases over 370 mathematical results, prompting expert concerns
content:
OpenAI unveiled more than 370 new mathematical results on Tuesday, spanning areas such as algebra, theoretical computer science and mathematical logic. The release showcases the capabilities of the company’s most advanced artificial‑intelligence models.

However, leaders expressed concern that OpenAI has not performed sufficient due‑diligence to verify the findings and that its AI models remain inaccessible to the wider mathematical community. The criticism highlights worries that the results may not have been thoroughly vetted before publication.
summary: OpenAI published more than 370 mathematical results covering areas such as algebra, theoretical computer science and mathematical logic. Leaders said the company has not done sufficient due‑diligence to vet the findings and its AI models are not accessible to the broader mathematics community.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Russia rejects transparency demands, says tests show no epidemic risk in Siberia
content:
Russia has dismissed calls for greater transparency amid reports of a second plague case in Siberia. Rospotrebnadzor said that nearly 5,000 tests found no dangerous pathogens and that there was "no epidemic risk."

The Kremlin called most media reporting on the situation "false" and stated that it had no knowledge of a U.S. demarche formally requesting additional information.
summary: Rospotrebnadzor said nearly 5,000 tests found no dangerous pathogens and saw "no epidemic risk." The Kremlin called most media reporting "false" and said it had no knowledge of a US demarche formally requesting additional information.
author: Euronews

title: Nailympia London displays fantasy nail art inspired by folklore, forests and steampunk
content:
Fantasy nail art took center stage at Nailympia London, where artists transformed fingernails into miniature worlds. The competition featured designs inspired by folklore, forests and steampunk aesthetics.

Global participants competed to craft detailed, fantasy‑themed nail creations, turning each nail into a tiny, imaginative scene.
summary: Nailympia London showcased fantasy nail art inspired by folklore, forests and steampunk. Global artists raced to create miniature worlds on nails.
author: Euronews

title: Trump mocks Sheinbaum after she urges him not to rename Gulf of Mexico
content:
President Donald Trump mocked Mexican leader Sheinbaum after saying she called him to urge that the Gulf of Mexico not be renamed. In a public remark, Trump imitated an alleged response from Sheinbaum, saying, “No, no, please.”

Trump defended the proposed name change by citing coastal data, asserting that the available figures do not support keeping the current name.
summary: The US president said Mexican leader Sheinbaum called to ask him not to rename the Gulf of Mexico. He mocked her with a "No, no, please" imitation and justified the rename using coastal data that he said available figures do not support.
author: Euronews

title: Elephant seal appears on Rio's Copacabana beach, drawing crowds
content:
A southern elephant seal appeared unexpectedly on Rio de Janeiro’s Copacabana beach, attracting large crowds of visitors who took photos and shared the sight on social media.  

The unexpected guest drew significant attention, with beachgoers gathering to watch the seal and capture the moment on their devices.  

In response, officials erected barriers to protect the animal and manage the crowds.
summary: A southern elephant seal surprised Rio’s Copacabana beachgoers, drawing crowds, photos and social media buzz. Officials set up barriers to protect the animal.
author: Euronews

title: Southern right whales return to Hermanus, South Africa, attracting crowds
content:
Southern right whales have returned to Hermanus, South Africa, drawing crowds to the coastal cliffs and a local whale festival.  

Mothers are nursing newborn calves in Walker Bay as visitors gather to watch the seasonal visitors.  

The arrival of the whales is attracting large numbers of people to the area.
summary: Southern right whales have returned to Hermanus, South Africa. They are drawing crowds to the cliffs and whale festival as mothers nurse newborn calves in Walker Bay.
author: Euronews

title: Iranian authorities urge exiled singers to return as music fuels dissent
content:
Why music in Iran is more than just entertainment

Iranian authorities are trying to persuade prominent singers in exile to return home.  

While the state seeks to harness music as a political tool, music has also become a powerful expression of dissent and resistance.
summary: Iranian authorities are trying to persuade prominent singers in exile to return home. The state seeks to harness music as a political tool, and music has become a powerful expression of dissent and resistance.
author: DW World

title: European Commission proposes reforms to prepare EU for new members
content:
The European Commission has tabled a set of reforms aimed at preparing the European Union for future enlargement.  

The proposal includes earlier access to EU markets for candidate countries, new voting rules designed to reduce veto power, and additional safeguards for a larger bloc.  

The Commission’s plan raises questions about whether the reforms are fair and feasible.
summary: The European Commission is proposing earlier access to EU markets for candidate countries, new voting rules to reduce vetoes, and extra safeguards for a bigger bloc. The reform's fairness and feasibility are questioned.
author: DW World

title: Pakistan, Turkey agree practical measures to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks
content: Pakistan and Turkey have agreed to provide “practical measures” to defend Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks. The two countries’ commitment is part of a broader discussion about a potential Mecca defense pact that could alter the dynamics of the war in Yemen. The alliance’s impact on the conflict remains uncertain, as analysts weigh how the new support might shift the balance against the Houthis.
summary: Pakistan and Turkey have agreed to provide practical measures to defend Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks. The new alliance could reshape the war against the Houthis in Yemen.
author: DW World

title: Canada to indefinitely bar mental illness as sole reason for euthanasia
content:
Canada’s federal government announced on Wednesday that it will move forward with legislation to indefinitely bar people whose sole health condition is a mental illness from accessing physician‑assisted death. The proposal, driven by the ruling Liberal party, is intended to address a growing clash over eligibility for medical assistance in dying (MAID).

Under the current framework, individuals whose only underlying medical condition is a mental illness have already been prohibited from receiving MAID. That prohibition was slated to be lifted in March, but the issue has divided lawmakers who are debating whether to expand the MAID program to include such cases.

Crisis support resources are listed for those in need: Canada’s Crisis Services Canada can be reached at 1.833.456.4566 or by texting 45645 from 4 p.m. to 12 a.m. ET; the U.S. 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline is available at 988 or via chat at 988lifeline.org; the UK and Ireland Samaritans can be called toll‑free at 116 123; and Australia’s Lifeline is reachable at 13 11 14. Additional international helplines are available through Befrienders.org.
summary: Canada’s federal government will advance legislation to prevent people whose sole health condition is mental illness from accessing medical assistance in dying (Maid). The ruling Liberals say the move will address a clash over who can access physician‑assisted death.
author: Guardian World

title: Most Americans oppose Trump’s taxpayer‑funded “golden age” ads, poll finds
content:
A recent poll found that most Americans oppose President Donald Trump’s use of taxpayer money for his “golden age” political advertisements. The survey indicates widespread disapproval of the campaign’s funding strategy.

Trump has stated that he will cover the costs of future advertisements himself. In contrast, the White House has clarified that taxpayers will not be reimbursed for the expenses already incurred on past ads.
summary: A poll finds most Americans oppose Trump’s taxpayer‑funded “golden age” ads. Trump says he will pay for future ads, but the White House says taxpayers will not be reimbursed for past ones.
author: Al Jazeera

title: LSD returns to labs after history in psychiatry, counterculture, and CIA experiments
content:
LSD is reappearing in scientific research after a varied past that includes psychiatric studies, a prominent role in counterculture, and secret CIA mind‑control experiments.  

The hallucinogen’s early use in psychiatric research gave way to widespread adoption by the 1960s counterculture movement, while U.S. intelligence agencies conducted clandestine experiments aimed at manipulating behavior.  

Now, the substance is once again being examined in laboratory settings, signaling a renewed interest in its potential applications. LSD makes its way back to the lab.
summary: LSD has been involved in psychiatric research, counterculture, and secret CIA mind‑control experiments. It is now making its way back to the lab.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Saudi Arabia says Houthi airport attacks killed three foreign nationals
content:
Saudi Arabia said that Houthi attacks on airports resulted in the deaths of three foreign nationals. The ministry identified the victims as a Moroccan woman, an Algerian woman and a Sudanese national.

The Moroccan and Algerian women were killed in the city of Abha, while the Sudanese national died in Riyadh.
summary: Saudi Arabia said Houthi attacks on airports killed three foreign nationals. The victims were a Moroccan woman and an Algerian woman in Abha and a Sudanese national in Riyadh.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Kenya raises alert after first Ebola death, cites border screening concerns
content:
Kenya has placed the country on high alert after the first Ebola death was reported, prompting officials to step up preparedness measures. The government said it is intensifying its Ebola response amid growing concern that lapses in border screening may have contributed to the fatal case.

Authorities are focusing on strengthening screening procedures at points of entry and enhancing overall readiness to contain further transmission. The heightened vigilance reflects the government's effort to address the identified screening gaps and protect public health.
summary: Kenya’s government has intensified Ebola preparedness efforts. The move follows concern over lapses in border screening after the country’s first Ebola death.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Russia's massive overnight barrage kills at least 24 in Ukraine
content:
At least 24 people were killed as Russia launched a massive attack on Ukraine, Ukrainian officials said.

Ukraine reported that the overnight barrage included 130 drones, 48 cruise missiles and an unspecified number of ballistic missiles. The coordinated strike was described as massive by Ukrainian authorities.
summary: At least 24 people were killed as Russia launched a massive attack on Ukraine. Ukraine said the attack used 130 drones, 48 cruise missiles and ballistic missiles.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Rabbi Dov Lando's anti‑Zionist remarks spark Israel election controversy
content:
Rabbi Dov Lando’s anti‑Zionist remarks have ignited a row ahead of Israel’s election, drawing attention to deep‑seated disputes within the country’s political landscape.  

The rabbi’s comments have highlighted ongoing tensions over Zionism, the issue of conscription for ultra‑Orthodox Jews, and the role of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s ultra‑Orthodox allies in the coalition.
summary: Rabbi Dov Lando's anti‑Zionist remarks have stirred an Israel election row. His comments expose tensions over Zionism, conscription and Netanyahu's ultra‑Orthodox allies.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israelis demand accountability for 7 Oct failures, three years after attacks
content:
Israelis are calling for accountability over the failures surrounding the 7 October attacks, three years after the events.  

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has declined to assume personal responsibility for the incident and has refused to order a state inquiry.  

The demand for answers persists despite the prime minister’s refusal to initiate an official investigation.
summary: Israelis are demanding accountability for the failures of the 7 October attacks, three years after the events. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has refused to take personal responsibility or order a state inquiry.
author: BBC World

title: Goodbye Warner, hello Skydance: how will the major merger really impact Hollywood?
content:
Paramount and Warner Bros. have officially merged under the corporate umbrella of Skydance, reducing Hollywood’s major studio count from five to four. The deal, led by billionaire David Ellison, concluded after Skydance outbid Netflix for the century-old studio and overcame legal opposition. Skydance now joins Sony, Disney, and Universal as the remaining major players in the film industry.

The merger extends beyond film production to include the eventual combination of streaming services HBO Max and Paramount+, although no specific timeline has been provided. The combined entity now owns a vast array of television channels, including HBO, Showtime, CBS, MTV, Comedy Central, Cartoon Network, Nickelodeon, TNT, TBS, and CNN.

The inclusion of CNN has drawn particular scrutiny due to recent changes at CBS News, where Bari Weiss’s stewardship has been linked to declines in ratings and prestige for the program 60 Minutes. While Weiss is not expected to oversee CNN and current chair Mark Thompson remains in place, Skydance has stated that CNN will maintain editorial independence. However, concerns persist regarding an oversight board with Ellison appointees, especially given Ellison’s relationship with Donald Trump, who has frequently criticized CNN.
summary: After a windier road than expected, Paramount and Warner are now one, under the banner of Skydance, and the film industry is set for a shake-upHollywood’s big five have officially become the big four. Following a twist-filled saga that saw the century-old studio Warner Bros nearly acquired by the streaming giant Netflix, only to be outbid by Paramount owners Skydance, the company led by billionaire scion David Ellison.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Tom Pidcock furious after police motorbike hits two teammates at Tre Valli Varesine
content:
Tom Pidcock was furious after a police motorcyclist crashed into two of his teammates during the Tre Valli Varesine in Italy, saying he almost quit the race in a rage.  

The incident involved a police motorbike that was traveling the wrong way down the course and struck Pinarello‑Q36.5 riders Camprubí and Gloag, sending them floored in the crash. Pidcock described the event as something that “shouldn’t happen.”  

Despite the chaos, Pidcock finished second in the race. He attributed his frustration to the unexpected collision caused by the police motorcyclist.
summary: Tom Pidcock said he almost quit the Tre Valli Varesine after a police motorbike traveling the wrong way struck his Pinarello Q36.5 teammates Camprubí and Gloag. He finished second in the race.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Ronaldo says Jorge Jesus agreed to make eight points on his behalf
content:
Cristiano Ronaldo issued a lengthy statement on Tuesday asserting that Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus had agreed to present eight specific points regarding the player during a press conference before the national team’s match in Denmark last week. Ronaldo claimed he had approved a document outlining these points following a video meeting that included Jesus, his adviser Tiago Craveiro, and Al-Nassr sporting director Simão Coutinho.

The statement indicated that the “validated” notes covered various topics, with mentions made of Pelé, Maradona, loyalty, and selfies. Ronaldo described the process as one where he personally approved the content to be shared by the coach.
summary: Cristiano Ronaldo stated that Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus agreed to make eight points regarding him in a press conference before a game in Denmark. Ronaldo claimed he approved a document listing these points after a video meeting with Jesus, his adviser, and Al-Nassr's sporting director.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Pocognoli's Scotland start raises questions over flawed plan and third-place finish
content:
Scotland faces a potential third-place finish in Group B1 of the Nations League, a result that would impact their seeding for Euro 2028 qualifying. This outcome follows the first four matches under manager Sébastien Pocognoli, during which the team has not shown a "manager bounce."

Critics have noted that Ben Gannon-Doak is playing in an odd position while the wider tactical plan appears flawed. These performance issues have raised questions about the current system employed by the national team.
summary: Scotland are facing a third-place finish in Group B1 of the Nations League, which will impact their seeding for Euro 2028 qualifying. The article notes that there has been no new manager bounce under Sébastien Pocognoli and that the wider plan appears flawed.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Mikel Arteta signs four-year contract worth over £20m a season
content:
Mikel Arteta has signed a new four-year contract with Arsenal, a deal reportedly worth more than £20m a season that secures his position as the Premier League’s best-paid manager. The agreement extends his tenure at the club, potentially taking his reign beyond a decade if he fulfills the entire term.

The Spanish manager hailed the new deal as “only the beginning” of what he can achieve with the team. The significant pay rise follows his success in leading Arsenal to the league title last season, ending a 22-year wait for the club after three consecutive runner-up finishes.
summary: Mikel Arteta has signed a new four-year contract worth more than £20m a season, making him the best-paid manager in the Premier League. The deal secures his future at Arsenal following their title win after a 22-year wait.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Faf du Plessis questions Canada Super60 T10 format and tiny boundaries
content:
Faf du Plessis questioned the legitimacy of Canada’s “Super60” T10 cricket tournament, stating, “It doesn’t look like proper cricket.” The tournament took place in Vancouver, where players competed in a 50,000-seater stadium that was virtually empty. The event featured extremely short straight boundaries at BC Place, leading to controversial scoring situations, such as a ball traveling 35 meters off the edge of a bat.

During the competition, Mississauga Masters’ Ali Khan bowled a delivery that flew over Toronto Sixers batter Kieron Pollard’s head and crossed the lilliputian straight boundaries. Although the ball landed in the empty stands and was retrieved by a fielder, the shot was technically classified as a five, consisting of a wide plus four, because a six must be struck off the bat. The unusual conditions and sparse attendance have raised questions about the nature of the spectacle.
summary: Faf du Plessis stated that Canada's Super60 tournament does not look like proper cricket due to its extremely small boundaries. The T10 event in Vancouver featured a 50,000-seater stadium with very few spectators, raising questions about the format's spectacle.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Portuguese authorities took 83 days to inform Rui Pinto his witness protection was ending
content:
Portuguese authorities delayed notifying Manchester City whistleblower Rui Pinto for 83 days regarding the termination of his witness protection status, informing him only ten days before the measures were scheduled to expire. Documents reviewed by the Guardian indicate that the special security programmes commission (CPES), the body overseeing Portugal’s witness protection programme, kept Pinto uninformed of their decision for nearly three months.

The CPES convened on July 8 and 9 to evaluate Pinto’s case and determined that the threat level against him had dropped to low levels. Based on this assessment, the commission concluded that the special protection measures were no longer necessary, leading to the eventual end of his protected witness status.
summary: Portuguese authorities kept Rui Pinto unaware for almost three months that his witness protection status was ending, and they notified him only 10 days before it was due to expire. The special security programmes commission (CPES) met on 8 and 9 July, concluded the threat level against him was low, and determined that special protection measures were no longer warranted.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England faces Twickenham ticket sales slump as Springboks and All Blacks demand outstrips hosts
content:
England is facing a slump in ticket sales for the Nations Championship finals at Twickenham, as demand for matches involving South Africa and New Zealand has outstripped interest in the hosts. This development represents an embarrassing snub for Steve Borthwick’s side, particularly following their 42-21 loss to Ireland in their previous game at the stadium.

The finals weekend will feature six ranking matches at Twickenham next month, with two games scheduled for each day from Friday through Sunday. This event marks the culmination of the competition’s first edition, concluding with a grand finale on Sunday that pits the top nation from the Northern Hemisphere pool against their southern counterparts. The remaining fixtures will match the second-place teams against each other, followed by the third-place teams.
summary: Demand for tickets to the Springboks and All Blacks matches has outstripped that for the host England team during the Nations Championship finals. This ticket sales slump is described as an embarrassing snub for Steve Borthwick’s side following their 42-21 loss to Ireland in the last Twickenham game.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Tom Pidcock angry after teammates hit by police vehicle at Tre Valli Varesine
content: Tom Pidcock expressed his anger and stated he wanted to "stop racing" after two of his team-mates were struck by a police vehicle at the Tre Valli Varesine. The incident occurred when the police vehicle was travelling the wrong way down the race course.
summary: Tom Pidcock said he wanted to stop racing after two teammates were hit by a police vehicle. The vehicle was traveling the wrong way down the course at the Tre Valli Varesine.
author: BBC Sport

title: Senior English Figures Fear Manchester City Could Play Champions League After Relegation
content:
Senior figures in English football have expressed concern that Manchester City could still qualify for the Champions League next season, even if the club is relegated for breaching financial regulations.  

The worry centers on the possibility that the club might be allowed to compete in Europe despite being demoted from the Premier League due to the regulatory breach.
summary: Senior figures in English football are worried that Manchester City could qualify for the Champions League next season. This could happen even if the club is relegated due to breaching financial regulations.
author: BBC Sport

title: Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan's execution scheduled for December 3
content: Nidal Malik Hasan, convicted of killing 13 people in the 2009 Fort Hood mass shooting, is scheduled for execution in December, the U.S. Army announced. A memo released on Tuesday, obtained by NewsNation, specifies the date and time as December 3 at 1 p.m. CDT. The execution will be carried out at Fort Hood.
summary: The U.S. Army has scheduled the execution of Nidal Malik Hasan for December 3 at 1 p.m. CDT. Hasan was convicted of killing 13 people in the 2009 Fort Hood mass shooting.
author: The Hill

title: Sarri Singer Calls for Global Action on Terrorism at Oct. 7 Attack's Third Anniversary
content:
On the third anniversary of the Oct. 7 attacks, author Sarri Singer highlighted the continued global indifference to terrorism. In his commentary, Singer argues that the world must confront the universal threat of terrorism by acknowledging it for what it is.

Singer calls for three specific actions: first, to label terrorism accurately; second, to cut off funding to enemy groups; and third, to treat survivor recovery as a matter of national security. He stresses that these steps are essential for addressing the problem on a global scale.
summary: Sarri Singer highlighted the third anniversary of the Oct. 7 attacks, urging the global community to confront terrorism. He called for cutting off enemy funding and treating survivor recovery as a matter of national security.
author: The Hill

title: What should teachers teach about the October 7 attacks?
content:
What should teachers teach about the October 7 attacks?

A recent commentary reflects on the challenges of teaching about the October 7 attacks. After three years of listening to how we should teach October 7, the author notes that critics consistently fail to accommodate the complexity of the conflict. The piece underscores the difficulty of presenting a nuanced perspective in educational settings.
summary: After three years of listening to how we should teach October 7, what always strikes me is critics’ utter inability to accommodate the complexity of the conflict.
author: The Hill

title: Tillis defends insults in memoir toward Trump officials
content:
Sen. Thom Tillis (R‑NC) defended the harsh remarks he made in his new memoir, saying he stands “by all that.”  The comments, which target Trump administration officials, were read by CNN’s Kaitlan Collins during a Tuesday segment.

Tillis’s book, titled How to Lose Friends and Antagonize Presidents, contains “unsparing” remarks, beginning with a reference to his vote to confirm Defense Secretary Pete.
summary: Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N. C.) defended insults he made in his new memoir toward Trump administration officials. He said he stands by all that, as CNN’s Kaitlan Collins read his unsparing remarks from “How to Lose Friends and Antagonize Presidents,” including his vote to confirm Defense Secretary Pete.
author: The Hill

title: OpenAI releases 377 new math breakthroughs on Tuesday
content:
OpenAI announced on Tuesday the release of a new batch of mathematics breakthroughs. The company issued 377 results that span physics, mathematics, and other scientific problems.

The breakthroughs were produced by an internal frontier model that is not yet available to the public. The release follows calls from AI researchers and developers to slow the growth of the technology.

The announcement included the statement: “Towards acceleration of scientific…”.
summary: OpenAI released a new batch of mathematics breakthroughs on Tuesday. The company released 377 results that cover different physics, mathematical and other scientific problems solved by an internal frontier model not yet available to the public.
author: The Hill

title: Vance says Iran must make meaningful enrichment reduction to end war
content:
Vice President Kamala Vance told Reuters on Tuesday that Iran must take a “meaningful” step concerning its stockpile of enriched uranium to move forward in nuclear negotiations with the United States.  

Vance said a reduction in Iran’s enrichment activities is essential for progress, noting that Iran’s claim of a right to enrichment remains a key sticking point in talks over its nuclear program.
summary: Vice President Vance told Reuters on Tuesday that Iran must take a meaningful step concerning its enriched uranium stockpile to advance nuclear negotiations with the United States. He said Iran’s claim of a right to enrichment is a key sticking point in the talks.
author: The Hill

title: Rand Paul warns Russian plague research could be weaponized
content:
Sen. Rand Paul (R‑Ky.) has voiced concerns that Russia could be conducting biological weapons research involving the plague, following the mysterious death of a worker at a Siberian laboratory.  

The 28‑year‑old worker died on Oct. 2 after being hospitalized with a severe case of pneumonia.  

Global health officials are seeking more information about the death, prompting the World.
summary: Sen. Rand Paul (R-Ky.) expressed concern that Russia may be conducting biological weapons research involving the plague. These concerns arose after a 28-year-old worker at a Siberian lab died on Oct. 2 from a severe case of pneumonia.
author: The Hill

title: Complex candidate and potential blue wave threaten Nevada's safe red House seat
content:
Northern Nevada’s congressional seat has long been a reliably red district, represented by a Republican since the district was drawn in the early 1980s. The seat’s history reflects a consistent pattern of Republican dominance in the region.

This year, however, the race has become competitive. A complicated candidate and a potential blue wave could change that, putting the district’s long‑standing partisan alignment at risk.
summary: Northern Nevada has a reliably red congressional seat represented by a Republican since the early 1980s. A complicated candidate and a potential blue wave this year could change that.
author: NPR Politics

title: Widdecombe suspect accused of trying to break into Farage's home
content:
Joshua Kerry, 28, has been accused of attempting to break into the home of Nigel Farage. The suspect, linked to the Widdecombe incident, appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court to face the charges.

Following his court appearance, Kerry was remanded in custody.
summary: Joshua Kerry, 28, appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court and was remanded in custody.
author: BBC Politics

title: Heatstroke ruined his health. Years before, it took the life of another farm worker at the same company
content:
Farm labor contractor Carlos Vargas Moreno and other workers on H-2A agricultural visas were exposed to hazardous heat conditions while weeding a watermelon field in Goldsboro, North Carolina, on July 19, 2022. The workday began at 7:00 a.m. and continued until 4:00 p.m., during which the temperature reached 90°F (32°C) and the heat index hit 98.3°F. Workers took two 15-minute breaks and ate a one-hour lunch outdoors, conditions that the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (Osha) and the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (Niosh) heat safety app defines as “hazardous” for outdoor laborers.

The contractor is accused of exposing laborers to heat-related health hazards that ruined the health of one worker and previously took the life of another farm worker at the same company. Despite these incidents, the company continues to bring hundreds of migrant farm workers to North Carolina.
summary: A farm labor contractor exposed laborers on H-2A agricultural visas to heat-related health hazards, but is still bringing hundreds of migrant farm workers to North CarolinaIt was 4pm and 90F (32C) when Carlos Vargas Moreno and other farm workers set out to weed a watermelon field in Goldsboro, North Carolina, on 19 July 2022. The work day had begun at 7am and included two 15-minute breaks and a one-hour lunch eaten outdoors.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Curtin Study Finds Nearly Half of Concussion Patients Still Suffering After One Year
content:
A new study from Curtin University indicates that nearly 50% of individuals who suffer a concussion continue to experience issues one year after the injury. The research also identified specific factors that place patients at the highest risk for developing long-term symptoms.

Mental health conditions and sleep disorders were highlighted as key risk factors contributing to the persistence of these symptoms.
summary: A new Curtin University study found that almost half of people who experience a concussion still have problems a year later. The study also identified factors that put patients at greatest risk for long-term symptoms.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Flu Cases Rise in U.S., Early 2026‑27 Season Expected in West
content: Health authorities have warned that the 2026–27 flu season may be beginning early in some western regions of the United States. This alert coincides with a reported increase in the number of people sick with the flu across the country.
summary: Flu illness is rising across the United States. Health authorities warn that the 2026‑27 flu season may start early in some western regions.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Invention and community engagement help children with autism enjoy music
content:
An invention and community engagement are helping children with autism enjoy music, according to a recent report.  

The invention enables a performer to cue an instrument to begin playing onstage with the wave of a hand or press of a button, creating a more interactive concert experience.
summary: An invention and community engagement help children with autism enjoy music. The invention allows a user to cue an instrument to begin playing onstage with a wave of a hand or a press of a button.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Review links adipocyte ferroptosis to inflammation in obesity
content:
A new review examines adipocyte ferroptosis, the breakdown of fat cells due to oxidation from intracellular iron. The review identifies this process as an emerging molecular mechanism that may contribute to adipose tissue dysfunction.

The authors suggest that iron‑induced oxidation of fat cells can trigger chronic inflammation and metabolic complications associated with obesity. The review highlights the role of ferroptosis in the development of obesity‑related health issues.
summary: A new review examines adipocyte ferroptosis, the breakdown of fat cells due to oxidation from intracellular iron. It proposes this mechanism may contribute to adipose tissue dysfunction, chronic inflammation, and metabolic complications associated with obesity.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Heart disease mortality gaps persist across U.S. counties despite overall decline
content:
Heart disease mortality rates in the United States have continued to decline overall, but significant gaps remain. A county‑by‑cause‑by‑population analysis published in the Journal of the American College of Cardiology found that disparities based on race, ethnicity and geographic location persist.

The study shows that while national cardiovascular disease mortality has fallen, the variation in death rates is far greater from one county to another than it is from one state to another. This indicates that local factors continue to drive unequal outcomes in heart disease across the country.
summary: A county‑by‑cause analysis in the Journal of the American College of Cardiology found that cardiovascular disease mortality has declined overall in the U.S. However, disparities by race, ethnicity, and place persist, with county‑level mortality varying far more than state‑level.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Gene expression linked to survival differs by kidney cancer subtype
content:
Gene expression linked to survival differs by kidney cancer subtype

Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is the most common form of kidney cancer, accounting for about 90 % of kidney cancers. It develops when abnormal cells in the kidney's small tubules begin to grow uncontrollably. RCC has several subtypes that differ in their origin, molecular characteristics and genetic makeup.
summary: Renal cell carcinoma accounts for about 90% of kidney cancers and arises from abnormal growth in the kidney's small tubules. The disease has several subtypes that vary in origin, molecular characteristics, and genetic makeup.
author: Medical Xpress

title: WHO warns against obesity drugs for children under 10
content:
The World Health Organization has released new global guidelines that caution against the use of obesity drugs for children under the age of ten.  

The guidelines state that care should focus on healthy eating and exercise rather than medicines such as weight‑loss injections.
summary: The World Health Organization says care should focus on healthy eating and exercise. It warns against medicines such as weight‑loss injections for children under 10.
author: BBC Health

title: McDonald's sued for using AI tool to set franchise pricing
content:
McDonald’s is facing a federal lawsuit alleging that it used an artificial‑intelligence tool to set prices across its independently owned franchises.  

The suit claims the AI tool allows those franchises to exchange nonpublic price and sales information, a practice prosecutors say violates antitrust laws and has unfairly inflated menu prices for consumers.  

Most McDonald’s restaurants in the United States are independently owned and are said to set prices individually under company policy. Antitrust laws require businesses to set prices independently from their competitors, as coordinating prices can stifle competition and raise costs for consumers.  

The case is currently pending in federal court.
summary: A federal lawsuit accuses McDonald’s of using an AI tool to set prices for its independently owned U.S. franchises, allegedly violating antitrust laws and inflating menu prices. The suit claims the tool enables franchises to share nonpublic price and sales information, contrary to company policy that requires independent price setting.
author: Guardian Business

title: Trump’s Iowa Steel Plant Project Faces Doubts Over Delivery
content:
Skepticism mires Trump’s Iowa steel plant project: ‘Promises are not the same as jobs’

The Trump administration’s announcement of a $15 billion steel plant in Lee County, Iowa, has raised doubts about whether the project will be built and delivered as promised. Critics point to the president’s record on steel policy as a source of concern.

Trump has long portrayed himself as a “man of steel,” from White House photoshopping him to look like Superman to enacting steel tariffs and approving the sale of US Steel to Japan’s Nippon Steel, which included a “golden” share for the U.S. government. The new plant is to be built by India‑based Mesabi Metallics, but questions remain over the feasibility of the project.

The project’s viability is under scrutiny, with observers questioning whether the promised jobs and production will materialize.
summary: The Trump administration plans to build the largest U.S. steel plant, a $15bn facility in Lee County, Iowa, by India-based Mesabi Metallics. Critics question whether the plant will be built and delivered as promised, citing Trump’s record.
author: Guardian Business

title: Drought cuts wheat harvest in 2026 and raises dairy farmers' costs
content:
Drought conditions have sharply reduced farm output, with wheat harvests in 2026 falling far below previous levels and dairy producers confronting higher operating costs.  

The lower wheat yields and rising expenses for dairy farms illustrate the dual pressure on agricultural producers, highlighting the broader impact of the drought on the sector.
summary: Drought led to a much smaller wheat harvest in 2026. It also caused dairy farmers' expenses to increase.
author: BBC Business

title: Penguin poop fertilizes snow algae blooms, speeding Antarctic melt
content:
A new study indicates that penguin droppings are fertilizing snow algae blooms along the Antarctic Peninsula, resulting in dense green algae patches along the coastline. These nutrient-rich deposits sustain the growth of the algae in the snow.

The expanding areas of green snow melt more rapidly than clean, white snow. This accelerated melting process potentially speeds up the spread of snow- and ice-free areas across Antarctica.
summary: Penguin poop fertilizes snow algae blooms along the Antarctic Peninsula, feeding dense green algae patches along the coastline. These expanding stretches of green snow melt faster than clean, white snow, potentially speeding up the spread of snow‑and ice‑free areas of Antarctica.
author: Phys.org

title: ICC approves trial of pink balls in Tests affected by bad light
content:
The International Cricket Council (ICC) approved a trial of pink balls in Test matches in June this year, targeting games expected to be affected by poor lighting conditions. The use of the pink ball is subject to prior agreement from both participating teams.

This development builds on the introduction of the pink ball for day-night matches more than a decade ago.
summary: The International Cricket Council approved a trial of pink balls in Test matches expected to be affected by bad light. This trial is subject to prior agreement from both teams.
author: Phys.org

title: Techno-optimistic scientists take fewer climate actions, study finds
content:
A recent study indicates that scientists holding techno-optimistic views regarding climate change are less likely to take personal action to address the issue. Specifically, researchers who believe technology will largely solve climate-related problems are 23% less likely to engage in civic climate action than those who disagree with this perspective.

Additionally, the study found that these techno-optimistic scientists are 18% less likely to make high-impact lifestyle changes compared to their counterparts who do not hold this belief.
summary: Scientists who believe technology will largely solve climate change problems are 23% less likely to engage in civic climate action. They are also 18% less likely to make high-impact lifestyle changes compared with scientists who disagree with this belief.
author: Phys.org

title: New framework guides relocation of endangered species outside historical range
content: A new framework aimed at guiding the decision to move endangered species outside their historical ranges to prevent extinction has been published in the journal Conservation Science and Practice. This development marks the conclusion of a multiyear, Pacific-wide initiative. The University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa served as a central supporting participant in this effort.
summary: A new framework to guide the decision to move endangered species outside their historical range was published in Conservation Science and Practice. The multiyear Pacific-wide effort, in which the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa played a central supporting role, produced the framework.
author: Phys.org

title: OpenAI Releases Hundreds of Mathematical Papers Simultaneously
content:
OpenAI announced that it has released 722 mathematical discoveries in a single batch, a move that has surprised the mathematical community.

The announcement follows the company’s simultaneous release of hundreds of papers, underscoring AI’s growing capability in mathematics.

Mathematicians have expressed astonishment at the scale and speed of the new findings.
summary: OpenAI released hundreds of papers at once, showcasing its growing mathematical capabilities. The simultaneous release surprised mathematicians.
author: New Scientist

title: NASA Measures Earth’s Center of Mass Shifts
content:
Earth’s center of mass is constantly on the move, shifting by a few millimeters as enormous amounts of water, ice, and even air migrate around the planet with the seasons.  

NASA scientists have developed a more precise way to track these tiny swings using laser‑range satellites, GPS data, and measurements of how water and ice deform Earth’s crust.
summary: Earth’s center of mass shifts by a few millimeters as water, ice, and air move seasonally. NASA scientists have developed a precise method using laser‑range satellites, GPS data, and measurements of how water and ice deform Earth’s crust.
author: Science Daily

title: Webb finds atmosphere on scorching lava world HD 3167 b
content:
The James Webb Space Telescope has found strong evidence that the rocky lava world HD 3167 b possesses an atmosphere, even though the planet orbits its star every 24 hours under extreme heat.  

The discovery is surprising because HD 3167 b is a hot, rocky planet that was expected to lose its atmosphere.  Scientists say the finding could help them understand how rocky planets retain atmospheres and what the young, molten Earth may once have looked like.
summary: The James Webb Space Telescope has found strong evidence that the rocky lava world HD 3167 b has an atmosphere, despite circling its star every 24 hours under extreme heat. The discovery could help scientists understand how rocky planets retain atmospheres and what the young, molten Earth may once have looked like.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists reprogram immune cells inside the body to fight cancer
content:
Scientists at UC San Francisco have developed a method to generate cancer‑fighting CAR‑T cells directly inside the body, potentially bypassing the slow and expensive process of removing, engineering, and reinfusing a patient’s immune cells.  

The researchers used a two‑particle delivery system to send CRISPR gene‑editing tools and new cancer‑targeting DNA specifically into T cells. The DNA was inserted at a precise location in the genome, creating the engineered CAR‑T cells in situ.  

This in‑body approach could avoid the current ex‑vivo manufacturing steps required for CAR‑T therapy.
summary: Scientists at UC San Francisco have developed a way to create cancer-fighting CAR-T cells directly inside the body, potentially avoiding the slow and extremely expensive process of removing, engineering, and reinfusing a patient’s immune cells. Using a two-particle delivery system, the researchers sent CRISPR gene-editing tools and new cancer-targeting DNA specifically into T cells, where the DNA was inserted at a precise location in the genome.
author: Science Daily

title: Zoo lions show wild behavior after switching to whole carcasses
content:
Scientists at a zoo altered the feeding routine for their lions by providing whole carcasses on a feast‑and‑fast schedule. The change appeared to bring out more natural behavior.  

Under the new regimen, the lions spent nearly three times longer feeding than before. They also engaged in more tearing and manipulating of food and rested more heavily after meals. During the fasting period, their activity increased gradually, closely resembling the rhythm seen in wild lions.
summary: Zoo lions fed whole carcasses on a feast-and-fast schedule spent nearly three times longer feeding, tore and manipulated food more, and rested heavily after meals. Their activity then increased gradually during the fasting period, closely resembling the rhythm seen in wild lions.
author: Science Daily

title: Sugar intake during antibiotics linked to gut microbiome disruption
content:
Eating more sugar while taking antibiotics was linked to greater disruption of the gut microbiome and increased growth of potentially harmful bacteria.  

Researchers suggest that temporarily cutting back on sweets during and after antibiotic treatment could be a simple way to reduce this damage, though clinical trials are still needed.
summary: Eating more sugar while taking antibiotics was linked to greater disruption of the gut microbiome and increased growth of potentially harmful bacteria. Researchers suggest temporarily cutting back on sweets during and after antibiotic treatment could reduce this damage, though clinical trials are still needed.
author: Science Daily

title: James Webb Telescope detects debris indicating Mars‑sized planetary collisions
content:
NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope is giving astronomers a glimpse of the violent collisions that may have shaped our own solar system, including the giant impact that created the Moon.  

By studying 21 rare “extreme debris disks” around young stars, researchers found that the dust in these disks can reveal the scale and intensity of planetary collisions.  

The findings show how the dust produced in such collisions can be used to infer the dynamics of planetary impacts.
summary: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope studied 21 extreme debris disks around young stars to observe signs of violent planetary collisions. The dust in these disks suggests impacts involving Mars‑sized worlds, akin to the giant impact thought to have created the Moon.
author: Science Daily

title: Russian lab worker Darya Shipilova dies after plague centre accident
content:
A 28‑year‑old laboratory worker, Darya Shipilova, died after falling ill at a plague research centre in Siberia. The incident followed a reported accident at the facility, prompting quarantine measures in several hospitals in eastern Russia.

Russia’s health watchdog has stated that Shipilova died of “pneumonia of unknown aetiology.”  Despite this official cause, there is speculation that the worker may have contracted a plague infection.

Lucy Hough spoke to Science Weekly co‑host Madeleine Finlay about the incident.
summary: Quarantine measures have been in place in several hospitals in eastern Russia after 28‑year‑old laboratory worker Darya Shipilova died following a reported accident at a plague research centre in Siberia. Russia’s health watchdog said she died of pneumonia of unknown aetiology, though speculation about a plague infection exists.
author: Guardian Science

title: Karl Deisseroth shares Nobel medicine prize win with family after making school lunches
content:
Stanford University released a video showing Karl Deisseroth informing his two daughters and one son that he has been awarded the Nobel Prize in Medicine. The 54-year-old scientist, who shares the honor with two researchers in Germany, was recognized for his contributions to optogenetics, a field that uses light and genes to control neurons in living brains.

Following the announcement, Deisseroth spent hours on Monday receiving congratulatory calls. Despite the high-profile recognition, he paused to prepare school lunches for his children, who were asleep in the family home in Stanford. This domestic task occurred while he had been speaking with journalists and well-wishers in the middle of the night.
summary: Stanford University shared a video of Karl Deisseroth telling his children he won the Nobel Prize in medicine for his work in optogenetics. The scientist shared the award with two researchers in Germany for research that uses light to control neurons in living brains.
author: Guardian Science

title: Francis Halzen wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for IceCube neutrino work
content:
The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to Francis Halzen.  

Halzen, a Belgian physicist, received the prize for his work on the IceCube detector, which observes ghostly particles called neutrinos. The detector uses sensors buried in the ice to detect these extraterrestrial particles.  

Science editor Ian Sample explained to host Madeleine Finlay how Halzen conceived the idea of using ice‑borne sensors to detect neutrinos.
summary: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to Belgian physicist Francis Halzen. He received the prize for his work on the IceCube detector, which observes neutrinos in the ice.
author: Guardian Science

title: Study links post-war sugar rationing to long-term health effects
content:
Research suggests that the first 1,000 days of sugar exposure may leave a lasting mark on health, affecting factors such as blood pressure and aging. This potential long-term impact is being examined in the generation born in Britain during the post-war recovery period, a time when many everyday foods, including sugar, remained subject to strict rationing.

During this era, adults were limited to approximately 3 tablespoons (40g) of sugar per day, while children were restricted to less than a tablespoon. Infants and very young children were expected to consume little to no added sugar. These restrictions were lifted in stages beginning in 1953, with limits on sweets and chocolate removed in February and general sugar rationing ending in September. By the second half of 1954, average sugar consumption in the country had nearly doubled.
summary: Research suggests that sugar exposure during the first 1,000 days of life may leave a decades-long mark on health indicators like blood pressure and aging. British sugar rationing ended in 1953, leading to average consumption almost doubling by late 1954.
author: Guardian Science

title: Nobel Prize in Chemistry Awarded to Kagan and Soai for Mirror-Image Molecule Discovery
content:
The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to Henri B Kagan of Paris-Sud University in France and Kensō Soai of Tokyo University of Science in Japan. The prize recognized their discovery of nonlinear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis, which demonstrated how chemical reactions can produce an overwhelming excess of one of two mirror-image forms of a molecule.

This scientific breakthrough has aided the understanding of how medicines work in the body.
summary: Henri B Kagan of Paris‑Sud University and Kensō Soai of Tokyo University of Science received the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for discovering nonlinear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis. Their discovery showed how chemical reactions can produce an overwhelming excess of one of two mirror‑image forms of a molecule, aiding understanding of how medicines work in the body.
author: Guardian Science

content:

The report notes that drugmakers, including Eli Lilly, are exploring this potential effect.

title: OpenAI’s New Agent Dots Aims to Automate Online Tasks, Including Buying Furniture
content:
OpenAI has announced a new always‑on agent that it claims can manage a wide range of online tasks, from purchasing furniture to completing routine web interactions. The company describes the agent, referred to as “Dots,” as a tool designed to automate tasks that normally require human input.

In an early user test, the agent demonstrated some limitations. The always‑on agent was described as buggy and was unable to solve a captcha during the trial. This issue highlights challenges in the agent’s current ability to handle all aspects of online interactions.

The release of Dots marks a step toward OpenAI’s goal of creating agents that can run users’ digital lives, though early feedback indicates further development is needed to ensure reliable performance.
summary: Dots is designed to automate online tasks, such as buying furniture. In my initial experience, the always‑on agent was buggy and could not complete a captcha.

title: Ring’s first smart lock can be charged by turning a dial when the battery unexpectedly dies
content:
Amazon has unveiled its first smart lock that eliminates the need for a physical backup key when the rechargeable battery runs out while you are away. The new Ring Smart Lock uses a built‑in charger integrated into its thumb‑turn dial, allowing the lock to be powered by a few turns of the dial. According to Amazon, this action generates enough energy to unlock the door and fully recharge the battery.

Unlike other smart locks that rely on hidden USB ports or metal contacts to connect a 9‑volt battery, the Ring Smart Lock’s dial‑charger offers a more convenient solution. The device is expected to be available in the United States sometime.
summary: Amazon announced its first smart lock that eliminates the need for a physical backup key should its rechargeable battery die while you're away from home. While other smart locks lean on hidden USB ports or metal contacts for connecting a 9-volt battery to replenish a dead battery, the new Ring Smart Lock incorporates a more convenient charger right into its thumb-turn dial.

title: Thatcherism via the Walkman: Stuart Hall’s British cultural studies preserved online
content:
A major digital archive of Stuart Hall’s previously unpublished papers, notebooks, recordings and videos has been launched to celebrate the “incredible contributions” the Jamaica‑born sociologist made to Britain’s culture, according to the project lead.

Hall was a public intellectual who coined the term Thatcherism and, in 1985, warned of the dangers of “authoritarian populism.” His obituary in The Guardian described him as “among the first to identify key questions of the age” and noted he was a seminal figure in postwar Black British history. He died in 2014 at the age of 82.
summary: Project lead says it celebrates ‘incredible contributions’ Jamaica-born sociologist made to Britain’s cultureWhether it was Thatcherism, populism or the story of the Sony Walkman, Stuart Hall was a public intellectual famed for defining the times. Now a major digital archive of his previously unpublished papers, notebooks, recordings and videos has been launched.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Pornhub Returns to Australia After Age-Verification Implementation
content:
Pornhub has resumed service for Australian adults after the site’s parent company, Aylo, introduced an age‑checking system on Apple devices. The move follows legal requirements that adult websites verify users are 18 or older or face potential fines of $49.5 million.

In March, Aylo blocked Australian users when online safety codes mandated such verification. With the new age‑checking feature in place, Australian adults can now access the world’s most popular porn site again.
summary: Australian adults can access Pornhub again after the site introduced age checking on Apple devices. Aylo blocked Australian users in March when online safety codes required adult sites to verify users were 18 or older or risk fines of $49.5m.
