title: Finnish regulator orders Google to halt work on two northern datacentres
content:
Google has been ordered to temporarily halt construction on two data‑centre sites in Finland after failing to complete required environmental impact assessments. The order follows a review that found the company did not carry out the necessary environmental studies for its projects.

The affected sites are in Muhos and Kajanni, and are part of a €13 billion (£11 billion) project that spans multiple locations in northern Finland. The initiative reflects the growing demand for space to house online infrastructure.
summary: Google has been ordered to temporarily stop work on datacentres in Muhos and Kajanni after failing to complete required environmental impact assessments. The sites are part of a €13 billion project to build multiple datacentres in northern Finland.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Australian privacy regulator investigates Shenzhen Qingcheng over Kmart HeyCyan smartglasses app
content:
The Australian privacy regulator has opened an investigation into Shenzhen Qingcheng, the China‑based software company that created the HeyCyan app used in Kmart’s $89 smartglasses.

The regulator’s commissioner said Shenzhen Qingcheng failed to respond to her inquiries about the app, which is embedded in the Anko‑branded discount version of Meta’s smartglasses that can capture images and record high‑definition video. In August, Guardian Australia reported that Kmart had sold out of the glasses, prompting public outrage over their covert use and calls to ban or restrict the devices.

The investigation is now underway.
summary: The Australian privacy regulator has opened an investigation into Shenzhen Qingcheng, the China‑based software company behind the HeyCyan app in Kmart’s $89 smartglasses. The commissioner said the company failed to respond to her inquiries after public outrage over the devices’ covert image and video capture capabilities.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Police in England and Wales often fail to investigate revenge porn complaints, research shows
content:
Lawyers have filed a super‑complaint after research showed that police forces in England and Wales often fail to investigate reports of image‑based abuse, formerly known as “revenge pornography”.  

The study, which compiled evidence from 100 individuals whose intimate images were shared online without consent, found that many complaints are dismissed or not recognised as criminal offences.  

The findings have prompted the super‑complaint to challenge the handling of such cases, a matter highlighted by former prime minister Keir Starmer, who called image‑based abuse a national emergency.
summary: Research using evidence from 100 people shows officers in England and Wales frequently dismiss or do not recognise image‑based abuse complaints. The findings have led lawyers to launch a super‑complaint, noting the issue despite former prime minister Keir Starmer calling it a national emergency.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Drones considered for cloud seeding as countries seek more rainfall
content:
Cloud seeding is attracting interest as nations seek ways to increase rainfall, according to recent reports. The emerging technology under consideration involves the use of drones to disperse seeding agents into clouds.

Industry observers are questioning whether drones can effectively enhance cloud‑seeding efforts, prompting further investigation into their potential role in boosting precipitation.
summary: Cloud seeding is gaining attention as countries look to boost rainfall. The piece raises the question of whether drones could assist in cloud seeding.
author: BBC Technology

title: Trump to discuss plague with Putin as Russia downplays outbreak fears
content:
President Donald Trump is set to discuss the plague with Russian President Vladimir Putin as Moscow downplays concerns about an outbreak. The Kremlin said it welcomed the offer for talks.

Russia’s health watchdog added that Moscow is “ready to assist the US in tackling infectious disease outbreaks,” while the World Health Organization has asked Russia for additional information.
summary: The Kremlin welcomed Trump's offer to discuss the plague with Putin. Russia's health watchdog said Moscow was ready to assist the US in tackling infectious disease outbreaks as the WHO asked Russia for additional information.

title: Tokyo sleep competition offers ¥2 million prize to best sleeper
content:
A sleep competition held in Tokyo and organized by the company Koala offered a prize of ¥2 million to the participant judged the best sleeper.  

The event was presented as a commentary on Japan’s long‑hours work culture and the resulting sleep deprivation affecting many workers.
summary: A sleep competition in Tokyo organized by Koala offered a prize of ¥2 million to the best sleeper. The event highlighted Japan’s long‑hours work culture and sleep deprivation.

title: Scientists identify nose‑less ancient Egyptian crocodile, linking it to the Great Sphinx
content:
Scientists have identified an ancient Egyptian crocodile whose skull is missing its nose, a feature the researchers say resembles the Great Sphinx.

The skull, discovered nearly a century ago, was examined by Egyptian and European researchers who used it to revise a portion of the crocodile family tree. Their analysis sheds new light on the prehistoric wildlife that once inhabited the Mediterranean region and highlights an unexpected link to the iconic Sphinx.
summary: Egyptian and European researchers used a skull found nearly a century ago to identify an ancient Egyptian crocodile whose nose is missing, like the Great Sphinx. The find prompted a revision of part of the crocodile family tree and sheds light on Mediterranean prehistoric wildlife.
author: Euronews

title: Iran parliament passes bill criminalising interviews with hostile foreign media
content:
Iran’s parliament approved a bill that would criminalise interviews with foreign media outlets designated as “hostile” by the Intelligence Ministry. The measure passed by a vote of 174 to six, despite opposition from the cabinet.  

The legislation imposes penalties of up to two years in prison, fines and flogging on Iranians who speak to those designated outlets.  

The bill has not yet become law and must still be reviewed by the Guardian Council.
summary: The bill was approved by a 174‑to‑6 vote despite cabinet opposition, targeting Iranians who speak to outlets designated as hostile by the Intelligence Ministry. It imposes up to two years in prison, fines and flogging, but has not yet become law and awaits Guardian Council review.
author: Euronews

title: Madrid homes cost more per square metre than major Latin American cities
content:
A comparison of housing costs shows that homes in Madrid command a higher price per square metre than those in several major Latin American cities.  

Despite the lower per‑metre price in those Latin American markets, lower wages in the region can make renting comparatively less affordable for residents.
summary: Homes cost more per square metre in Madrid than in several major Latin American cities. However, lower wages in those cities can make renting even less affordable.
author: Euronews

title: Iran says forces ready for pre‑emptive strike; US doubts authority of Pezeshkian, Araghchi
content:
Iran’s military warned it is ready to launch pre‑emptive strikes if circumstances demand, according to a statement from the army’s spokesman. The remark came as officials from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) asserted that Tehran has tightened its control over the strategic Strait of Hormuz.

In Washington, officials publicly debated the extent of authority held by Pezeshkian and Araghchi within the Iranian hierarchy. The discussion highlighted U.S. uncertainty about who actually directs Tehran’s policy decisions.
summary: Iran's army spokesman said Tehran's forces were prepared to strike first "should circumstances require it." IRGC officials claimed tighter control of Hormuz, and Washington publicly pondered how much authority Pezeshkian and Araghchi actually wielded.
author: Euronews

title: Mali junta forces re-enter Kidal after Tuareg separatists withdraw
content:
Malian army forces entered the strategic northern city of Kidal on Tuesday after Tuareg separatists announced their withdrawal as the military advanced. The town, seized about five months earlier by the separatists, had been a focal point of the conflict in the north.

The recapture is being presented as a symbolic boost for Mali’s junta and its Russian backers. In late April, jihadists from the Al‑Qaeda‑linked JNIM network and their Tuareg separatist allies launched a series of attacks aimed at weakening the junta, including taking control of Kidal and killing the defence minister. FRANCE 24 senior journalist Wassim Nasr reported on the development.
summary: The Malian army says it has entered the strategic northern city of Kidal, which was captured around five months ago by Tuareg separatists. The separatists announced their withdrawal on Tuesday as the military advanced, a symbolic boost to the junta and its Russian backers.
author: France 24

title: France's student protests continue from Mai 68 to 2026 over high‑school under‑investment
content:
Students, parents and trade unions demonstrated across France on Tuesday, protesting what they say is under‑investment in high schools. The nationwide rallies are part of a long‑standing tradition of French student activism.

From the Mai 68 protests to the CPE crisis in 2006, major French student and youth demonstrations have pressured leaders and transformed national politics. The current actions continue that legacy, extending the pattern of protest into 2026.
summary: Students, parents and trade unions demonstrated across France on Tuesday, protesting what they say is under‑investment in high schools. From Mai 68 to the CPE crisis in 2006, major French student and youth protests have pressured leaders and transformed national politics.
author: France 24

title: German court keeps ex-spy chief August Hanning in detention on espionage, treason
content:
A German court on Wednesday ordered former foreign intelligence chief August Hanning to remain in pre‑trial detention after his arrest on suspicion of espionage and treason.  

The detention order also involves a former deputy of the agency, who prosecutors say supplied Hanning with secret files.  

Authorities describe the case as one of the biggest security breaches in German history. The court’s ruling keeps Hanning in custody while the investigation proceeds.
summary: A court on Wednesday ordered the former head of Germany's foreign intelligence service August Hanning to remain in pretrial detention after his arrest on suspicion of espionage and treason, along with a former deputy who allegedly supplied him with secret files. Here's what we know about one of the biggest security breaches in German history.
author: France 24

title: New French film adaptation of Les Misérables stars Vincent Lindon and Tahar Rahim
content:
This week on arts24, film critic Manon Kerjean surveys the latest French cinema releases, beginning with a new adaptation of Victor Hugo’s Les Misérables.

The three‑hour epic stars Vincent Lindon as Jean Valjean opposite Tahar Rahim as Inspector Javert, delivering a thriller‑like tension to the classic story.
summary: Film critic Manon Kerjean on arts24 reviews the latest French cinema releases, beginning with a new adaptation of Victor Hugo's "Les Misérables". The three‑hour film stars Vincent Lindon as Jean Valjean opposite Tahar Rahim as Inspector Javert and adds thriller‑like tension to the classic story.
author: France 24

title: Comoros passes law banning foreign nationals from small‑scale businesses
content:
A new law in the Comoros prohibits foreign nationals from operating certain small‑scale businesses.  

The restriction threatens the livelihoods of thousands of workers, the majority of whom are Malagasy migrants. The measure is described as part of a broader trend of economic protectionism aimed at migrant workers across the African continent.
summary: A new law in the Comoros bans foreign nationals from operating certain small‑scale businesses. The measure threatens the livelihoods of thousands of people, most of them Malagasy, and reflects a broader trend of economic protectionism targeting migrant workers in Africa.
author: France 24

title: British adventurer Karl Bushby reaches UK after 28-year trek
content:
British adventurer Karl Bushby has set foot on UK soil after a 28‑year, 50,000‑kilometre trek from South America, publicists said Tuesday. The 57‑year‑old former paratrooper completed the final leg by swimming across the English Channel.

Bushby began his journey in November 1998 from Punta Arenas, Chile, vowing to reach his mother’s home near Hull in northern England without using planes, trains, boats, vehicles or other transport modes. His arrival marks the end of the long‑running round‑the‑world walk.
summary: British adventurer Karl Bushby, a 57-year-old former paratrooper, arrived on UK soil after swimming the Channel, completing his 28-year, 50,000‑kilometre trek from South America. He began the journey from Punta Arenas, Chile, in November 1998, vowing to reach his mother’s home near Hull without using planes, trains, boats, vehicles or other transport.
author: France 24

title: African tourists may turn away as xenophobia shadows South Africa tourism
content:
South Africa has logged record tourist arrivals in the past two months, with more than one million visitors arriving by air each month, according to FRANCE 24’s on‑the‑ground reporting. Tourism now contributes over 8 percent of the country’s GDP.

Despite the surge, a growing concern is that African tourists may begin to avoid South Africa. The nation’s xenophobic image, highlighted by the FRANCE 24 team, is seen as a factor that could gradually turn away visitors from the continent.
summary: South Africa recorded record tourist arrivals of more than one million visitors arriving by air each month over the past two months. Nevertheless, the country's xenophobic image is causing concerns that African tourists may gradually turn away, even as tourism accounts for more than 8% of GDP, according to FRANCE 24’s team.
author: France 24

title: Oct. 7 attack fuels divisions over Netanyahu ahead of Israel's election
content:
Israel is preparing for its first national elections since the Hamas attack of Oct. 7, 2023, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his political rivals centering their campaigns on the fallout from that day.  

Three years after what officials described as the worst security failure in Israel’s history, the incident is now seen as a threat to Netanyahu’s career, the country’s longest‑serving prime minister, according to France 24’s Noga Tarnopolsky reporting from Jerusalem.
summary: Israel is preparing for its first elections since the Hamas attack on Oct. 7, 2023. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his opponents are centering the attack in their campaigns, and the security failure now threatens to end his career.
author: France 24

title: Houthis claim strikes on Aden and Riyadh airports amid Yemen fighting
content:
Yemen’s Houthi movement said it carried out strikes on both Aden and Riyadh airports as fighting in the country escalated.  

Aden International Airport was hit in an attack attributed to the Houthis, part of a broader effort by the group to target key transport hubs.  

The intensified conflict between government forces and the Houthis has displaced around 200,000 people.
summary: The Houthis claimed strikes on Aden International Airport and Riyadh airports. Around 200,000 people have been displaced by the fighting between government forces and the Houthis.
author: DW World

title: China’s Golden Week shows cautious consumer spending despite travel surge
content: Chinese visitors are returning home after the 13‑day Golden Week holiday, a period that saw a surge in travel across the country.  Despite the increase in trips, their spending remained subdued, prompting analysts to question the strength of domestic demand in China, the world’s second‑largest economy.
summary: Chinese visitors are returning from trips after the 13‑day Golden Week holiday. Their subdued spending has raised fresh questions about domestic demand in the world’s second‑largest economy.
author: DW World

title: South Sudan's first general election set for Dec 22 amid credibility doubts
content:
South Sudan’s first general election is scheduled for December 22, but its prospects remain uncertain.  

Officials and observers say that ongoing insecurity, heightened political tensions and the fact that voter registration has not yet begun have raised doubts about whether the poll can be conducted credibly.
summary: South Sudan's first general election is scheduled for December 22. Insecurity, political tensions and the failure to begin voter registration have raised doubts about holding a credible poll.
author: DW World

title: Israeli demolition in At Tur, East Jerusalem displaces 69 Palestinians
content:
Israeli authorities approved the demolition of a residential building in the At Tur area of East Jerusalem on Tuesday, displacing sixty‑nine Palestinians, according to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA).

More than half of those displaced were children. OCHA reported the demolition and the resulting displacement of the residents.
summary: Sixty‑nine Palestinians, more than half of them children, were displaced on Tuesday after Israeli authorities green‑lit the demolition of their residential building in the At Tur area of East Jerusalem. The UN aid coordination office (OCHA) reported the displacement.
author: UN News

title: Rocket revolution expands access to space launches
content:
The “rocket revolution” is widening the door to space, according to the latest commentary on launch capabilities.  

For many years, only a relatively small group of national space programmes could send payloads beyond Earth, but that situation is now changing.
summary: Launching beyond Earth was once limited to a relatively small number of national space programmes. That is now changing.
author: UN News

title: WHO issues first global child obesity guidelines as rates rise to 8%
content:
The United Nations World Health Organization (WHO) has issued its first global guidelines on child obesity as the condition continues to rise sharply worldwide.  

According to WHO data, obesity among children and adolescents aged five to 19 has quadrupled since 1990, increasing from two percent to roughly eight percent of that age group.
summary: The UN World Health Organization released its first global guidelines on child obesity. Child and adolescent obesity has quadrupled since 1990, rising from two percent to around eight percent among 5‑19 year olds.
author: UN News

title: Governments urge UN reform at New York General Assembly to match modern world
content:
Governments are urging the United Nations to modernize, warning that the organization must reflect today’s world or risk losing trust. The call for reform was a central theme at the United Nations General Assembly in New York last month.

During the debate on UN reform, a diverse range of Member States voiced a strikingly common refrain, questioning whether the UN can remain relevant if it continues to look and act as it did when it was founded in 1945. The consensus underscores growing pressure on the UN to adapt its structures and practices to contemporary realities.
summary: The General Assembly in New York held a debate on UN reform last month, drawing a common refrain from a diverse range of Member States. Members questioned whether the UN can stay relevant if it continues to look and act like the organization created in 1945.
author: UN News

title: WHO warns funding gap endangers health response in Yemen
content:
The World Health Organization warned that a critical funding gap is endangering the health response in Yemen. WHO officials said that significantly more resources are needed to scale up its operations in the country.

The warning comes as the conflict in Yemen escalates and health needs continue to rise, prompting the agency to call for urgent additional funding to sustain and expand its response.
summary: The World Health Organization warned that a critical funding gap threatens its health response in Yemen. It said significantly more resources are needed to scale up the response amid escalating conflict and rising needs.
author: UN News

title: Parti Québécois wins Quebec election but falls short of majority, referendum doubtful
content:
The Parti Québécois (PQ) won Monday’s Quebec provincial election, adding 56 seats and more than doubling its vote share from the 2022 contest, giving the party its first taste of power in 14 years.  Despite the surge, the PQ fell five seats short of a majority in the National Assembly.

The shortfall undermines the party’s pledge to hold a sovereignty referendum after U.S. President Donald Trump leaves office in 2028, a promise now described as “nearly impossible.”  Analysts note that the result comes amid a bruising trade dispute with the Trump administration, further complicating any push toward separation.
summary: The Parti Québécois won Monday’s Quebec election, adding 56 seats and more than doubling its vote share from 2022, giving it its first taste of power in 14 years. However, the party finished five seats short of a majority, making its pledge to hold a sovereignty referendum after Donald Trump leaves office in 2028 unlikely.
author: Guardian World

title: Flávio Bolsonaro leads first round of Brazil election, alarming climate activists
content:
Flávio Bolsonaro’s lead in the first round of Brazil’s presidential election this week has been described as a grim jolt for climate campaigners. An inquest is under way to understand why President Lula’s success in curbing Amazon deforestation has not translated into electoral support.

Campaigners warn that if Bolsonaro maintains the advantage he established, the Amazon rainforest could face “more fire, more ash, more crime, more death” and be driven further toward a point of no return over the next four years. The concern appears to be greater among the international community than among voters in Latin America’s biggest, richest and most biodiverse nation.
summary: Flávio Bolsonaro established a lead in the first round of Brazil’s presidential election this week. Climate campaigners say his potential four‑year term could increase Amazon fires, ash, crime and deaths, reversing President Lula’s gains in curbing deforestation.
author: Guardian World

title: Flávio Bolsonaro vows to ‘re‑democratise’ Brazil, sparking fears of authoritarian rule
content:
Flávio Bolsonaro secured a surprise first‑round victory, positioning him as the far‑right frontrunner to become Brazil’s next president. His win has been described as a rapid rise for the “House of Bolsonaro,” prompting heightened scrutiny of his political agenda.

In his post‑victory remarks, Bolsonaro pledged to “re‑democratise” Brazil, a statement that critics say could signal a continuation of the authoritarian approach associated with his father, disgraced ex‑president Jair Bolsonaro. Observers warn that such rhetoric may pave the way for a shift toward authoritarian rule if Flávio assumes office.

Brazil’s current democratic framework dates back to the 1980s, when the nation emerged from a 21‑year dictatorship that Jair Bolsonaro has publicly praised. The prospect of a new administration echoing those authoritarian sentiments has intensified concerns about the country’s democratic future.
summary: Flávio Bolsonaro, the far‑right frontrunner, secured a surprise first‑round victory in Brazil’s presidential race. He has vowed to “re‑democratise” Brazil, prompting critics to warn that his win could extend the authoritarian legacy of his father, disgraced ex‑president Jair Bolsonaro.
author: Guardian World

title: Israeli soldier filmed assaulting Palestinian woman during West Bank raid
content:
An Israeli soldier was filmed assaulting a Palestinian woman during a raid on a family home in the occupied West Bank. The incident was captured on video as the soldier entered the residence.

The assault occurred while the soldier was conducting the raid, targeting a family dwelling in the territory. The footage shows the soldier physically attacking the woman during the operation.

The video of the assault has been released, documenting the soldier’s actions against the Palestinian woman during the raid.
summary: An Israeli soldier was filmed assaulting a Palestinian woman. The incident occurred during a raid on a family home in the occupied West Bank.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Coco Gauff calls online racist abuse at China Open draining after early exit
content:
Coco Gauff said the online racist abuse she endured during the China Open was “draining.” The U.S. tennis star made the comments after she failed to reach the quarterfinals of the tournament.  

Gauff admitted that the racism she suffered exhausted her following her exit from the event.
summary: Coco Gauff said the online racist abuse she faced during the China Open was draining. The US tennis star was eliminated before reaching the quarterfinals.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai win Nobel chemistry prize for mirror‑image work
content:
Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai have been awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for their “mirror image” work on asymmetric molecules.  

The prize honors the scientists for solving the mystery of asymmetric molecules, a breakthrough that has aided the manufacture of pharmaceuticals.  

The award underscores the impact of their research on drug production.
summary: Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai were awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for their work on mirror‑image molecules. Their research solved the mystery of asymmetric molecules and has helped in the manufacture of pharmaceuticals.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Saudi Arabia defeats UAE 2-0 to claim fourth Arabian Gulf Cup after 22-year gap
content:
Saudi Arabia defeated the United Arab Emirates 2‑0 to capture the Arabian Gulf Cup, ending a 22‑year wait for the title.  

Goals from Hammam Al‑Hammami and Firas al‑Buraikan secured the win and gave the hosts their fourth Arabian Gulf Cup trophy.
summary: Saudi Arabia beat UAE 2-0 in the Arabian Gulf Cup final. Goals from Hammam Al-Hammami and Firas al-Buraikan gave the hosts their fourth Arabian Gulf Cup trophy, ending a 22-year wait.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Okinawa governor urges Japan action after US Marine Devin Jacob Ballard arrested
content:
The governor of Okinawa has called on the Japanese government to take action after U.S. Marine Devin Jacob Ballard was arrested on suspicion of strangling 39‑year‑old Anna Yagi.  

The arrest has sparked growing anger among local residents.  

Ballard’s detention follows the allegation that he killed Yagi, prompting the governor’s appeal for a response from Japanese authorities.
summary: The Okinawa governor urged Japan to act following the arrest of a US Marine. US Marine Devin Jacob Ballard was arrested on suspicion of strangling 39‑year‑old Anna Yagi, prompting growing anger.
author: Al Jazeera

title: South Korea to tighten military exemption rules for Asian Games gold medallists
content: South Korea announced it will consider cutting military exemption benefits for athletes who win gold medals at the Asian Games. The proposal follows a public backlash over comments made by athletes about the Asian Games. Authorities said the move aims to address criticism and reassess the exemption policy for gold‑medal winners.
summary: South Korea says it will cut military exemptions for gold medallists. The decision follows backlash over athletes' Asian Games comments.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Paramount-Warner merger raises press freedom concerns over chairman's ties to Trump, Israel
content:
The proposed merger of Paramount and Warner has ignited concerns that it could threaten press freedom. Critics point to the deal’s potential impact on the media landscape and the independence of news outlets.

The chairman’s family connections to former President Donald Trump and to Israel have prompted questions about editorial independence at CNN and CBS, raising further doubts about how the consolidation might affect journalistic autonomy.
summary: The proposed Paramount-Warner merger has sparked fears about press freedom. The chairman's family ties to Trump and Israel raise questions over editorial independence at CNN and CBS.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Pakistan subsidises petrol for millions, but some in need left out
content:
Pakistan’s government has introduced a petrol subsidy that now benefits millions of citizens. The relief program lowers the cost of fuel for a large segment of the population.

However, some economists warn that the subsidy does not reach the people who need it most, leaving a portion of the population without assistance.
summary: The Pakistani government has subsidised petrol for millions of people. Some economists caution that those most needing help are left out.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Ten linked to Kenya's first Ebola case quarantined amid screening concerns
content:
Ten people linked to Kenya’s first‑ever Ebola case have been placed under quarantine as screening concerns grow.  

The index patient traveled through multiple cities in the Democratic Republic of Congo, drove to Uganda and ultimately flew to Kenya.  

The quarantine of the ten contacts underscores the heightened vigilance of Kenyan health authorities.
summary: Ten people linked to Kenya's first-ever Ebola case have been placed in quarantine as screening concerns grow. The patient passed through multiple cities in DR Congo, drove to Uganda and eventually flew to Kenya.
author: BBC World

title: Sri Lanka's ex-first lady, 73, arrested over alleged misuse of children's hospital donations
content:
Sri Lanka’s former first lady, a 73‑year‑old woman, was arrested on suspicion of involvement in the misuse of charitable contributions.  

Authorities say the arrest stems from allegations that a charity linked to her misappropriated donations intended for a children’s hospital.
summary: The 73-year-old ex-first lady of Sri Lanka has been arrested. She is accused of being linked to a charity that misused donations intended for a children's hospital.
author: BBC World

title: Trump to speak with Putin about Russian lab worker's death
content:
Former President Donald Trump is set to speak with Russian President Vladimir Putin about the death of a laboratory worker in Russia, according to the headline.  

Officials and observers have expressed concerns that the worker’s death may have been caused by pneumonic plague, prompting demands for greater transparency from Russian authorities.  

Calls for more openness from Russia have intensified in response to the plague‑related fears.
summary: Trump will speak with Putin about the death of a lab worker in Russia. Fears that the death may have been caused by pneumonic plague have prompted calls for more transparency from Russia.
author: BBC World

title: Justin Ellis helps US cap a perfect international window with 1-0 win over Canada
content:
Justin Ellis scored the decisive goal in a 1-0 victory over Canada, securing a fourth win in four matches for the United States during a perfect international window. The match, described as chippy and at times ugly, was managed by referee Steven Madrigal, who was noted for paying tribute to the history of the referee’s whistle.

The article highlights the evolution of officiating tools, referencing Joseph Hudson, a Birmingham-bred tool maker who founded Acme Whistles. Hudson introduced his signature product to an FA Cup match in 1878, replacing the prior practice of referees waving a white handkerchief to signal fouls. This innovation occurred nearly 150 years before the recent match between the United States and Canada.
summary: Justin Ellis helped the United States defeat Canada 1-0, capping a perfect international window. The win completed the US's streak of victories.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Lionel Messi bids tearful farewell to Argentina after scoring in 3-0 win over Benin
content:
Lionel Messi concluded his 21-year international career on Tuesday with a tearful farewell to Argentina fans in Buenos Aires. The 39-year-old, widely regarded as the greatest football player in history, made his final appearance for the former world champions in front of 85,000 supporters.

In a decisive match, Messi scored his 126th international goal, helping Argentina secure a 3-0 victory over Benin.
summary: Lionel Messi ended his 21-year international career in a 3-0 victory over Benin, scoring his 126th international goal. The match drew 85,000 fans in Buenos Aires as Messi bid farewell to Argentina.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Wrexham's new Kop stand signals ambition to reach Premier League
content: Wrexham’s new Kop stand serves as a signal of the club’s ambition to continue its ascent from the Championship to the Premier League. The project is designed to match the team’s recent rise, reflecting a broader strategic goal to progress to the top tier of English football.
summary: Wrexham's new Kop stand signals the club's ambition to climb from the Championship to the Premier League. The project reflects the club's rising trajectory.
author: BBC Sport

title: Collins, Jackson clash in first Maine Senate debate
content:
Republican Sen. Susan Collins and Democrat Troy Jackson faced off Tuesday in the first debate of their closely contested Senate race in Maine. Collins, a five-term senator and a rare Republican to win statewide in the blue-leaning state, used the debate stage to highlight instances where she has defied her party.

During the discussion, Collins pointed to her pro-choice position and her vote against President Trump’s signature legislation as examples of times she has bucked her party.
summary: Republican Sen. Susan Collins and Democrat Troy Jackson faced off in the first debate of their Senate race in Maine. Collins highlighted her pro-choice position and her vote against President Trump’s signature legislation.
author: The Hill

title: Benson, James spar in Michigan gubernatorial debate: 3 takeaways
content: Michigan Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson and Representative John James faced off in a gubernatorial debate hosted by Nexstar’s WOOD-TV on Tuesday. The candidates discussed issues specific to the state in the final month before voters select the next governor of Michigan.
summary: Michigan Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson (D) and Rep. John James (R-Mich.) debated on Tuesday, hosted by Nexstar’s WOOD-TV, less than a month before the gubernatorial election. They discussed issues specific to Michigan.

title: Iowa Governor Debate Focuses on Carpetbagging Accusations and Family Wealth Attacks
content:
The first televised debate between Republican Zach Lahn and Democrat Rob Sand was marked by accusations of carpetbagging, attacks regarding family wealth, and exchanges over culture war issues. The two candidates are competing to succeed retiring Governor Kim Reynolds (R) next month.

The hour-long debate was hosted by KWQC and took place at St. Ambrose.
summary: The first televised debate between Republican Zach Lahn and Democrat Rob Sand, who are vying to replace retiring Gov. Kim Reynolds (R) next month, was dominated by accusations of carpetbagging, attacks over family wealth, and barbs over culture war issues. The hour-long debate was hosted by KWQC and held at St. Ambrose.
author: The Hill

title: Three Arrested in Raid on Gang Accused of Helping Migrants Pretend to Be Gay for Asylum
content: Three individuals were arrested following a raid on a gang alleged to help migrants pretend to be gay in order to secure asylum. The Home Office immigration enforcement officers carried out the operation, targeting members of the gang. Those targeted by the officers are accused of charging migrants up to £4,500 for fabricated evidence.
summary: Three individuals were arrested after a raid on a gang accused of helping migrants pretend to be gay to obtain asylum. The Home Office immigration enforcement officers claim the gang charged migrants up to £4,500 for fabricated evidence.
author: BBC Politics

title: Nobel winner Halzen says years of October 'misery' finally over
content:
Physicist Francis Halzen says the years of October “misery” are finally over.  

Halzen, who has an impressively long list of academic accolades, has long been a contender for the Nobel Prize.  Each October, as the Nobel announcement rolled around, he found himself unable to secure the award, a failure that left him “miserable,” he admits.  

He now declares that the cycle of disappointment has ended, marking a new chapter in his career.
summary: Physicist Francis Halzen says his repeated failures to win the Nobel Prize each October made him miserable. He has a long list of academic accolades, but the Nobel Prize has eluded him.
author: Phys.org

title: Study estimates oyster reefs could generate $12 trillion annually for planetary health
content:
A recent study estimates that the world’s oyster reefs could contribute up to $12 trillion annually to planetary health if they were better managed.  

The researchers calculated the reefs’ potential gross ecosystem product (GEP)—the ecological counterpart of gross domestic product—finding that the reefs deliver trillions of dollars in ecosystem goods and services each year to various aspects of planetary health, including human well‑being.  

The study notes that oyster reefs are vastly underestimated and underutilized. To unlock their full value, oyster reefs around the world must be restored and protected.
summary: A new study calculated the gross ecosystem product of oyster reefs, estimating trillions of dollars in ecosystem goods and services each year. The study says the reefs' full potential can only be realized if they are restored and protected.
author: Phys.org

title: EU faces fierce lobbying over banning PFAS 'forever chemicals'
content:
The European Union faces mounting pressure to ban “forever chemicals.” The debate is intensifying in Brussels over the toxic substances known as PFAS, with industry groups actively seeking as many exemptions as possible.

The fight over PFAS highlights the tension between regulatory efforts to curb the use of these persistent chemicals and industry interests that wish to maintain flexibility in their production and use.
summary: The European Union is under pressure to ban PFAS, also known as 'forever chemicals'. Industry groups in Brussels are seeking as many exemptions as possible.
author: Phys.org

title: Sleep, appetite, gene‑editing experts vie for Nobel chemistry prize
content:
Sleep, appetite, gene‑editing experts contend for Nobel chemistry prize

Research into molecules that regulate sleep and appetite, as well as methods for editing genes, could be among the contenders for the Nobel Prize in chemistry, to be announced Wednesday, commentators say.
summary: Research into molecules that regulate sleep and appetite or methods for editing genes could be among the contenders for the Nobel Prize in chemistry. The prize will be announced Wednesday, commentators say.
author: Phys.org

title: A new way to fight gum disease without wiping out good bacteria
content:
Scientists have discovered that interfering with the chemical signals bacteria use to communicate can shift dental plaque toward a healthier microbial balance.  

The technique, which targets bacterial communication, may enable treatments for gum disease that suppress harmful bacteria while preserving beneficial species.  

Researchers suggest this approach could form the basis for new therapies that control gum‑related infections without wiping out good bacteria.
summary: Scientists discovered that disrupting the chemical messages bacteria use to communicate can push dental plaque toward a healthier microbial balance. The approach could lead to new treatments for gum disease that control harmful bacteria without destroying beneficial species.
author: Science Daily

title: Study of 100 primate species shows humans not hardwired for violence
content:
A recent comparative study of 100 primate species, including humans, challenges the idea that everyday aggression and lethal violence are part of a single behavioral spectrum.  

The research found that species that frequently fight or show mild aggression are not necessarily more likely to kill rivals. Instead, extreme acts such as infanticide and lethal attacks appear to follow their own distinct evolutionary patterns.  

These findings suggest that humans may not be as hardwired for violence as previously thought.
summary: A study comparing 100 primate species, including humans, found that everyday aggression and lethal violence did not evolve as part of the same simple behavioral spectrum. Species that frequently fight or show mild aggression are not necessarily more likely to kill rivals, while extreme acts such as infanticide and lethal attacks appear to follow their own evolutionary patterns.
author: Science Daily

title: LSE study finds techno‑optimist scientists 23% less likely to sign climate petitions
content:
A study from the London School of Economics found that scientists who believe technology will largely solve the problems caused by the climate crisis are less likely to take climate action.

The report shows that these techno‑optimists are 23 % less likely to sign petitions or participate in protests than peers who doubt that technology is the answer. They are also 18 % less likely to adopt high‑impact lifestyle changes, such as reducing flights or switching to a vegan or vegetarian diet.

The findings suggest a link between technology optimism and lower engagement in climate action.
summary: Scientists who believe technology will largely solve climate problems are less likely to engage in civic climate action, a London School of Economics report found. The report says they are 23% less likely to sign petitions or join protests and 18% less likely to make high‑impact lifestyle changes such as reducing flights or adopting a vegan or vegetarian diet.
author: Guardian Science

content:
Doha will host the Asian Games in 2030 and is listed among seven cities under consideration to host the 2036 Olympic Games.  

Formula 1 confirmed that its races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will proceed as scheduled, providing relief after months of uncertainty.  

The confirmations underscore Qatar’s continued focus on securing major international sporting events.

content:

title: New island forms as Caspian Sea shrinks, scientists warn of northern pressure
content: The Caspian Sea, which has been shrinking for decades, has produced a new island. Scientists warn that parts of the northern Caspian could face an Aral Sea‑like scenario. They say climate change and human water use are adding pressure on the region.
summary: The Caspian Sea has been shrinking for decades and a new island has emerged. Scientists warn that parts of the northern Caspian could face an Aral Sea‑like scenario as climate change and human water use add pressure.
author: Euronews

title: Government delay of Verifactu e‑invoicing gives Spanish SMEs and self‑employed more time
content:
The Spanish government has postponed the implementation of the Verifactu electronic invoicing system. The delay provides additional time for small and medium‑sized enterprises and self‑employed workers to prepare for the new requirement.

However, the postponement also heightens uncertainty about when and how the rollout will ultimately occur.
summary: The Government has delayed bringing the Verifactu e‑invoicing system into force. The postponement gives firms and the self‑employed additional time but fuels uncertainty over its rollout.
author: Euronews

title: Christa Pike awake a week after lethal injection, still shackled in hospital
content:
Christa Pike is awake a week after a lethal injection attempt, but she remains shackled to a hospital bed with burned and blistered arms, according to reports.

The incident has coincided with Tennessee’s suspension of executions and the resignation of the state’s prison chief.
summary: Christa Pike is awake a week after a lethal injection and remains shackled to a hospital bed with burned and blistered arms. Tennessee has suspended executions and its prison chief has resigned.
author: Euronews

title: Paris student protests turn violent, police use tear gas and fireworks
content:
Student protests in Paris turned violent, with tear gas and fireworks reported as clashes erupted.  

School pupils demanding better funding confronted riot police, part of a wave of nationwide protests over shortages and crumbling schools. The confrontations in the capital led police to deploy tear gas against the demonstrators.
summary: Clashes erupted in Paris as school pupils demanding better funding faced riot police. The protests are part of nationwide demonstrations over shortages and crumbling schools.
author: Euronews

title: Israelis hold ceremonies at Nova site and Kfar Aza, three years after Hamas attack
content:
Israelis gathered at the Nova festival site and in Kfar Aza to mourn the victims of the October 7 Hamas‑led attack, three years after the assault that ignited the Gaza war.

The ceremonies marked the anniversary of the Hamas‑led October 7 attack, which sparked the ongoing conflict in Gaza.
summary: Ceremonies were held at the Nova festival site and in Kfar Aza. They marked three years since the Hamas‑led October 7 attack that sparked the Gaza war.
author: Euronews

title: Haiti indefinitely postpones December and February elections amid gang violence
content:
Haiti’s electoral council announced on Tuesday that the country’s elections, originally set for December and February, have been postponed indefinitely. The council cited technical and operational requirements, noting that ongoing gang violence continues to disrupt election preparations.

The postponement leaves Haitians without a democratic process as authorities work to register voters and secure the areas needed for a poll. No new date for the elections has been provided.
summary: Haiti’s electoral council said the December and February elections are postponed indefinitely, citing technical and operational requirements. Gang violence continues to disrupt voter registration and security for the polls, leaving the country without a democratic process.
author: France 24

title: Lionel Messi bids farewell, scores in 3-0 win over Benin at Monumental Stadium
content:
Lionel Messi said farewell to Argentina fans Tuesday in an emotional final international appearance.  

He scored in a 3‑0 win over Benin at Buenos Aires' Monumental Stadium.  

The match was watched by 85,000 supporters who celebrated the end of a career that brought the country its long‑awaited 2022 World Cup triumph.
summary: Lionel Messi said farewell to Argentina fans on Tuesday in his final international appearance, scoring in a 3-0 win over Benin at Buenos Aires' Monumental Stadium. The match was attended by 85,000 supporters who celebrated the end of a career that delivered Argentina's 2022 World Cup triumph.
author: France 24

title: Israel to hold memorials for third anniversary of Oct. 7 Hamas attack amid election campaign
content:
Israel will observe the third anniversary of the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack on Wednesday with memorial events held across the country.  

Heightened security will surround the commemorations as voters prepare for an upcoming election in which the deadliest day in Israel’s history is expected to remain a central issue.
summary: Israel will mark the third anniversary of the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack with memorial events across the country on Wednesday. Heightened security will surround the commemorations as voters prepare for an election where the deadliest day in Israel’s history is expected to remain a central issue.
author: France 24

title: Israel commemorates third anniversary of Hamas Oct 7 attacks, all hostages home
content:
Live: Israel marks three years since Hamas’s deadly October 7 attacks

Israelis began commemorations on Wednesday for the victims of Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attacks. The attacks killed 1,200 people and saw 251 hostages taken.

This year – the third anniversary of the attacks – is the first time all the hostages or their remains are home.

Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.
summary: Israelis began commemorations on Wednesday for the victims of Hamas's October 7, 2023 attacks that killed 1,200 people and involved 251 hostages. The third anniversary marks the first time all hostages or their remains have been returned home.
author: France 24

title: Netanyahu seeks political survival three years after October 7 attacks
content:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is fighting for political survival as Israel heads to legislative elections later this month, three years after the deadly Hamas‑led attacks on October 7 in southern Israel.  

Reports that Arab leaders warned him of the assault in advance have undercut Netanyahu’s claims that Israel’s security chiefs were to blame.  

Despite the controversy, his political base appears to be holding.
summary: Three years after the deadly Hamas-led October 7 attacks in southern Israel, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is fighting for political survival ahead of legislative elections later this month. Reports that Arab leaders warned him of the assault in advance have undercut his claims that Israel's security chiefs are to blame, but his political base appears to be holding.
author: France 24

title: Lionel Messi scores in Argentina's 3-0 win over Benin in his final match
content:
Lionel Messi scored in Argentina’s 3‑0 victory over Benin, marking his final appearance for the national team.  

The match concluded with a 3‑0 win for Argentina, and a full tribute to Messi was presented both before and after the game.
summary: Lionel Messi scored as Argentina defeated Benin 3-0. The game was his final appearance for Argentina and he received a full tribute before and after the match.
author: France 24

title: At least two killed in Kyiv fire after massive strikes
content:
At least two people were killed in a fire in Kyiv after President Volodymyr Zelensky described the incident as the result of “massive strikes” on the Ukrainian capital on Wednesday.  

Ukraine has faced a surge in attacks in recent weeks, with Russian forces targeting energy infrastructure as well as rail and road transport networks.
summary: At least two people were killed in a fire in Kyiv after President Volodymyr Zelensky described "massive strikes" on the capital on Wednesday. Ukraine has faced increased attacks in recent weeks, with Russian strikes targeting energy infrastructure and rail and road transport.
author: France 24

title: Spain PM Pedro Sanchez calls early election; housing, migration and Vox dominate campaign
content:
Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has called an early election in Spain, describing the move as a gamble.  

Analysts note that the campaign is expected to focus on three main issues: the country’s housing crisis, migration concerns and the growing influence of the right‑wing populist Vox party.
summary: Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is taking a gamble by calling an early election in Spain. The housing crisis, migration and the rise of the right‑wing populist Vox party are likely to dominate the campaign.
author: DW World

title: Lionel Messi scores and assists in Argentina's 3-0 farewell win
content:
Argentina defeated its opponent 3-0 in what was Lionel Messi’s final match for the national team.  

Messi contributed directly to all three goals, scoring one and creating two additional chances that were converted by teammates.  

The victory served as a farewell to the country’s most decorated footballer.
summary: Messi scored a goal and provided two assists as Argentina defeated their opponent 3-0. The match marked Argentina's farewell to its most decorated footballer.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Yemen's conflict leaves over 137,000 students without school access
content:
Displaced children in Yemen are longing to resume their studies as the country’s education system remains under severe strain.  

According to recent figures, more than 137,000 students in conflict‑affected areas have lost access to schooling, deepening an already dire crisis for Yemen’s education sector.
summary: More than 137,000 students in conflict zones have lost access to education. The loss deepens Yemen's already dire schooling crisis.
author: Al Jazeera

title: At least two killed in Kyiv during Russia's massive strike on Ukraine
content:
At least two people were killed in Kyiv as Russia launched a “massive” attack on Ukraine.  

Russia’s Defence Ministry said its forces carried out a massive strike on Kyiv and other Ukrainian regions.  

The strike resulted in casualties in the Ukrainian capital.
summary: At least two people were killed in Kyiv. Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces carried out a massive strike on Kyiv and other Ukrainian regions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Gaza City port, once fishing and tourism hub, now shown in ruins after genocide
content:
Gaza City’s port, once a bustling hub for fishing and tourism, has been dramatically altered. The change follows the period described as a genocide.  

Al Jazeera journalist Maram Humaid has documented the remaining conditions at the port, showing what is left after the conflict. The footage highlights the stark contrast between the port’s former role and its present state.
summary: Gaza City’s port was a hub for fishing and tourism before the genocide. Al Jazeera’s Maram Humaid shows what’s left.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Russia's fuel crisis could open Central Asian market for Iranian oil
content:
Iran’s oil exports have been hampered by a United States blockade, limiting the country’s ability to sell its petroleum abroad.  

Recent disruptions to Russia’s fuel supply, caused by Ukrainian attacks on Russian energy infrastructure, have created a shortage that could open opportunities for Iranian oil in Central Asian markets.  

Analysts note that the Russian crisis may provide a pathway for Iran to increase its presence in the region despite the ongoing U.S. restrictions.
summary: Iran's oil exports have struggled amid a US blockade. A Russian energy crisis caused by Ukrainian attacks could help Iranian oil.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Houthis strike Aden airport runway; Saudi forces shoot down missile near Riyadh
content:
Yemen’s Houthi rebels launched an attack on Aden’s international airport, and Saudi forces reported downing a missile near Riyadh, officials said.

The Yemeni government said one of the missiles struck Aden airport’s runway only minutes before a scheduled flight from Cairo was due to land, disrupting the approach. Saudi forces intercepted a separate missile in the vicinity of Riyadh, preventing it from reaching its target.
summary: Yemeni officials say a missile struck Aden airport's runway shortly before a scheduled Cairo flight was to land. Saudi forces said they downed a missile near Riyadh.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Pornhub back in Australia, limited to adult Apple device users
content:
Pornhub, the world’s most popular adult‑content website, has resumed operations in Australia but is now accessible only to adult users on Apple devices.  

The site was taken offline in March after Australian authorities introduced age‑verification requirements that it could not meet. Its limited return means the platform remains unavailable on non‑Apple hardware.
summary: Pornhub has resumed service in Australia but only for adults using Apple devices. The site was taken offline in March after age‑verification laws were introduced.
author: BBC World

title: Former Bishop of Broome jailed for sexually abusing young men
content:
The former Bishop of Broome, a senior Catholic cleric, has been sentenced to jail after being found guilty of sexually abusing young men.  

His case marks him as one of the most senior Catholic officials worldwide to face sex‑abuse charges.
summary: The former Bishop of Broome, an Australian Catholic cleric, was jailed for sexually abusing young men. He is one of the most senior Catholic clerics worldwide to face sex‑abuse charges.
author: BBC World

title: Ex-US spy David Rush admits $200m scam, providing secrets to foreign government
content:
Former U.S. intelligence officer David Rush has admitted to orchestrating a $200 million fraud scheme and to storing gold bars in his home, according to prosecutors.  

Rush also confessed to passing classified information to a foreign government and disclosed the existence of a “clandestine human source,” officials said.
summary: David Rush, a former U.S. spy, admitted he stashed gold bars in his home as part of a $200 million scam. He also confessed to providing secrets to a foreign government and revealed a “clandestine human source,” prosecutors said.
author: BBC World

title: Survivors of Nir Oz kibbutz return three years after Hamas attack
content:
Three years after the Hamas‑led attack on October 7 that devastated the kibbutz Nir Oz, residents are confronting the challenge of rebuilding. The assault killed 47 people and resulted in 76 hostages being taken.

Some survivors have now returned to live in the community as they grapple with how to reconstruct their homes and lives.
summary: The Nir Oz kibbutz was destroyed in the 7 October Hamas-led attacks. Three years later, some survivors have returned to live there after 47 people were killed and 76 were taken hostage.
author: BBC World

title: USMNT faces Canada in international friendly at Allianz Field
content:
The United States men’s national team faces Canada in an international friendly scheduled to kick off at 8 p.m. ET at Allianz Field in Saint Paul. This match follows the USA’s 3-0 victory over Mexico in their previous outing.

Goalkeeper competition has reopened following shaky performances from World Cup incumbents Matt Freese and Chris Brady, while Diego Kochen impressed in his first start against Mexico. Brian Schwake is expected to start, aiming to translate his recent form with Nashville into his second appearance for the national team.

In defense, Auston Trusty is set to play left-back, potentially partnering with Chris Richards, while Alex Freeman may advance further up the right flank. Mathis Albert earned a surprise start over Zavier Gozo due to his dynamism during the training camp, offering a look at a potential future star for the program.
summary: The United States men's national team will play Canada in a friendly match at Allianz Field in Saint Paul. Goalkeeper competition is described as reopened after shaky performances from Matt Freese and Chris Brady, while Diego Kochen shone in his first start against Mexico.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Lionel Messi farewell match live – updates and analysis from Argentina v Benin
content:
Lionel Messi’s farewell match against Argentina and Benin is scheduled to kick off at 7pm ET, marking the end of his professional football career. The event has generated significant online discussion, with The Guardian receiving reader feedback via email regarding the historic occasion.

Among the comments shared by The Guardian, reader Paul engaged with a 20-year-old article about Messi, while another reader, “snafuclarke,” posted a critical opinion arguing that Messi is “hugely overrated.” This specific comment claimed that the hype surrounding the player has not matched his on-pitch performances, with the exception of his most recent game.
summary: Farewell match kicks off at 7pm ETMessi has completed footballEmail Pablo your analysis, jokes and moreGuardian reader Paul reached out via email and is apparently deep in the comments section of a 20-year-old Messi article we published here at the Guardian. I can only hope Guardian reader “snafuclarke” has fully recovered from such a scorchingly terrible take:don’t kid yourselves.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Pocognoli's Scotland left with questions after inert performance
content: Sebastien Pocognoli faces scrutiny following a lackluster performance by Scotland, which has left the manager still searching for his first home victory. The match highlighted ongoing domestic disharmony within the squad, prompting questions about the team's direction under his leadership.
summary: Sebastien Pocognoli is left with questions to answer following an inert Scotland performance. The result leaves him still searching for his first home win.
author: BBC Sport

title: Midfield options and a fab front four - what we've learned about England
content:
Phil McNulty has assessed the key takeaways for the England national team following the recent international window. His analysis highlights significant developments in the squad, specifically focusing on the return of Trent Alexander-Arnold and the debut of Alex Scott.

The evaluation also examines the team's tactical options, noting a strong midfield configuration and the emergence of a formidable front four. These factors represent the primary lessons England have gained from the latest period of international fixtures.
summary: From Trent Alexander-Arnold's return to Alex Scott's debut, Phil McNulty assesses what England have learned during this international window.
author: BBC Sport

title: Appeals panel reviews block of RFK Jr.'s vaccine panel appointments
content: The Trump administration argued to a federal appeals panel on Tuesday that a lower court made an error by preventing Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. from installing his chosen members on a major vaccine advisory committee. Justice Department attorney Matthew Zorn presented the case to the 1st U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, asserting that the district court judge lacked the legal power to issue the block.
summary: The Trump administration told a federal appeals panel that a lower court erred in blocking Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s appointees from a vaccine advisory panel. Justice Department attorney Matthew Zorn argued that the district court judge lacked the authority to issue the block.
author: The Hill

title: US renews do-not-travel warning for Russia over suspected pneumonic plague
content:
The U.S. State Department has renewed its warning for Americans not to travel to Russia, citing a suspected case of pneumonic plague in Siberia. The announcement was made on Tuesday via a post on the social platform X.

The State Department stated that the U.S. Embassy is aware of press reports regarding the suspected pneumonic plague in the Irkutsk region.
summary: The U.S. State Department is refreshing its call for Americans not to travel to Russia following a suspected case of pneumonic plague in Siberia. The department stated on X that the U.S. Embassy is aware of press reports regarding the suspected outbreak in the Irkutsk region.
author: The Hill

title: Trump: Government to take 40% stake in Sparrows Point submarine shipyard
content:
President Trump announced on Tuesday that the U.S. government will acquire a 40 percent stake in a planned “next generation” submarine shipyard located in Sparrows Point, Maryland. The industrial area, situated in Baltimore County, was the site of a presidential visit on the same day.

Trump stated that American taxpayers would receive this significant ownership share as part of a commitment to ensuring the enduring success of the shipyard.
summary: President Trump stated that American taxpayers will receive a 40 percent stake in the planned shipyard in Sparrows Point, Md. He made the announcement during a Tuesday visit to the unincorporated industrial area in Baltimore County.
author: The Hill

title: US trade deficit tops $100B in August, highest since March 2025
content: The U.S. trade deficit reached a 17-month high in August, surpassing $100 billion for the first time since March 2025. According to data released Tuesday by the Census Bureau and the Bureau of Economic Analysis, U.S. imports of goods and services exceeded the value of exports by $105.6 billion during that month.
summary: The U.S. trade deficit rose to a 17-month high in August, exceeding $100 billion for the first time since March 2025. Imports of goods and services were worth $105.6 billion more than exports, according to data from the Census Bureau and Bureau of Economic Analysis.
author: The Hill

title: Archdiocese of St. Louis sues ICE officials over blocked religious services
content: The Archdiocese of St. Louis has filed a lawsuit against Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officials, alleging that a jail visitation policy obstructs religious services. The legal action contends that the policy prevents Catholic detainees from practicing essential aspects of their faith.
summary: The lawsuit argues that the jail's visitation policy prevents Catholic detainees from practicing important parts of their faith.
author: The Hill

title: Planned Parenthood Votes adds $1M to ads targeting Maine, Michigan Senate races
content: Planned Parenthood Votes, a super PAC affiliated with Planned Parenthood, is investing an additional $1 million in ad buys to support Democratic Senate candidates in Maine and Michigan. The funds will be used for digital ad campaigns targeting incumbent Sen. Susan Collins (R-Maine) and former Rep. Mike Rogers (R-Mich.).
summary: Planned Parenthood Votes is investing an additional $1 million in digital ad campaigns to boost Democratic Senate candidates in Maine and Michigan. The funds will target Senator Susan Collins of Maine and former Representative Mike Rogers of Michigan.
author: The Hill

title: Plague in Russia sparks concern, COVID-19 pandemic memories: 5 things to know
content: The death of a Russian laboratory technician researching the plague has raised concerns both domestically and internationally, with observers drawing parallels to conditions that some theorized preceded the COVID-19 pandemic. Reports surfaced last week indicating that a worker at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East died shortly after being hospitalized.
summary: The death of Russian lab technician researching the plague has set off alarms abroad and at home as observers note resemblances to the conditions that some theorized preceded the COVID-19 pandemic. Reports emerged last week that a laboratory worker at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East had died shortly after being hospitalized.  The news…
author: The Hill

title: Green member behind Zionism motion named as 'close friend' of jailed al-Qaeda supporter in court
content:
Lubna Speitan, a Green Party member who introduced a motion on Zionism, has been identified in court as a "close friend" of Minh Quang Pham. Pham is currently serving a 40-year prison sentence following a Heathrow bomb plot investigation.

Speitan has offered to testify on Pham’s behalf during the legal proceedings.
summary: Lubna Speitan offered to testify on behalf of Minh Quang Pham, who was jailed for 40 years after a Heathrow bomb plot investigation.
author: BBC Politics

title: Hunter Valley group wins landmark high court climate change case over Mount Pleasant coalmine
content:
A Hunter Valley community group has secured a victory in Australia’s first High Court case to address climate change, a ruling advocates describe as a binding national precedent for fossil fuel projects in New South Wales. The nation’s highest court upheld a unanimous decision from the NSW Court of Appeal, which had previously overturned the proposed expansion of MACH Energy’s Mount Pleasant coalmine in Muswellbrook.

The community group stated that the ruling demonstrates that society "cannot continue to dig up coal … and pretend the consequences have nothing to do with us." This landmark judgment effectively blocks the mine expansion, marking a significant legal development regarding the intersection of climate change and industrial development in the region.
summary: A Hunter Valley community group won Australia's first high court case to consider climate change, with the ruling setting a binding national precedent for fossil fuel projects in New South Wales. The nation's highest court upheld a unanimous ruling by the NSW court of appeal that overturned MACH Energy's proposed expansion of its Mount Pleasant coalmine in Muswellbrook.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Study: about one‑third of lupus patients use supplement‑med combos that may interact
content:
A recent study published online on September 22 in Arthritis Care & Research found that nearly one in three patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) are taking a supplement‑medication combination that could potentially interact.

The research highlights the prevalence of such combinations among people with SLE, underscoring the importance of monitoring for possible drug‑supplement interactions.
summary: Nearly one in three patients with systemic lupus erythematosus are taking a supplement‑medication combination with potential for an interaction. The result was reported in a study published online Sept. 22 in Arthritis Care & Research.
author: Medical Xpress

title: UK study links pregnancy complications to higher cardiac and renal risk
content: A U.K. study published in the open-access journal BMJ Medicine indicates that women experiencing complications during their latest or previous pregnancies face an elevated risk of developing cardiometabolic-renal conditions in the years following delivery. The research highlights a link between these pregnancy-related health issues and subsequent cardiac and renal health problems.
summary: A UK study published in BMJ Medicine suggests women with pregnancy complications face elevated risks of cardiometabolic-renal conditions. This increased risk applies to complications in either the latest or a previous pregnancy.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Frozen yoghurt chains return to UK with £12 tubs
content: Frozen yoghurt, a popular trend during the 2000s and 2010s, has experienced a resurgence with multiple chains opening across the wider UK. The return of the treat has sparked questions about its sustainability, particularly given that a single tub now costs £12.
summary: Frozen yoghurt has made a comeback with multiple chains opening across the wider UK. The article questions whether the trend will last given the price of £12 per tub.
author: BBC Business

title: INRAE study finds sorghum may boost European yields under climate change
content:
Research conducted by INRAE and AgroParisTech indicates that global warming could positively impact sorghum yields in Europe. The study identifies sorghum as a viable alternative to maize for livestock feed, noting that the crop requires less water and can tolerate higher temperatures.

The researchers utilized simulations based on past climate data and future climate scenarios to explore new strategies for European agriculture. Their findings were published in the journal Earth's Future.
summary: Research by INRAE and AgroParisTech indicates that global warming could positively impact sorghum yields in Europe. The crop is a promising alternative to maize for livestock feed because it requires less water and tolerates higher temperatures.
author: Phys.org

title: 10,000 mapped reactions reveal steps in CO₂-to-fuel conversion
content: Scientists are increasingly exploring carbon dioxide (CO₂) hydrogenation, a process where CO₂ reacts with hydrogen over a catalyst to produce useful chemicals and fuels such as methanol. This conversion involves thousands of tiny chemical steps occurring on the catalyst surface.
summary: Scientists are exploring CO₂ hydrogenation to convert carbon dioxide into useful chemicals and fuels like methanol. The process involves thousands of small chemical steps occurring on the catalyst surface.
author: Phys.org

title: Linguists find Madonna's voice defies age-related expectations
content: Linguists have observed that Madonna’s voice defies typical age-related expectations for women. Generally, as women progress through menopause, their voices tend to become deeper due to physiological changes such as swelling of the vocal folds and a loss of elasticity in surrounding muscles, which results in a lower pitch. These age-related shifts can also impact the pronunciation of specific vowels.
summary: As women go through menopause, their voices tend to become deeper. This is partly because the vocal folds may swell and the surrounding muscles lose elasticity, resulting in a lower pitch.
author: Phys.org

title: Study maps European coastal regions at greatest risk from light pollution
content: Scientists have released a novel assessment identifying the coastal regions of Europe that face the highest risk from harmful light pollution. This study represents the first of its kind to evaluate the specific vulnerabilities of European waters to this environmental issue.
summary: Scientists have produced a first-of-its-kind assessment identifying which coastal regions of Europe are at greatest risk from harmful light pollution. The study highlights specific areas within European waters that face the highest levels of this environmental threat.
author: Phys.org

title: Computer scientist tracks satellites with automated observatory built from off-the-shelf technology
content:
Allen Schnibben, a computer scientist at Sandia National Laboratories, has maintained an interest in space since childhood, beginning with elementary school books and progressing to night sky observations with a telescope in middle school. He now applies this long-standing passion to his professional work by collecting data on satellites at Sandia’s SOHBRIT facility.

The SOHBRIT facility is a 12-foot-wide (3.7-meter-wide) observatory constructed from off-the-shelf technology. This automated setup allows Schnibben to track satellites as part of his duties at the national laboratory.
summary: Allen Schnibben's interest in space started when he was a child. "I picked up some books about the solar system when I was in elementary school.
author: Phys.org

title: OpenAI Shares AI Progress in Mathematics via GitHub Repository
content:
OpenAI has released a new GitHub repository to share its progress in mathematics. The repository is hosted at https://github.com/openai/math and contains a collection of preprints that can be viewed at https://github.com/openai/math/tree/main/preprints.

The announcement was posted on Hacker News, where it earned 314 points and generated 282 comments. The repository and its preprints are publicly available at the links provided.
summary: OpenAI has shared its AI progress in mathematics on GitHub at https://github.com/openai/math. The repository includes a preprints folder at https://github.com/openai/math/tree/main/preprints.
author: Hacker News

title: UniEvo-VL introduces self-distillation training for multimodal model improvement
content:
A new research paper titled “UniEvo‑VL: Self‑Distillation Training for Multimodal Model Self‑Improvement” has been posted on arXiv (identifier 2609.38721). The work proposes a self‑distillation approach aimed at enhancing multimodal models.

The paper’s listing was shared on Hacker News, where the submission received eight points and generated no comments. No additional details about the study’s methodology, results, or authors are provided in the source.
summary: The paper titled UniEvo-VL proposes a self-distillation training approach for multimodal model self-improvement. It is posted on arXiv and received eight points with no comments on Hacker News.
author: Hacker News

title: OpenAI Preprint Claims Integer Multiplication Below n log n
content:
A new preprint titled "Integer multiplication below n log n" has been published on the OpenAI Math GitHub repository, dated September 23, 2026. The document is currently available for public review at the specified URL.

The article has garnered 32 points on the Hacker News platform, where it is being discussed in a thread containing 18 comments.
summary: An OpenAI preprint titled "Integer multiplication below n log n" was released on September 23, 2026. The article has received 32 points and 18 comments on Hacker News.
author: Hacker News

title: Best Anti-Prime Day Deals for Amazon Haters: WIRED-Approved Savings
content:
A new roundup of deals targets shoppers who prefer to avoid Amazon. The article, titled “The Best Anti–Prime Day Deals for Amazon Haters,” highlights a selection of offers that do not involve Amazon.

According to the source, the roundup features a range of deals on items that have been approved by WIRED. The focus is on providing savings while steering clear of Amazon’s platform.
summary: The roundup presents deals that allow readers to save money without supporting Amazon. It includes WIRED-approved favorites.
author: Wired

title: Best Prime Day Digital Wall Calendar Deals: Skylight, Everblog, Apolosign
content:
Prime Day 2026 is spotlighting digital wall calendar deals from Skylight, Everblog, and Apolosign.  

These calendars can organize multiple family calendars, meal plans, chores, and to‑do lists, and they can also double as a digital photo frame.  

The products are on sale during the Prime Day event.
summary: Digital wall calendars can organize multiple family calendars, meal plans, chores, and to-do lists, and even double as a digital photo frame. They are on sale.
author: Wired

title: Apple and LG Partner on New Smart Home Devices Including Lock, Doorbell, Thermostat
content:
Apple and LG are partnering to launch a new line of smart‑home devices, beginning with a lock, doorbell, and thermostat. Bloomberg reports that the products will carry LG branding while integrating with Apple’s rumored smart‑home hub, which is slated to debut at an event on October 13.

The lineup will include a video doorbell, thermostat, indoor camera, deadbolt lock, outdoor security camera, and a floodlight camera. Several of the devices are expected to support the Thread and Matter protocols as part of a formal reboot of Apple’s HomeKit platform.

The partnership was disclosed by Bloomberg, with the full story available on The Verge.
summary: Apple is teaming with LG to produce a new lineup of smart home devices, such as a video doorbell, thermostat, indoor camera, deadbolt lock, outdoor security camera, and floodlight camera, which will carry LG branding and integrate with Apple's upcoming smart home hub expected to launch during an event on October 13. The devices will support Thread and Matter protocols amid a formal reboot of Apple's HomeKit platform.
author: The Verge

title: Xbox Secures Exclusive Streaming Rights for GTA 6
content:
Microsoft’s Xbox division has secured exclusive streaming rights for Grand Theft Auto VI, according to a statement from Xbox CEO Asha Sharma to employees during an all‑hands meeting. Sharma said Microsoft is preparing a move around the game that “no other platform holder is doing.”

Sources familiar with the plans confirm that the deal will allow only Xbox Cloud Gaming to stream GTA VI at launch, though the duration of the agreement has not been disclosed. Rockstar Games has not announced a PC version of the title, so the exclusive streaming arrangement positions Xbox to promote its cloud‑gaming service to players.
