The researchers note that when every participant in a meeting echoes the same opinion, organizations risk overlooking warning signs and missing new ideas. By fostering a sense of security, groups can encourage richer dissent that improves the quality of collective judgments.
summary: A research team from KAIST says that when members feel securely accepted in a group, they can express dissenting opinions in greater detail and more persuasively. summary: A federal judge ruled that a sheriff’s deputy violated a woman’s Fourth Amendment rights by using Flock to search her license plate without a warrant. The judge called Flock “indiscriminate mass surveillance.”
author: TechCrunch

title: OpenAI safety leader David Robinson quits, says company culture is broken
content:
David Robinson, a safety leader at OpenAI, resigned from the company, citing a broken culture. In an essay titled “I quit OpenAI because its culture is broken,” he explained his decision and warned that AI firms were not “being nearly careful enough” about developing the technology.

Robinson had led the writing of safety reports that accompanied the ChatGPT developer’s product releases. His resignation joins other insiders who are urging the industry to take more care over rapidly developing technology.
summary: David Robinson, who led the writing of safety reports for ChatGPT product releases, resigned from OpenAI. In his resignation essay, he warned that OpenAI’s culture is broken and that AI firms are not being nearly careful enough about developing the technology.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Azerbaijan, Turkey, Uzbekistan hold “Power of Unity 2026” drill in Karabakh
content:
Thousands of military personnel from Azerbaijan, Turkey and Uzbekistan gathered for the first time in the “Power of Unity, 2026” exercise. The joint drill took place in the Hojavend district of Azerbaijan’s Karabakh region.  

Other nations participated as observers, including Iran. The exercise marked a significant collaboration among the three countries’ armed forces.
summary: Thousands of military personnel from Azerbaijan, Turkey and Uzbekistan joined forces in the “Power of Unity, 2026” exercise. Observers from other nations, including Iran, were present in the Hojavend district of Azerbaijan’s Karabakh region.

title: Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro finish campaigns in Sao Paulo ahead of Brazil election
content: Brazil’s President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and his main challenger Flavio Bolsonaro concluded their campaigns on Saturday in the powerhouse state of São Paulo, where a fifth of the nation’s vote is based. Both leaders sought to rally supporters and persuade undecided voters on the eve of Sunday’s nail‑biter election.
summary: Brazil's President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and his main challenger Flavio Bolsonaro wrapped up their campaigns on Saturday in Sao Paulo. They sought to rally supporters and convince the undecided on the eve of Sunday's nail‑biter election in a state that provides a fifth of the nation's vote.

title: Latvia exit polls show PM Andris Kulbergs' pro‑Ukraine party leads, coalition partners lag
content:
Latvia’s parliamentary election results were projected by exit polls to favor Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs’ pro‑Ukraine and pro‑Europe party, which was seen winning on Saturday by an unexpectedly wide margin.  

The polls indicated that Kulbergs’ coalition partners performed poorly, suggesting that the centrist prime minister would need to form a new ruling coalition to govern.
summary: Exit polls showed that Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs' pro‑Ukraine and pro‑Europe party is projected to win the parliamentary election on Saturday by an unexpectedly wide margin. Projected results for the other coalition parties indicate the centrist prime minister will have to form a new ruling coalition.
author: France 24

title: UAE says Flydubai co-pilot attempted terrorist attack after stabbing fellow pilot
content:
Flydubai says a co‑pilot attempted a “terrorist attack” after stabbing his fellow pilot on an Israel‑bound flight, according to UAE officials.  

The incident involved the crew member stabbing the other pilot during the flight, prompting an investigation by the airline and authorities.  

The man, identified as a native of Oman, was reportedly barred from flying in Oman over security concerns.
summary: The co-pilot stabbed his fellow pilot on an Israel-bound Flydubai flight. He was reportedly barred from flying in his native Oman over security concerns.
author: DW World

title: Outgoing OpenAI safety engineer says AI giants not being nearly careful enough
content:
AI safety concerns were voiced by an outgoing OpenAI safety engineer who warned that “AI giants are not being nearly careful enough.” The engineer, a former OpenAI employee, said the industry should be regulated with safeguards comparable to those governing nuclear power and aviation.

The remarks came days after President Donald Trump signed a voluntary pact with artificial‑intelligence companies. The former OpenAI worker’s comments underscore a call for stricter safety measures despite the recent agreement.
summary: An outgoing OpenAI safety engineer warned that AI giants are not being nearly careful enough. He said the industry needs safeguards comparable to those for nuclear power or aviation, days after President Donald Trump signed a voluntary pact with artificial intelligence giants.
author: DW World

title: Al Jazeera interviews Palestinian boy from viral West Bank photograph
content:
Al Jazeera has spoken with a Palestinian schoolboy who appeared in a photograph that went viral online. The image shows the boy hiding from Israeli forces while walking home from class in the occupied West Bank.

The widely shared picture captured the child’s attempt to evade the soldiers, highlighting the everyday pressures faced by students in the territory. Al Jazeera’s interview provides the boy’s perspective on the incident captured in the viral photo.
summary: Al Jazeera speaks with the Palestinian schoolboy shown in a viral photograph. The photo captured him hiding from Israeli forces while walking home from class in the occupied West Bank.

content:
A youth‑led movement is demanding the resignation of India’s chief election commissioner, prompting discussion about the role of the CJP in the country’s political landscape.  

The activists’ call reflects concerns that the chief election commissioner’s actions may be influencing political processes.  

The demand underscores growing scrutiny of election administration in India.

title: Bulgaria brings Czar Samuel’s remains home after 1,000 years
content:
Remains of Bulgaria’s Czar Samuel have been returned to the country after roughly a thousand years.  

The emperor is regarded as a symbol of Bulgarian national identity, and his repatriation has stoked tensions with Greece.  

The transfer highlights the enduring significance of the ruler in Bulgaria’s historical narrative.
summary: The remains of Bulgaria’s Czar Samuel have been returned to Bulgaria after about 1,000 years. The repatriation, viewed as a symbol of Bulgarian national identity, has heightened tensions with Greece.

title: Funeral prayers for Palestinian mother and daughter held at Gaza's Saint Porphyrius
content:
Funeral prayers were held at Gaza City’s Saint Porphyrius Greek Orthodox Church for a Palestinian mother and her daughter who were killed in a Gaza strike.  

The service took place at the historic Saint Porphyrius church, where mourners gathered to honor the two victims.
summary: Funeral prayers were held at Gaza City's Saint Porphyrius Greek Orthodox Church. The service was for a Palestinian mother and daughter who were killed in a Gaza strike.

title: Trump urges Republicans to pass bill making daylight saving time permanent
content:
President Donald Trump is intensifying pressure on Republican lawmakers to end the United States’ practice of switching clocks twice a year.  

In a recent outreach, the president published a lawmaker’s cell‑phone number while urging the passage of a bill that would make daylight‑saving time permanent.  

The effort is aimed at securing Republican support for ending the biannual clock change.
summary: The US president published a lawmaker’s cell phone number as he called for the passage of a bill making DST permanent. He is ramping up pressure on US Republicans to end US clock switching.

title: Bruno Fernandes says he spoke to Ronaldo and denies squad rift
content: Bruno Fernandes said he has spoken to Cristiano Ronaldo and praised the forward after a walk‑out incident involving the Portugal squad. The midfielder denied reports of a rift within the national team, emphasizing that relations remain intact. Fernandes’ comments came as the team addressed speculation about internal discord. No further details were provided.
summary: Bruno Fernandes says he has spoken to Cristiano Ronaldo. He denies a rift within Portugal’s squad.

title: England rout Croatia U14, Kane and Bellingham score
content:
England dominated a Nations League match against Croatia’s under‑14 side at Stadion HNK Rijeka, securing a decisive victory that cemented second place in their group and strengthened their chances of reaching next year’s quarter‑finals. The 6,200 Croatian fans were invited free of charge, creating a lively atmosphere for the young visitors.

Harry Kane delivered a standout performance, scoring his 88th and 89th international goals to mark his 124th cap. Jude Bellingham also shone, providing three assists and scoring once himself. Their combined efforts were praised by manager Thomas Tuchel, who highlighted the match as England’s most complete display since the 4‑2 win over Croatia at the World Cup.
summary: England defeated the Croatian under‑14 side, securing second place in their Nations League group and improving their chances of reaching next year’s quarter‑finals. Harry Kane scored his 88th and 89th international goals on his 124th cap while Jude Bellingham provided three assists and a goal, a performance praised by manager Thomas Tuchel.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Wakefield Trinity defeat Warrington Wolves 23-10 in Super League Grand Final
content:
Wakefield Trinity defeated Warrington Wolves 23‑10 in the Super League Grand Final held at Old Trafford, with the match kicking off at 6 pm BST.

In the fourth minute, a strong carry by Scott pushed Wakefield close to the Warrington 20‑metre line, but a mix‑up late in the set produced an offside from a poor kick. Williams then cleared the Warrington lines from the resulting penalty. The next attack from Wakefield saw Walmsley claim a towering kick near the Trinity line, but after landing the ball was turned over. Mail Lee was also mentioned in the commentary.

The match concluded with Wakefield Trinity securing a 23‑10 victory over Warrington Wolves.
summary: Wakefield Trinity beat Warrington Wolves 23-10 in the Super League Grand Final at Old Trafford. The match opened at 6pm BST with a strong carry by Scott for Wakefield, but a mix‑up and offside penalty gave Warrington a chance to counterattack.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Manchester United manager Eva Olid seeks city recommendations during international break
content:
Manchester United manager Eva Olid said she is “asking for recommendations” as she prepares to explore the city for the first time during the international break.  

Olid, who has recently taken charge of the club, plans to look around Manchester while the team is on break.
summary: Manchester United manager Eva Olid is asking for recommendations as she prepares to look around the city for the first time during the international break. She is seeking suggestions for places to visit.

title: Gloucester thrash Harlequins to top early Premiership standings
content:
Gloucester thrash a limp Harlequins at Kingsholm, propelling the club to the top of the early Premiership standings.

The match saw Gloucester dominate the game, with the Harlequins struggling to keep pace. Their defeat at Kingsholm moved Gloucester to the forefront of the league table.
summary: Gloucester defeated Harlequins at Kingsholm. The win moved Gloucester to the top of the early Premiership standings.

title: Pennsylvania Approaches 1,000 Measles Cases in 2026, Health Department Reports
content:
Pennsylvania is approaching 1,000 confirmed measles cases for 2026, the state health department reported on Friday. The Department of Health said 977 cases have been confirmed across 39 counties in the state.

The agency highlighted that 34 new Pennsylvania measles cases had been reported.
summary: Pennsylvania's Department of Health confirmed 977 measles cases across 39 counties in 2026. The department said the total had recently surpassed 900, bringing the state close to 1,000 cases.

title: Trump Shares Tom Cotton’s Cell Phone Number Over Daylight Saving Act Stall
content:
President Trump posted Sen. Tom Cotton’s (R‑Ark.) cell phone number on Truth Social Saturday, lashing out at Senate Republicans for not advancing the Sunshine Protection Act, legislation that would make daylight saving time permanent.  

In his post, Trump called Cotton a “friend of mine” and accused him of holding up a “very important Bill.” The tweet was aimed at urging Republicans in the Senate to move the Sunshine Protection Act forward.
summary: President Trump posted Sen. Tom Cotton’s cell phone number on Truth Social Saturday. He criticized Cotton for holding up the Sunshine Protection Act, a bill that would make daylight saving time permanent.

title: Nepal's catastrophic flooding warns mountain towns worldwide
content:
Neap’s catastrophic flooding is a red alert for the world’s mountain towns

The title highlights the severe flooding in Nepal, underscoring a broader warning for mountain communities worldwide. According to the source, towers of ice and snow weakened by a quickly heating planet will, one way or another, wreak havoc down‑mountain in vulnerable landscapes.

The content points to the vulnerability of downstream areas as ice and snow masses lose stability in a warming climate. This instability poses a direct threat to the safety and infrastructure of mountain towns that rely on the natural barrier these ice towers provide.

The weakening of ice and snow towers due to a quickly heating planet could cause havoc down‑mountain in vulnerable landscapes.
summary: Nepal is experiencing catastrophic flooding. The flooding is described as a red alert for the world’s mountain towns as warming ice and snow threaten vulnerable down‑mountain landscapes.
author: The Hill

title: Ted Cruz Criticizes Tucker Carlson Over World War II Comments
content:
Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) criticized conservative commentator Tucker Carlson over remarks made during a recent podcast appearance. The former Fox News host questioned whether the United Kingdom “benefited” from its involvement in World War II, a statement that prompted a sharp rebuttal from the Texas senator.

In a post published on Friday night, Cruz directly addressed the clip, stating, “Yes, Tucker, the UK is better off for winning WWII.”
summary: Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) criticized former Fox News host Tucker Carlson for questioning if the United Kingdom benefited from its involvement in World War II. Cruz responded to a clip of the podcast appearance by stating that the UK is better off for winning the war.

title: Florida dengue outbreak reaches 252 cases, largest in US in decades
content: A dengue fever outbreak in Florida has grown to the largest in the continental United States in decades, with 252 reported cases recorded this year according to an update released this week. The disease is transmitted through infected mosquito bites and is rarely fatal, with most infected individuals experiencing mild symptoms.
summary: Florida has reported 252 dengue fever cases this year, marking the largest outbreak in the continental United States in decades. The disease is transmitted through infected mosquito bites and is rarely fatal.
author: The Hill

title: Human tau seeds trigger disease-specific shapes in mouse brains
content:
A new study reveals that human tau seeds induce disease-specific shapes within mouse brains. Tau is a protein naturally present in the brain, where it plays an essential role in proper neuron development and facilitates communication between neurons.

When this protein becomes misshapen or misfolded, it can drive the progression of neurodegenerative diseases. The abnormal buildup of tau is a hallmark of Alzheimer's disease, and scientists have also linked misfolded tau to more than 20 other neurodegenerative conditions.
summary: A new study found that human tau seeds trigger disease-specific shapes in mouse brains. Misfolded tau, a protein essential for neuron development, is associated with Alzheimer's and more than 20 other neurodegenerative diseases.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Mapping parasite mitochondria uncovers ancient pathways and new drug targets
content: A four-year research initiative focused on mapping the complete protein profile of mitochondria in parasites responsible for sleeping sickness, giardiasis, leishmaniasis, and babesiosis has identified ancient pathways and dozens of potential new drug targets. The study was driven by the critical role mitochondria play as the "powerhouse of the cell," with researchers noting that disrupting this energy production halts the parasite's function. These four diseases collectively impact nearly one billion people annually.
summary: A four‑year study mapped every protein in the mitochondria of parasites that cause sleeping sickness, giardiasis, leishmaniasis, and babesiosis. The analysis uncovered ancient metabolic pathways and identified dozens of potential new drug targets.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Atmospheric momentum exchange alters Earth rotation under global warming
content:
Atmospheric circulation influences weather and climate while also carrying angular momentum. When wind patterns shift or mass redistributes, the atmosphere exchanges momentum with the solid Earth, resulting in slight alterations to the planet's rotation rate.

While the mechanism of this momentum exchange is not a new concept, researchers are investigating the specific effects that occur under conditions of long-term global warming.
summary: Atmospheric circulation carries angular momentum and can exchange it with the solid Earth to slightly alter the planet's rotation rate. The article investigates how this process occurs under long-term global warming.
author: Phys.org

title: Visible light does not speed up water evaporation, rigorous experiments suggest
content: Recent experiments involving hydrogels and water droplets have led researchers to propose that exposure to visible light can accelerate water evaporation without causing heating. Despite these proposals, direct evidence confirming that light acts directly on the water itself has remained difficult to obtain.
summary: Researchers conducted experiments with hydrogels and water droplets to test whether visible light could accelerate water evaporation without heating. The experiments found no direct evidence that light acts on water itself.
author: Phys.org

title: New Study Finds Two-Sun Star System Could Host Earth-Sized Planet with Liquid Water
content: A new paper examining the dynamics of a nearby star system suggests that it could potentially support an Earth-sized planet in a region where liquid water could exist. The system features two suns, creating conditions that researchers are analyzing for habitability.
summary: A nearby star system with two suns could potentially support an Earth-sized planet in a region where liquid water could exist. This possibility was identified in a new paper examining the dynamics of the system.
author: Phys.org

title: Physicists Find Topological Wave Knots in Materials That Resist Imperfections
content: Physicists have identified topological properties in certain materials and devices, characterized by wave behaviors that resemble knots in a rope. These properties are defined by whole numbers that remain unchanged despite small imperfections, much like a knot persists through stretching or twisting until the rope is cut. This robustness against defects and noise has established topology as a central concept in modern physics, offering potential for the development of resilient electronics, photonics, and quantum devices.
summary: Physicists have found that some materials and devices carry topological properties in how waves move through them. These properties, labeled by whole numbers that do not change under small imperfections, promise electronics, photonics, and quantum devices that tolerate defects and noise.
author: Phys.org

title: New study finds effective recovery methods for intimate partner violence victims
content:
Recovery after intimate partner violence: New study reveals what works

Violence in the home can range from intimidation to physical abuse. When it occurs there, we refer to it as domestic violence.  

Every year, more than 1 million people in the Netherlands age 16 and older experience domestic violence. This type of violence is often perpetrated by a current or former partner, in which case it is referred to as intimate partner violence.
summary: A new study identifies effective approaches for recovery after intimate partner violence. More than 1 million people aged 16 and older in the Netherlands experience domestic violence each year, often by a current or former partner.
author: Phys.org

content:

content:

Ishida said the solution is “successfully
summary: Satoshi Ishida presented at Capcom Open Conference RE: 2026, outlining challenges of scaling Resident Evil development and proposing AI integration into workflows. Capcom's Pragmata studio is not opposed to AI, despite earlier concerns.

content:

title: Lula and Bolsonaro Hold Final Rally in São Paulo Ahead of Tight Election
content:
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro are wrapping up their campaigns on Saturday, holding final rallies in the crucial state of São Paulo to try to sway voters before the election.

The upcoming vote is described as tight and is being conducted amid scandals and personal attacks.

title: Tennessee prison chief resigns after Christa Pike execution failure
content:
The head of Tennessee’s prison system has resigned, marking the first major personnel change since the state’s botched execution of Christa Pike.  

Pike survived two lethal injections and remains in critical condition. The resignation follows the failed execution, which prompted a statewide review.  

Governor Bill Lee, who had previously denied Pike clemency, has halted all executions for the remainder of the year while the review proceeds.
summary: The head of Tennessee's prison system resigned following the failed execution of Christa Pike, who remains in critical condition after surviving two lethal injections. Governor Bill Lee has halted all remaining executions for the rest of the year and is conducting a review.
author: France 24

title: Former Ukrainian FM Dmytro Kuleba says Putin seeks legacy in Ukraine war on France 24
content:
Former Ukrainian Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba told France 24 that “Putin only cares about what will be written about him in history books.” He linked the Russian leader’s ambitions to the iconic Bronze Horseman, the equestrian statue on Senate Square in St Petersburg that was commissioned by Catherine the Great in honor of the city’s founder, Peter the Great. The pedestal bears the dedication “To Peter the First, Catherine the Second, 1782.”  

Kuleba asked whether Putin wants to become a third great ruler—“Vladimir the Great”—and suggested that a drive for expansion “at any cost” may be the real reason behind the war in Ukraine.
summary: Former Ukrainian Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba told France 24 that Putin “only cares about what will be written about him in history books.” He suggested that Putin’s ambition for a lasting legacy may be driving the war in Ukraine.
author: France 24

title: Bosnia and Herzegovina's politics still defined by post-war system, ethnic divisions and EU push
content:
Bosnia and Herzegovina remains governed by a political system created after the Bosnian war, which ended more than 30 years ago.  

The country’s political reality is shaped by persistent ethnic divisions and a complex administrative framework established in the post‑war settlement.  

European integration ambitions also influence the nation’s governance, alongside the legacy of separatist tendencies.
summary: Bosnia and Herzegovina is governed by a system created after the Bosnian war more than 30 years ago. Ethnic divisions, a complex administration and European integration all influence the country's political reality.
author: DW World

title: US Coast Guard searches for missing Gulfstream G-100 air ambulance off Massachusetts
content:
The U.S. Coast Guard is conducting a search for an air‑ambulance jet that went missing off the coast of Massachusetts on Saturday morning.

The aircraft, a Gulfstream G‑100, was on a medical evacuation flight from Bermuda to Boston with six people aboard when it lost contact with the Federal Aviation Administration. An FAA spokesperson said the agency issued a search‑and‑rescue alert for the plane at about 1:20 a.m. local time on Saturday.

The Coast Guard’s search operation continues as authorities work to locate the missing aircraft.
summary: The US Coast Guard is searching for a Gulfstream G-100 air ambulance that lost contact with the FAA while flying from Bermuda to Boston early Saturday. The flight had six people aboard and the FAA issued a search-and-rescue alert at about 1.20 am local time.
author: Guardian World

title: England beat Croatia 7-0 in Nations League as Kane scores sixth straight away goal
content:
England defeated Croatia 7-0 in a Nations League match, extending Harry Kane’s scoring streak.  

Kane found the net, marking his sixth consecutive away game in which he has scored for England, while Bukayo Saka contributed two goals.  

The victory was recorded as a 7-0 win in the Nations League competition.
summary: Harry Kane scored, marking his sixth successive away game for England. Bukayo Saka also scored twice as England thumped Croatia 7-0 in the Nations League.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Bruno Fernandes praises Ronaldo and urges Portugal unity before Norway match
content:
Bruno Fernandes praised Cristiano Ronaldo and urged national unity as Portugal prepares for its upcoming match against Norway. The midfielder said the forward remains the team's “greatest symbol” despite recent developments.

Ronaldo withdrew from the Portugal squad, but Fernandes emphasized that his influence endures and called for the squad to stay united ahead of the Norway game.
summary: Cristiano Ronaldo withdrew from the Portugal squad. Bruno Fernandes said the forward remains the team's greatest symbol and called for Portugal unity ahead of the Norway game.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Tennessee prison chief to resign after Christa Pike survives botched execution
content:
The Tennessee prison chief announced plans to resign following the botched execution of inmate Christa Pike.  

Pike’s attorneys said the failure “goes far beyond any one person,” highlighting broader concerns about the execution process.  

Pike remains in critical condition after surviving two lethal injections.
summary: The Tennessee prison chief will resign following the failed execution of Christa Pike. Pike is in critical condition after surviving two lethal injections, and her lawyers said the failure goes far beyond any one person.
author: BBC World

title: Zigiotti Olme's lob gives United 1‑0 win over Liverpool
content:
Manchester United secured a second Women’s Super League victory of the season with a 1-0 home win over Liverpool, powered by an early goal from Julia Zigiotti Olme. The forward capitalized on a mistake by Liverpool goalkeeper Khiara Keating to lob the ball into the net in the sixth minute.

Despite late pressure from Gareth Taylor’s side, United held on to keep their winning streak alive. The result marks back-to-back league wins for the team managed by Eva Olid.
summary: Julia Zigiotti Olme scored a sixth‑minute lob to give Manchester United coach Eva Olid a 1‑0 home win over Liverpool. The goal capitalised on a mistake by Liverpool goalkeeper Khiara Keating, and United held on for back‑to‑back league victories.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Ireland's press conference cut short before Nations League match with Israel
content:
The Republic of Ireland’s press conference on the eve of their second Nations League match against Israel in Serbia was cut short while head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson answered questions from Israeli journalists. The team is preparing for a fixture that follows their 3-0 victory over Israel in Hungary on Tuesday, a match that was preceded by a turbulent buildup where the Irish squad voted to proceed despite unease over the war in Gaza.

During the event, Hallgrimsson called for “cool heads” and dismissed accusations of racism as “completely untrue.”
summary: The Republic of Ireland’s press conference before their second Nations League match against Israel in Serbia was cut short as head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson fielded questions from Israeli journalists and dismissed accusations of racism as ‘completely untrue’, calling for ‘cool heads’. Ireland had beaten Israel 3‑0 in their first match in Hungary on Tuesday after the squad voted to fulfil the fixture despite unease over the war in Gaza.
author: Guardian Sport

title: F1 confirms Qatar and Abu Dhabi races will proceed despite Middle East conflict
content:
Formula One chief executive Stefano Domenicali confirmed on Saturday that the final races of the season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will proceed as scheduled despite the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. Speaking to French broadcaster Canal+ on the sidelines of the Bahrain Grand Prix, Domenicali stated, “Based on the information we have, everything is confirmed for [us to stay in] Qatar and Abu Dhabi.”

The announcement came after the Bahrain and Saudi Arabia races were scrapped. The Bahrain Grand Prix was relocated to the Sepang circuit in Malaysia, where Domenicali made the statement regarding the remaining calendar.
summary: Formula One chief Stefano Domenicali confirmed that the final races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will go ahead as planned. This decision follows the scrapping of the Bahrain and Saudi Arabia events due to the ongoing conflict in the region.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Croatia vs England Nations League match live with cap milestones
content:
Croatia and England face off in a Nations League match that kicked off at 5 pm BST (6 pm local). Live scores are being updated as the game progresses.

Head coach Thomas Tuchel said that the sunny Adriatic coast of Rijeka has helped his side unwind and recharge. He added that the atmosphere is different and that they want the match to be “really competitive.” Tuchel noted that Alex Scott performed well on his debut and that there is a lot to defend on Jarell Quansah’s side with Ivan Perišić. He also mentioned Trent Alexander‑Arnold as an option from the bench, hoping the team can gain an edge in physicality.

The match sees several players reach milestone caps. Harry Kane earns his 124th England appearance, one shy of Peter Shilton’s record of 125. Jordan Pickford takes his 92nd cap, and Bukayo Saka reaches 58. For Croatia, Luka Modrić earns his 203rd cap, Ivan Perišić his 159th, Mateo Kovačić his 118th, and Andrej Kramarić would reach 120 if he takes the field.
summary: The Nations League match between Croatia and England is live, with England's Harry Kane set to earn his 124th cap and Jordan Pickford his 92nd. Croatia's Luka Modrić will reach his 203rd cap, while Ivan Perišić and Mateo Kovačić will earn caps 159 and 118 respectively.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Ireland secure 43-19 win over Japan at Virgin Media Park
content:
Ireland secured a comprehensive 43‑19 victory over Japan in an international Test match held at Virgin Media Park in Cork.  

The win marked a second straight triumph for Ireland against Japan, with the Irish side scoring seven tries in the match.  

The result extended Ireland’s winning streak over the Japanese team.
summary: Ireland secured a comprehensive 43-19 win over Japan in an international Test at Virgin Media Park in Cork. The match featured a seven-try performance by Ireland, sealing consecutive victories over Japan.
author: BBC Sport

title: Kartal Reaches China Open Last-32, Zverev Sets Up Djokovic Quarter-Final
content:
Great Britain's Sonay Kartal has advanced to the last‑32 of the China Open, securing another victory in the tournament.  

In a separate match, Alexander Zverev has progressed to a quarter‑final clash against Novak Djokovic in Beijing.  

The upcoming quarter‑final will feature Zverev versus Djokovic.
summary: Great Britain's Sonay Kartal reached the last-32 of the China Open. Alexander Zverev will face Novak Djokovic in the quarter-finals in Beijing.
author: BBC Sport

title: Red Bull upgrade energizes F1 at Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia
content:
Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

The recent Red Bull upgrade has enlivened the Malaysian Grand Prix, according to the headline.  

Even Lewis Hamilton fears Max Verstappen will be tough to beat in Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.  

The upgrade has brought new excitement to the event.
summary: Lewis Hamilton fears Max Verstappen will be tough to beat at Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The Bahrain Grand Prix will take place on Sunday in Malaysia.
author: BBC Sport

title: Education Department Extends Student Loan Interest Rate Reduction Deadline
content:
The U.S. Department of Education has extended the deadline for student loan borrowers to obtain a small reduction on their interest rates. The change allows eligible borrowers an additional period to apply for the rate cut.

The extension was announced a day before the original deadline was set to expire, giving borrowers more time to take advantage of the reduced interest rate option.
summary: The Education Department extended the window for student loan borrowers to obtain a small reduction on their interest rates. The extension was announced a day before the original deadline was set to end.
author: The Hill

title: Trump thanks Israeli plumber Yaniv Hayoun for averting Flydubai crash
content:
President Trump thanked Israeli plumber Yaniv Hayoun for intervening after a pilot stabbed his co‑pilot and attempted to crash a Flydubai flight this week.  

In a video message shared on Truth Social, the former president praised Hayoun, saying he “did an amazing job” and adding, “He’s my kind of guy.” The message cut off with an incomplete statement, “He can….”
summary: President Trump thanked Israeli plumber Yaniv Hayoun on Friday morning for intervening after a pilot stabbed his co-pilot and attempted to crash a Flydubai flight. In a video message on Truth Social, Trump praised Hayoun, saying he did an amazing job and that he is his kind of guy.
author: The Hill

title: U.K.-Iranian dual national arrested over RAF Fairford threat released on bail
content:
A 25‑year‑old U.K.–Iranian dual national was released on bail after being arrested earlier this week on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts against RAF Fairford, a U.S.‑operated military base in England.  

British authorities confirmed the release on Saturday. The man was taken into custody in the City of Westminster, London, on “suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts” targeting the airbase.  

No further details were provided by the authorities.
summary: A 25-year-old U.K.-Iranian dual national was arrested in Westminster on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts against the U.S.-operated RAF Fairford base. British authorities said he was released on bail on Saturday.
author: The Hill

title: Democrats Edge Out or Neck-and-Neck with Republicans in Five Key Senate Races, Polls Show
content:
Senate Democratic candidates are currently edging out or polling neck and neck with their Republican counterparts in five competitive Senate races, according to new surveys. These results serve as the latest indicator that Republicans are facing a challenging midterm environment in areas that are traditionally more politically conservative.

The findings are based on polling released by The New York Times, which highlights the tight margins in these key contests. The data suggests that the race for Senate control remains closely contested, with Democrats holding a slight advantage or matching their GOP opponents in these specific districts.
summary: Senate Democratic candidates are edging out or polling neck and neck with their GOP counterparts in five competitive Senate races this cycle. The new surveys suggest Republicans face a tough midterm environment in traditionally redder areas.
author: The Hill

title: Amazon sends email notices for $309M returns class action settlement
content: A new class action settlement regarding Amazon returns has been finalized, potentially offering payments to individuals who returned items purchased through the platform over a several-year period. Notices regarding the $309 million settlement have been sent via email to those who may qualify.
summary: Amazon has sent email notices to customers who returned items over a several-year period. These individuals may qualify for payment in a new class action settlement.
author: The Hill

title: Tennessee's botched execution of Christa Pike renews death penalty scrutiny
content: Tennessee’s botched execution of Christa Pike has renewed scrutiny over state death penalty protocols and raised questions regarding the legal recourse available when these procedures fail. The incident mirrors recent execution failures in other states, where inmates and their legal representatives have argued in court that such errors constitute cruel and unusual punishment.
summary: Tennessee's botched execution of Christa Pike is renewing scrutiny over how states carry out the death penalty. The attempt mirrors recent failures in other states where inmates and lawyers argue such errors amount to cruel punishment.
author: The Hill

title: Greens to Offer Two-Year Jobs to Unemployed Under-24s
content: Mothin Ali, the co-deputy leader of the Greens, announced at the party’s conference that the party intends to offer two-year jobs to unemployed individuals under the age of 24. Ali stated that many young people are currently "bored, desperate and lost."
summary: The Greens plan to offer two-year jobs to unemployed people under 24. Co-deputy leader Mothin Ali told the party's conference that many young people are "bored, desperate and lost".
author: BBC Politics

title: New Study Finds Unknown Brain Circuit Linked to OCD
content:
Treatment for obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), a mental health condition defined by distressing, uncontrollable thoughts and repetitive behaviors, has traditionally relied on psychotherapy and medication to manage symptoms. New research has identified a previously unknown brain circuit involved in the condition.

This discovery could serve as a key step toward developing treatments that target specific brain regions, potentially allowing for better control of OCD.
summary: A study has identified a previously unknown brain circuit involved in obsessive‑compulsive disorder. This discovery could lead to treatments that target specific brain regions to better control the condition.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Menopause is a major health milestone, yet health records barely track it—new research
content:
A recent study has highlighted that menopause, a major health milestone for anyone with ovaries who lives long enough, is rarely documented in medical records.  

The research notes that menopause is a natural transition in midlife that can strongly affect a person's quality of life and increase their current and future risk of heart disease, osteoporosis, and other health issues.  

Given these significant health implications, it is notable that whether someone is experiencing or has gone through menopause is seldom recorded in their medical records.
summary: Anyone with ovaries who lives long enough will experience menopause. Medical records do not consistently reflect whether a person is experiencing or has gone through menopause, despite its impact on quality of life and risk of heart disease, osteoporosis, and other issues.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Injectable Foam Prototype Could Seal Deep Wounds and Prevent Amputations
content:
Injectable foam prototype could seal deep wounds and help prevent amputations

A new prototype uses a caulking gun filled with silicone compound to allow doctors and nurses to seal deep wounds caused by blast injuries. The device is intended for future use in clinical settings.

By sealing such wounds, the technology aims to prevent amputations and reduce mortality among patients with severe injuries.
summary: A caulking gun filled with silicone compound will allow doctors and nurses to seal deep blast‑injury wounds. This could prevent amputations and reduce mortality for patients with severe wounds.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Brain scans show shared changes during depression treatment and distinct antidepressant effects
content:
Brain scans have revealed that while depression treatment triggers common changes in the brain, some patients experience distinct antidepressant effects, according to new research. The study highlights how neuroimaging can capture both shared and individualized responses to therapy.

Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a widespread mental health condition primarily marked by persistent low mood or loss of interest in daily activities. It remains a significant challenge for patients and clinicians alike.

Although several medications are available to treat depression, identifying the right one for each individual can take time, underscoring the need for personalized approaches to treatment.
summary: Brain scans reveal shared neural changes during depression treatment and distinct effects of antidepressants in some patients. Major depressive disorder is a common mental health condition characterized by persistent low mood or loss of interest, and finding an effective medication can take time.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Climate change harms Indigenous children's health worldwide, study of 53 reports
content:
A review of 53 studies has found that climate change is affecting the health of Indigenous children worldwide. The research indicates that these children are experiencing significant climate‑related health impacts.  

The study reports a range of effects, including malnutrition, infectious diseases, impacts on mental health and cultural well‑being, and problems before birth.
summary: Indigenous children across the globe are experiencing significant climate-related health impacts. These impacts include malnutrition, infectious diseases, mental health and cultural well-being effects, and problems before birth, according to a new study.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Salinas, Steinbeck's hometown, ranks as US's least affordable city for middle class
content:
A recent Brookings Institution analysis found that John Steinbeck’s hometown of Salinas is the least affordable city in the United States for the middle class.

Nestled between two mountain ranges at the crook of central California’s coastline, the Salinas Valley is known as the “salad bowl of the world.” Farm workers stoop over neatly lined rows of crops off Highway 101 to harvest more than half of the nation’s supply of lettuce and nearly a third of its strawberries.

The valley’s rich soil inspired Steinbeck to portray it as a promised land in his literary depictions of people chasing the American dream—immigrants, farm workers, and westward‑moving hopefuls hungering for a better life.
summary: A Brookings Institution analysis found that Salinas, John Steinbeck’s hometown, is the least affordable city in the US for the middle class. The valley, known as the “salad bowl of the world,” produces more than half of the nation’s lettuce and nearly a third of its strawberries, and Steinbeck used it as the promised land in his depictions of people chasing the American dream.
author: Guardian Business

title: French court study shows national courts key to deportation decisions
content:
French court rulings on deportation illustrate how judges balance conflicting rules on forced removal. A new study, published in the International Journal of Migration and Border Studies, examines the complex legal framework that governs European deportation practices.

The paper notes that European, national, and human‑rights law all intersect in deportation cases. The author argues that this web of regulations shapes how decisions are made in France.

Based on analysis of 100,000 French court cases, the study finds that national courts play a central role in deciding whether individuals can be removed.
summary: A study published in the International Journal of Migration and Border Studies analyzes 100,000 French court cases. It shows that judges navigate conflicting European, national and human rights rules, with national courts playing a central role in removal decisions.
author: Phys.org

title: Energy production, virus defenses and toxin loading identified as bacterial vulnerabilities
content:
Antimicrobial resistance is recognized as one of the world’s leading public‑health threats. The condition, often described as a silent pandemic, has already caused millions of deaths each year.  

According to estimates from the World Health Organization, if antimicrobial‑resistant bacteria are not contained, the number of deaths could rise to 10 million annually by 2050.  

These projections underscore the urgent need for continued surveillance and new strategies to combat resistant bacterial infections.
summary: Energy production, virus defenses and toxin loading have been identified as vulnerabilities in antimicrobial‑resistant bacteria. Antimicrobial resistance is a top global public‑health threat that currently causes millions of deaths annually and could reach 10 million deaths per year by 2050, according to WHO estimates.
author: Phys.org

title: Interactive Tool Reveals State-by-State Private Equity Health Care Investments
content:
New interactive tool tracks private equity investments in health care across U.S.

A new interactive tool was launched on Tuesday, Sept. 8, giving policymakers, researchers, journalists and the public a state‑by‑state view of private equity investments in U.S. health care.

The tool allows users to examine how private equity is shaping the health care sector across individual states.
summary: A new interactive tool was launched on Tuesday, Sept. 8. It provides a state-by-state view of private equity investments in U.S. health care for policymakers, researchers, journalists, and the public.
author: Phys.org

title: Milky Way may have begun as thousands of galaxies, new simulations suggest
content:
Milky Way may have begun as thousands of galaxies, new simulations suggest

In the early days of the universe, our home looked very different from how it does today. Back then, the region in our universe that would eventually become our Milky Way neighborhood was a collection of thousands of smaller galaxies—some pumping out tons of new stars, others filled only with gas or littered with dead stars and black holes.
summary: New simulations indicate that the region that would become the Milky Way was once a collection of thousands of smaller galaxies. These galaxies varied, with some forming many new stars, while others contained only gas or were filled with dead stars and black holes.
author: Phys.org

title: Short Breath Extends Mating Calls of Male Tokay Geckos
content:
A short breath extends the mating calls of male tokay geckos

Tokay geckos (Gekko gecko) are large, mostly nocturnal reptiles native to parts of Asia. They are among the few non‑bird reptiles that produce sounds to attract potential mates, defend their territory and signal distress.

Male tokay geckos’ calls typically begin with quieter rattles, followed by louder two‑part sounds that can sound like “ge‑ko” or “to‑kay.” These vocalizations help the males attract mates, defend territory, and signal distress.
summary: Male tokay geckos (Gekko gecko) use mating calls that start with quieter rattles and finish with louder two‑part sounds. A short breath extends these calls, aiding in mate attraction, territorial defense, and distress signaling.
author: Phys.org

title: Scientists find hundreds of hair cells covering squid bodies, aiding hearing loss research
content:
Scientists have found that squid possess a far greater number of sensory cells than previously known. The animals have cells with bundles of tiny, hairlike protrusions—hair cells—on their heads and arms, similar to those that allow humans to hear.

Researchers at Case Western Reserve University discovered that hundreds more of these hair cells line the entire surface of the squid’s body. This new finding expands the known distribution of hair cells in the species.

The discovery may provide researchers with an unprecedented window into how humans use—and lose—their hearing.
summary: Researchers at Case Western Reserve University discovered that squid have hundreds of hair cells lining the entire surface of their bodies. The finding could provide an unprecedented window into how humans use and lose hearing.
author: Phys.org

title: New imaging technologies offer a clearer view of coral reef change
content:
University of Miami researchers are utilizing new imaging technologies to transform the observation of coral reefs, enabling the measurement of changes that were previously difficult, costly, or time-consuming to document.

The approach involves a range of tools, from drones flying above the waves to cameras positioned just inches from the seafloor. These methods provide a clearer view of reef conditions for scientific analysis.
summary: From a drone flying above the waves to a camera just inches from the seafloor, University of Miami researchers are transforming how scientists observe coral reefs and measure changes that were once difficult, costly or…
author: Phys.org

title: Leucine boosts cellular energy by protecting mitochondrial proteins
content:
Leucine, an essential amino acid, has been shown to enhance cellular energy production by safeguarding key proteins on mitochondria from degradation.  

This discovery uncovers a link between nutrition and metabolism, suggesting that leucine’s protective effect on mitochondrial proteins could inform future strategies for treating metabolic disorders and cancer.
summary: The essential amino acid leucine enhances cellular energy production by preventing the destruction of key proteins on mitochondria. This discovery highlights a new link between nutrition and metabolism, potentially leading to new treatments for metabolic disorders and cancer.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists find an “earthquake gate” as California fault stress hits a 1,000-year high
content:
Scientists have identified a potential “earthquake gate” in Southern California. Researchers report that stress on the San Andreas and San Jacinto faults has risen to some of the highest levels observed in a 1,000‑year simulation.

Because both faults are highly stressed simultaneously, the Cajon Pass junction may be increasingly primed for a rupture that could cross both fault systems. The study does not predict when an earthquake might occur.
summary: Researchers say stress on Southern California’s San Andreas and San Jacinto faults has reached some of the highest levels seen in a 1,000-year simulation. Because both faults are highly stressed at the same time, the Cajon Pass junction may be increasingly primed for a rupture that could cross both systems, although the study does not predict when an earthquake will happen.
author: Science Daily

title: MEGATRON project links JWST galaxy observations to ancient star chemistry
content:
Ultra‑detailed simulations are showing how the first stars lit up the dark Universe and seeded space with elements such as carbon, oxygen, and iron. The new models trace the early stars’ influence on the surrounding medium, revealing the processes that produced the first heavy elements.

The MEGATRON project could bridge observations from the James Webb Space Telescope of the earliest galaxies with the chemical clues preserved in ancient stars today, linking early star formation to the composition of the oldest stellar populations.
summary: Ultra-detailed simulations are showing how the first stars lit up the dark Universe and seeded space with elements such as carbon, oxygen, and iron. The MEGATRON project could bridge JWST observations of the earliest galaxies with chemical clues preserved in ancient stars today.
author: Science Daily

title: Chang’e-6 Lunar Soil Yields New Magnetic Mineral, γ-Fe
content:
Scientists studying Chang’e‑6 lunar soil have identified a previously unknown magnetic mineral in natural Moon samples. The mineral is a form of metallic iron called γ‑Fe.  

The γ‑Fe was found inside tiny impact‑glass particles. At the nanoscale, this iron can preserve a stable magnetic signal. Researchers suggest the mineral could act like a microscopic fossil of the Moon’s long‑lost magnetic field.
summary: Scientists studying Chang’e-6 lunar soil discovered a previously unknown magnetic mineral, a form of metallic iron called γ-Fe. The nanoscale iron, found inside tiny impact‑glass particles, can preserve a stable magnetic signal and may act as a microscopic fossil of the Moon’s long‑lost magnetic field.
author: Science Daily

title: NASA’s Roman Telescope Achieves Precise Pointing, Captures Large Magellanic Cloud Stars
content:
NASA’s Roman Space Telescope has opened its planet‑hunting eye, demonstrating remarkable pointing stability and its first look at the cosmos. The telescope can already stay locked on a target with precision comparable to aiming a laser at a dime from about 150 miles away.

Its coronagraph captured stars in the Large Magellanic Cloud, confirming that the instrument can produce focused images.
summary: NASA’s Roman Space Telescope demonstrated remarkable pointing stability, locking onto targets
author: Science Daily

title: ESA’s Juice uses Earth flyby to slingshot toward Jupiter
content:
ESA’s Juice spacecraft passed Earth on September 28, using the planet’s gravity to alter its trajectory en route to Jupiter. The flyby was executed without significant fuel consumption.

The maneuver changed Juice’s direction by 20 degrees and increased its speed by 3.5 km/s. It also provided scientists with a rare opportunity to test the spacecraft’s instruments on both Earth and the Moon.

The event marks a successful gravity‑assist maneuver for the mission.
summary: ESA’s Juice spacecraft passed Earth on September 28, using the planet’s gravity to alter its trajectory toward Jupiter. The flyby changed its direction by 20 degrees, increased its speed by 3.5 km/s, and allowed scientists to test its instruments on Earth and the Moon.
author: Science Daily

title: Enzyme UBE2N identified as potential defense against worsening fatty liver disease
content: Scientists have identified an enzyme that could serve as a natural defense against the worsening of fatty liver disease, which affects an estimated 100 million Americans. The enzyme, called UBE2N, helps liver cells clear away damaged mitochondria and break down fat. By performing these functions, UBE2N may prevent the inflammation, scarring, and cell damage that can lead to the more dangerous condition known as MASH.
summary: Scientists have identified the enzyme UBE2N, which may act as a natural defense against the worsening of fatty liver disease that affects an estimated 100 million Americans. UBE2N helps liver cells clear damaged mitochondria and break down fat, potentially preventing inflammation, scarring and cell damage associated with MASH.
author: Science Daily

title: UK Bacon Sales Shift to Nitrite‑Free Products Amid Health Concerns
content:
Nitrite‑free bacon sales boom in UK amid fears over curing chemicals

Shoppers are switching from traditional bacon despite little evidence that the alternative is safer.  

Bacon has long been a favourite of carnivores, but growing consumer concern about the health risks posed by nitrites—chemicals used to cure meats—has prompted a shift in buying habits.  

While many experts argue there is no evidence processed meat made without nitrites is safer, retailers have responded to consumer concerns by offering “nitrite‑free” products to meet demand.
summary: Shoppers in the UK are buying nitrite‑free bacon as concerns grow over the health risks of nitrites used in curing meats. Retailers are responding by offering nitrite‑free products, despite experts saying there is no evidence the alternative is safer.
author: Guardian Science

title: Aleph Alpha releases Kolibri, an open-weight LLM for German and English
content:
Kolibri, an open‑weight large language model developed by Aleph Alpha, is designed to operate in both German and English, according to the announcement.

The blog post announcing Kolibri was published at https://tej.As/blog/aleph-alpha-kolibri and generated notable discussion on Hacker News, receiving 262 points and 116 comments (https://news.Ycombinator.Com/item?Id=49943034).
summary: Kolibri is an open-weight large language model from Aleph Alpha that supports German and English. The blog post about Kolibri has received 262 points and 116 comments.
author: Hacker News

title: Great Question (YC W21) hiring product engineers for remote work in Canada
content: Great Question, a Y Combinator Winter 2021 company, announced that it is hiring product engineers based in Canada for remote positions. The job posting is listed on the company’s Y Combinator page. No additional details about the role, compensation, or application process were provided.
summary: Great Question, a Y Combinator Winter 2021 company, is hiring product engineers. The roles are remote and located in Canada.
author: Hacker News

title: FTL: New operating system for cloud environments
content:
A new operating system for cloud environments, titled “FTL: A new operating system for clouds,” has been posted online. The article is available at https://ftl‑os.org/.

The announcement was shared on Hacker News, where the discussion thread can be found at https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49944912. The post has received 13 points and has generated five comments.
summary: FTL is introduced as a new operating system for clouds. The article has received 13 points and 5 comments on Hacker News.
author: Hacker News

title: Meta's AI agent Muse builds detailed profiles of users' friends and family
content:
Meta’s AI agent Muse creates detailed profiles of users’ friends and family, and the tool has been downloaded by millions.  

According to the source, employing Muse to carry out user requests carries privacy costs. Privacy costs are a concern for users of Muse.
summary: Millions have downloaded Meta’s AI agent Muse. Getting it to do your bidding comes with privacy costs.
author: Wired

title: Xreal video glasses revive interest in 3D movies, author says
content:
A The Verge contributor reports that recent advances in video‑glass technology are finally delivering a satisfying 3D movie experience, prompting the writer to purchase 3D Blu‑ray titles in large numbers. The article notes that 3D had long been regarded as one of the biggest tech flops, with earlier theater viewing limited by polarized glasses that reduced resolution and brightness by roughly half.

The piece highlights a demonstration by colleague Cameron Faulkner, who modeled a pair of Xreal glasses, illustrating how modern video glasses overcome the shortcomings of older systems. The writer recalls James Cameron’s Avatar—released more than 15 years ago—as a landmark 3D film that became the highest‑grossing movie worldwide.
summary: The author says they are buying every 3D Blu‑ray they can find because new video glasses make 3D movies enjoyable. They note that earlier polarized theater glasses reduced resolution and brightness, and cite James Cameron’s Avatar as a past high‑grossing 3D film.
author: The Verge

title: OpenAI safety lead David Robinson resigns, warns of broken industry culture
content:
David Robinson, who authored the safety reports accompanying every major model release at OpenAI, resigned from his position this week. In an editorial published in The Atlantic, Robinson announced his departure and began publicly warning about risks associated with the technology he helped develop.

Robinson argues that the problems stem from a fundamentally broken culture within the AI industry, suggesting that merely adding new rules or regulations will not address the deeper issues. He emphasizes that the challenges go beyond surface‑level policy changes.

The full account of Robinson’s resignation and commentary appears in a story on The Verge.
summary: David Robinson, who wrote safety reports for every major OpenAI model release, resigned this week. He is now warning that industry culture is fundamentally broken in an editorial published in The Atlantic.
author: The Verge

title: Splice CEO Kakul Srivastava says AI emails are killing conversations
content:
Splice chief executive Kakul Srivastava says that the rise of AI‑generated emails is “killing conversations,” reflecting her concerns about how automated messaging is affecting communication.  

Srivastava leads Splice, a sample platform that producers use for one‑shot sounds and melodic loops, with tracks from the service appearing in hits such as Lisa’s “Money” and Sabrina Carpenter’s “Espresso.”  Prior to joining Splice, she held executive positions at Flickr, Yahoo, GitHub and Adobe, positioning her at the intersection of Silicon Valley and the creative community.  

Under her leadership, Splice has broadened its reach by acquiring Spitfire Audio and overseeing new initiatives for the company.
summary: Kakul Srivastava, CEO of the music sample platform Splice, believes AI-generated emails are harming conversations. She previously held executive roles at Flickr, Yahoo, GitHub and Adobe and expanded Splice by acquiring Spitfire Audio.
author: The Verge

title: Spotify billionaire’s Neko Health body‑scan startup expands to the United States
content:
Spotify billionaire’s body scan startup has come to America

Farooq Abbasi, an investor in Neko Health, spoke with Equity about the company’s future plans. Abbasi discussed the next steps for the hot health‑tech startup, outlining potential growth and strategic directions.
summary: Neko Health, a body‑scan startup associated with a Spotify billionaire, has entered the U.S. market. Investor Farooq Abbasi spoke to Equity about the company and its future plans.
author: TechCrunch

title: List of notable AI agents that can live in text messages
content:
A new compilation identifies the most notable AI agents that can operate within text messaging platforms.  

The list spans a variety of functions, including general‑purpose assistants as well as agents specifically designed for families, travel and work.  

The collection highlights the breadth of capabilities these text‑based AI agents can provide.

title: Vessev unveils electric hydrofoil ferry aiming to reshape boating
content:
Vessev built an electric ferry that almost flies

Vessev has developed an electric hydrofoil ferry that is designed to change how people and cities think about boats. The company hopes its innovative vessel will shift perceptions of maritime transport and inspire new approaches to urban water travel.
summary: Vessev built an electric ferry that almost flies. The company hopes it will change how people and cities think about boats.
author: TechCrunch

title: G7 agrees to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude amid Iran shipping restrictions
content:
The International Energy Agency said that 325 million barrels of emergency oil have been released, with an additional 75 million barrels slated for release.

G7 leaders agreed on Friday to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude after U.S. pressure on Europe, noting that supplies have been squeezed by Iran’s restrictions on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
summary: G7 leaders agreed on Friday to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude. The release was prompted by US pressure on Europe and Iran's restrictions on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
author: Euronews

title: Tens of thousands protest in Madrid after lawmakers reject tenant‑protection measures
content:
Tens of thousands of protesters marched in Madrid and other Spanish cities on Saturday, calling for affordable housing. The demonstrations were driven by anger over lawmakers’ narrow rejection of a set of measures put forward by Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez’s government.

The rejected proposals were intended to strengthen protection for tenants, prompting demonstrators to demand stronger housing relief.
summary: Tens of thousands of protesters marched in Madrid and other Spanish cities on Saturday demanding affordable housing. The demonstrations were sparked by lawmakers narrowly rejecting measures put forward by Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez’s government to strengthen protection for tenants.
author: France 24

title: Houthis say Saudi forces carried out 26 strikes on Sanaa amid loud blasts
content:
Loud blasts rocked Sanaa on Saturday, prompting Houthi rebels to accuse Saudi forces of launching 26 strikes on the Yemeni capital. The rebels said the explosions followed a series of attacks that they claim targeted the city, which is under the control of the Iran‑backed group.

In Saudi Arabia, observers reported flames and a large plume of smoke rising from an oil giant Aramco facility located south of the kingdom’s capital, Riyadh. The incident was noted as part of the broader conflict between the Saudi‑backed coalition and the Houthi movement.

The accusations and the reported Saudi facility fire were both reported on Saturday.
summary: Houthi rebels accused Saudi forces of launching 26 strikes on Sanaa on Saturday after loud explosions rocked the Yemeni capital, which they control. Flames and a large plume of smoke were seen rising from an Aramco facility south of Riyadh in Saudi Arabia.
author: France 24

title: France to share defence files with Italy in probe of 1980 Ustica jet crash
content:
France has agreed to share defence documents with the Italian judiciary, a move that has sparked hopes of a breakthrough in investigations into the 1980 crash of a passenger jet near the island of Ustica. The crash, which killed 81 people, has long been a subject of controversy, and a former Italian president has claimed that the aircraft was mistakenly shot down by a French fighter jet.

Despite the new access to French files, sceptics warn that the documents are unlikely to shed light on one of Italy’s most enduring mysteries or identify a culprit. The Italian authorities will now review the material, but no definitive outcome has been announced.
summary: France has decided to share defence documents with the Italian judiciary, sparking hopes of a breakthrough in the investigation of the 1980 passenger jet crash near the island of Ustica. Sceptics note that the files may not illuminate the long‑standing mystery or identify a responsible party, despite a former Italian president’s claim that a French fighter jet mistakenly shot down the aircraft.
author: France 24

title: Eritrea Cuts Ties with Ethiopia, Heightening War Fear in Horn of Africa
content:
The Tigray conflict has expanded beyond a domestic dispute, raising concerns across the Horn of Africa. After Eritrea severed diplomatic ties with Ethiopia, tensions have escalated as Ethiopia, Eritrea, and Egypt exchange accusations.

In response, the African Union has called for restraint amid the growing uncertainty. The situation prompts questions about whether the region is moving toward a broader crisis.
summary: The Tigray conflict has expanded beyond domestic borders as Ethiopia, Eritrea and Egypt trade accusations. The African Union (AU) urges restraint amid concerns the Horn of Africa may face a wider regional crisis.
author: DW World

title: Kenyan survivors challenge UK military over alleged decades of abuse and immunity
content: Kenyan survivors are challenging the United Kingdom’s military over decades of alleged abuses. The survivors contend that the UK forces have been protected by legal immunity that has shielded them from accountability. Their effort seeks to confront both the historic allegations and the legal safeguards that have prevented redress. The case underscores a broader dispute over responsibility and justice for the alleged misconduct.
summary: Kenyan survivors are challenging the UK military over alleged abuses that span decades. They argue that the military’s legal immunity has protected it from accountability.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israel election sees Arab leader forced to withdraw, far‑right candidates cleared
content:
In the latest Israeli election cycle, a Palestinian Israeli leader was compelled to withdraw his candidacy, while far‑right Israeli leaders were permitted to remain on the ballot.  

The contrasting treatment has been described as a double standard, with the forced exit of the Palestinian candidate standing in stark contrast to the clearance of right‑wing contenders.  

The episode has drawn attention to perceived disparities in how candidates are handled in the polls.
summary: A Palestinian Israeli leader was forced to withdraw his candidacy. Far‑right Israeli leaders were allowed to run in the polls.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Brazil 2026 presidential race tight between incumbent Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro
content:
Brazil’s 2026 presidential election is shaping up as a close contest, with polls indicating a tight race between incumbent Lula and right‑wing rival Flavio Bolsonaro.  

Voter concerns over crime and the economy are central to the campaign, underscoring the issues driving the competition between the two candidates.
summary: Polls show a tight race between incumbent Lula and right‑wing rival Flavio Bolsonaro. The contest is occurring amid concerns over crime and the economy.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Tens of thousands protest in Spain after parliament rejects two housing decrees
content:
Tens of thousands of people took to the streets in Spain after parliament struck down two affordable‑housing decrees, according to reports.  

The latest demonstrations have deepened a crisis that has persisted for several days, following the legislative rejection of the housing measures.
summary: Tens of thousands of people demonstrated in Spain. The demonstrations deepened a days‑long crisis after parliament struck down two affordable housing decrees.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Democrats upbeat in final US midterm month as Republicans spend to curb losses
content:
‘Bordering on angry’: The state of play as US midterms enter final month

As the United States midterm elections move into their final month, the political landscape is described as “bordering on angry.” The title underscores the heightened tension surrounding the closing weeks of the contests.

Democrats are entering the stretch with a surprisingly positive outlook, while Republican campaign funds are being deployed in an effort to stem damage to their party’s prospects.
summary: Democrats have entered the final stretch of the US midterms with a surprisingly positive outlook. Republican money is being deployed in an effort to stem damage.

title: Brazil accuses US of election interference amid Lula‑da‑Silva and Bolsonaro clash over sovereignty
content:
Brazil is preparing to vote for its next president, and the campaign has been marked by accusations that the United States is interfering in the election.  

The contest pits former president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva against former president Jair Bolsonaro, with both candidates sparring over issues of sovereignty, security and Brazil’s ties with Washington.  

The dispute over foreign influence has led Brazilian officials to publicly accuse the United States of meddling in the electoral process.
summary: Brazil has accused the United States of interfering in its upcoming presidential election. The accusation comes as Lula da Silva and Bolsonaro clash over sovereignty, security and ties with Washington.
author: BBC World

title: Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe 2026: Complete Horse‑by‑Horse Guide to Runners
content:
Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe 2026: horse‑by‑horse guide to all the runners

The 2026 edition of the Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe is shaping up to feature a rare repeat success, with Daryz well fancied to contend. In Paris, O’Brien Jr and Sr will go head‑to‑head, adding intrigue to the field.

Daryz is trained by Francis‑Henri Graffard and ridden by jockey Mickael Barzalona. The four‑year‑old draws 5 and carries a pedigree of Sea The Stars x Daryakana (by Selkirk). Market odds for the horse are 7‑4.
summary: Daryz is well fancied for a rare repeat success in the Prix de l’Arc de Tri
author: Guardian Sport

title: India defeat Pakistan by 19 runs to win Asian Games cricket gold in Japan
content:
India defeated arch‑rivals Pakistan by 19 runs to win the Asian Games men’s Twenty20 cricket gold medal in Nagoya, Japan. India posted 211 for 6 in 20 overs, while Pakistan finished on 192 for 6.

Key performances included Abhishek Sharma’s 61 and Tilak Varma’s unbeaten 51 for India, and Hasan Nawaz’s 96 for Pakistan. The match, played on a converted baseball field, drew a small but raucous crowd and was watched by millions of fans on television.

The captains of both sides declined the customary pre‑match handshakes, a gesture reflecting the political tensions between the two nations. After the victory, Indian players paraded their national flag around the ground.
summary: India posted 211‑6 and beat Pakistan, which scored 192‑6, by 19 runs in the Asian Games T20 final in Nagoya, Japan. The captains refused the traditional pre‑match handshakes and Indian players later paraded their national flag around the ground.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Verstappen grabs first pole of year at Bahrain GP in Malaysia as Russell risks points
content:
Max Verstappen secured his first pole position of the year at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, taking the top spot for Red Bull. Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton started second on the front row, Kimi Antonelli finished fourth, and George Russell was down in eighth.

The most consequential story for the Formula One World Championship is the widening gap between title leader Kimi Antonelli and his Mercedes teammate George Russell. Russell, who has been floundering in Sepang, now faces the risk of losing additional points that he cannot afford while chasing Antonelli.
summary: Max Verstappen secured his first pole position of the year for Red Bull at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. Mercedes drivers Kimi Antonelli qualified fourth and George Russell started eighth, leaving Russell at risk of losing further points in his chase of the Italian.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Croatia vs England set for mostly full Nations League match despite fan ban
content:
The upcoming Nations League match between Croatia and England is expected to be largely full despite a fan ban, according to the matchday preview for Saturday’s action.  

The same coverage also includes the latest updates on Manchester City.  

In a related feature, a quiz identified Oliver Irow – on loan at Plymouth – as the Spurs player with the most goals this season, tallying four goals in seven appearances, while Tottenham have scored two Premier League goals after five matches.
summary: Croatia and England are scheduled to play a Nations League match on Saturday with most seats expected to be filled despite a fan ban. A quiz note highlighted that Spurs loanee Oliver Irow, playing for Plymouth, has scored four goals in seven appearances this season.

title: Manchester City whistleblower Rui Pinto offers to aid UK case in exchange for protection
content:
Rui Pinto, the whistleblower whose leaks prompted the Premier League’s investigation into Manchester City’s financial affairs, is prepared to assist UK authorities with their legal case if he receives protection from threats, the Guardian reports.  

Pinto faces the possible loss of witness safeguarding in Portugal, and a crowdfunding campaign launched on Friday aims to fund a new life after he left the protection of the Portuguese police. He says his priority is to cooperate, provided adequate security arrangements are put in place.  

Additional documents concerning Manchester City’s affairs may also be made available to investigators.
summary: Rui Pinto, whose leaks prompted the Premier League’s investigation into Manchester City’s finances, says he will cooperate with UK authorities if he receives protection from threats. A crowdfunding campaign launched on Friday to fund a new life after leaving Portuguese police protection may accompany the release of additional City documents.
author: Guardian Sport

title: India defeats Pakistan to win Asian Games gold
content:
India defeated Pakistan to capture the gold medal at the Asian Games.  

Abhishek Sharma and Tilak Varma set India on its way to victory, contributing to the win over Pakistan.  

The triumph secured the gold medal for India in the competition.
summary: Abhishek Sharma and Tilak Varma helped India beat Pakistan. The win secured the gold medal for India at the Asian Games.

title: Wang Cong dismisses critics over UFC 332 flyweight title fight with Natalia Silva
content:
Wang Cong, who adopts a Joker‑inspired persona to unsettle rivals, dismissed criticism that she is unqualified to challenge for the flyweight world title.  

She said the remarks are unfounded as she prepares to face Natalia Silva at UFC 332 on Saturday.  

The bout will determine the flyweight champion at the event.
summary: Wang Cong dismissed critics who said she was not deserving of facing Natalia Silva for the flyweight world title. The bout is scheduled for UFC 332 on Saturday.
